surahs: Rubbing hands and feet with dust (Tayammum)
Virtues of Prayer at Masjid Makkah and Madinah
Pilgrims Prevented from Completing the Pilgrimage
Penalty of Hunting while on Pilgrimage
Virtues of the Night of Qadr
Retiring to a Mosque for Remembrance of Allah (I'tikaf)
Sales in which a Price is paid for Goods to be Delivered Later (As-Salam)
Transferance of a Debt from One Person to Another (Al-Hawaala)
Loans, Payment of Loans, Freezing of Property, Bankruptcy
Lost Things Picked up by Someone (Luqatah)
Fighting for the Cause of Allah (Jihaad)
One-fifth of Booty to the Cause of Allah (Khumus)
Virtues and Merits of the Prophet (pbuh) and his Companions
Merits of the Helpers in Madinah (Ansaar)
Military Expeditions led by the Prophet (pbuh) (Al-Maghaazi)
Prophetic Commentary on the Qur'an (Tafseer of the Prophet (pbuh))
Limits and Punishments set by Allah (Hudood)
Afflictions and the End of the World
Accepting Information Given by a Truthful Person
Holding Fast to the Qur'an and Sunnah
flows: Deeds are rewarded according to intention, so one who emigrates for worldly gain or to marry a woman gets only what he emigrated for.
Revelation came like a ringing bell or through an angel, began in Hira's cave with 'Read', resumed after a pause, and Allah undertook to fix it in the Prophet's memory.
The Prophet was the most generous of people, and most of all in Ramadan when Gabriel met him every night to teach him the Quran.
Heraclius questioned Abu Sufyan about the Prophet, read his letter inviting him to Islam, and urged the Byzantines to pledge allegiance to him, then drew back when they recoiled.
Islam is built on five: testifying that none is worshipped but Allah and Muhammad is His Messenger, prayer, zakat, Hajj and fasting in Ramadan.
Faith has over sixty branches and modesty is one; the true Muslim spares Muslims harm from his tongue and hand, and good Islam is feeding people and greeting everyone.
None truly believes until he wishes for his brother what he wants for himself and loves the Prophet most; loving for Allah's sake and loving the Ansar mark faith.

The Prophet took his companions' pledge not to associate partners with Allah, steal, commit illegal intercourse, kill their children, slander or disobey in good, worldly punishment expiating such a sin.
A time will come when a Muslim's best property will be sheep he takes to mountain tops and valleys, fleeing with his religion from afflictions.
The Prophet ordered people only deeds within their strength, and grew angry when they said they were unlike him, saying he feared and knew Allah best of all.
Whoever holds Allah and His Messenger dearest, loves others only for Allah's sake and hates returning to disbelief as he hates the fire tastes the sweetness of faith.
Allah will have those with a mustard seed's weight of faith taken out of Hell, charred, and they will revive in a river like seeds sprouting by a flood channel.
The Prophet dreamt of people in shirts of varying length, Umar's so long he dragged it, and interpreted the shirts as the religion.
The Prophet told an Ansari who was admonishing his brother about modesty to leave him, for modesty is part of faith.
The Prophet was ordered to fight people until they testify to Allah and His Messenger, pray and pay zakat; then their lives and property are safe, save by Islamic law.
Asked which deed is best, the Prophet named faith in Allah and His Messenger, then jihad in Allah's cause, then an accepted Hajj.
The Prophet told Sa'd a man passed over in a distribution might be only a Muslim, not a believer, and said good Islam is feeding people and greeting everyone.
The Prophet was shown the Fire, most of whose dwellers were women; asked whether they disbelieved in Allah, he said they were ungrateful to husbands and for kindness.
Rebuking Abu Dhar for insulting a man's mother, the Prophet said slaves are brothers, to be fed and clothed as oneself and helped with heavy tasks.
Abu Bakra turned back Al-Ahnaf, citing the Prophet: when two Muslims meet with swords, killer and killed both go to the Fire, for the killed also meant to kill.
When a verse spoke of believers who mix no wrong with their faith, the companions asked who had not done wrong, and Allah revealed that associating partners is great wrong.
The marks of a hypocrite are lying when he speaks, breaking promises, betraying trusts, being treacherous in covenants and abusive in quarrels; whoever has all four is a pure hypocrite.
Praying on the Night of Qadr and Ramadan nights and fasting Ramadan with faith and hope bring forgiveness of past sins, and fighting in Allah's cause earns reward or Paradise.
Religion is easy and whoever overburdens himself cannot keep it up, so avoid extremes, aim near perfection and draw strength from worship morning, afternoon and late night.
After sixteen or seventeen months praying toward Jerusalem in Medina, the Prophet turned to the Ka'bah, others turned mid-prayer, and Allah revealed that earlier prayers were not lost.
Whoever embraces Islam sincerely or follows it well has good deeds rewarded ten to seven hundred times, while an evil deed is recorded only as it is.
Told of a woman's excessive praying, the Prophet said to do deeds within one's capacity, for Allah does not tire, and the best deed is the one done regularly.
Whoever declared that none but Allah is worshipped, with good in his heart weighing even a barley grain, wheat grain or atom, will be taken out of Hell.
A Jew told Umar that had the verse perfecting the religion come to them they would celebrate its day; Umar said it came on a Friday at Arafat.
A man from Najd asked about Islam, was told five prayers, the Ramadan fast and zakat, with more only if he wished, and swore to do no more nor less.
Whoever follows a Muslim's funeral out of faith until the prayer and burial are done earns two qirats, each like Mount Uhud, and one qirat for the prayer alone.
Abusing a Muslim is evil-doing and killing him is disbelief.
The Prophet forgot the date of the Night of Qadr when two men quarrelled, and said to seek it on the seventh, ninth or fifth of Ramadan's last ten nights.
Gabriel came as a man and asked the Prophet about faith, Islam, excellence and the Hour, and the Prophet named its signs and said only Allah knows its time.
Heraclius told Abu Sufyan that the growth of the Prophet's followers and none leaving his religion are the way of true faith once its delight enters the heart.
The lawful and the unlawful are clear with doubtful things between; avoiding these protects religion and honour, Allah's forbidden things are His reserve, and the heart decides the body's soundness.
The Prophet told the Abdul Qais delegation that belief in Allah alone means the testimony, prayer, zakat, the Ramadan fast and a fifth of booty, and forbade four wine vessels.
Deeds are rewarded by intention, emigration counts for what it was meant for, and spending on one's family for Allah's sake, even a morsel for one's wife, is charity.
Jarir pledged allegiance to the Prophet to pray, pay zakat and be sincere to every Muslim, and on the day Al-Mughira died he told the people he kept that pledge.
Finishing his talk before answering a Bedouin, the Prophet said to await the Hour when honesty is lost, which happens when authority passes to unfit people.
Seeing companions only pass wet hands over their feet in ablution for an overdue prayer, the Prophet called out loudly to save their heels from the fire.
The Prophet asked his companions which tree, never shedding its leaves, is like a Muslim; Ibn Umar shyly kept silent, and the answer was the date palm.
Dimam bin Tha'laba adjured the Prophet by Allah to confirm his mission to all mankind, five prayers, the Ramadan fast and zakat, then declared his belief as his people's envoy.
The Prophet sent a letter that Chosroes tore up, and because rulers read only sealed letters he had a silver ring engraved 'Muhammad Allah's Messenger'.
Allah welcomed the man who joined the Prophet's circle, those present were told to inform the absent, and the Prophet preached at intervals and bade people make religion easy.
Allah grants understanding of the religion to whom He wishes good, the Prophet being only a distributor, and the Prophet asked which tree resembles a Muslim: the date palm.
One may wish to be like another only in two cases: one given wealth who spends it rightly, and one given wisdom who acts on it and teaches it.
Moses, saying he knew no one more learned than himself, was told of Allah's slave Khadir and found him by following the sign of a lost fish.
The Prophet embraced Ibn Abbas and prayed that Allah grant him knowledge of the Book.
Just past puberty, Ibn Abbas passed before a praying row at Mina and none objected, and Mahmud recalled the Prophet throwing water from his mouth onto his face at five.
Moses, saying he knew no one more learned than himself, was told of Allah's slave Khadir and went back along his path to find him where the fish was lost.
The guidance and knowledge sent with the Prophet is like rain on land: fertile soil is one who learns and teaches, barren ground one who ignores it.
Among the signs of the Hour: religious knowledge decreases, ignorance, drinking and open illegal sexual intercourse spread, and women so outnumber men that fifty depend on one man.
The Prophet dreamt he drank milk until its wetness came out of his nails and gave the rest to Umar, interpreting it as knowledge.
At Mina during his last Hajj, asked about rites done out of order, such as shaving before slaughtering, the Prophet said to do it now, for there is no harm.
Knowledge will be taken away, ignorance and afflictions will appear and harj, which the Prophet showed by gesture to mean killing, will increase.
After an eclipse prayer the Prophet said he had seen Paradise and Hell, and that in the grave people will be asked about him: believers answer, hypocrites cannot.
The Prophet taught the Abdul Qais delegation the testimony, prayer, zakat, the Ramadan fast and a fifth of booty, forbade four wine vessels, and told them to pass it on.
Uqba bin Al-Harith divorced his wife after a woman said she had nursed them both, the Prophet asking how he could keep her once that had been said.
Umar and an Ansari neighbour took turns attending the Prophet to share news of revelation; once alarming news sent Umar to the Prophet, who had not divorced his wives.
Told that an imam's long prayers kept a man away, the Prophet angrily said whoever leads people must shorten the prayer, for among them are the sick, weak and needy.
Found property is announced for a year, then used but returned if its owner comes; a stray camel is to be left alone, and a stray sheep may be taken.
Pressed with questions he disliked, the Prophet angrily invited any question and told men who their fathers were, until Umar knelt saying they accepted Allah, Islam and Muhammad and repented.
The Prophet repeated what he said three times so it would be understood, and asked permission to enter by knocking three times with a greeting.
Seeing companions only pass wet hands over their feet in ablution for an overdue Asr prayer, the Prophet called out loudly to save their heels from the fire.
Three earn double reward: a scripture follower who also believes in Muhammad, a slave true to Allah and master, and one who educates, frees and marries his slave woman.
Thinking the women had not heard his sermon, the Prophet went to them with Bilal and ordered them to give alms, and they gave earrings and rings into Bilal's garment.
Abu Huraira, eager for hadith, asked who will be luckiest with the Prophet's intercession on Resurrection Day: one who said sincerely from the heart that none but Allah is worshipped.
Allah takes away knowledge by the death of scholars, until people take ignorant leaders who give verdicts without knowledge, going astray and leading others astray.
On a day set aside to teach women, the Prophet said a woman whose three or even two young children die will be shielded by them from the Fire.
Aisha, who asked until she understood, queried the Prophet's saying that whoever is called to account is punished, and he explained the easy reckoning as mere presentation of deeds.
Abu Shuraih reminded Amr that after the conquest the Prophet said Allah made Mecca a sanctuary where no blood is shed nor trees cut, fighting allowed him only briefly.
The Prophet declared blood, property and honour mutually sacred like that day and month, told those present to inform the absent, and asked whether he had conveyed the message.
Whoever intentionally lies about the Prophet or ascribes to him what he did not say will take his seat in the Fire, which made some companions narrate little.
Ali kept a written sheet of rulings, the Prophet had the Mecca sermon written for a Yemeni, Abdullah bin Amr wrote hadith, and the ailing Prophet asked for paper.
Rising at night, the Prophet marvelled at the afflictions sent down and treasures opened, had his wives woken for prayer, and warned the well-dressed may be naked hereafter.
After an Isha prayer late in his life, the Prophet said no one then living on earth would remain alive a hundred years from that night.
Spending a night at Maimuna's house, Ibn Abbas saw the Prophet pray four rak'at after Isha, sleep, then rise to pray, moving Ibn Abbas from his left to his right.
Abu Huraira narrated much, citing verses against concealment and his constant company with the Prophet, never forgot after spreading his garment for him, and kept back one kind of knowledge.
During the Farewell Hajj the Prophet had the people silenced and told them not to revert to disbelief after him by striking one another's necks.
Admonished for calling himself most learned, Moses sought Khadir but could not stay patient as Khadir holed a boat, killed a boy and repaired a wall.
Asked whether fighting from anger or pride is in Allah's cause, the Prophet said only one who fights so that Allah's word is highest fights in Allah's cause.
Near the Jamra people asked about Hajj rites done out of order, and the Prophet told each to do it now, for there is no harm.
When some Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit, he fell silent as if inspired, then recited that its knowledge is with his Lord and people have little knowledge.
The Prophet told Aisha that, but for her people being newly out of ignorance, he would rebuild the Ka'bah with an entrance and an exit door, which Ibn Az-Zubair did.
The Prophet told Mu'adh that whoever sincerely testifies to Allah's oneness and his messengership is saved from Hell, but not to spread it lest people depend on it.
Um Sulaim asked whether a woman must bathe after a wet dream, and the Prophet said yes if she sees discharge, which explains why a child resembles its mother.
Ibn Umar was too shy to name the date palm when the Prophet asked which tree is like a Muslim, and his father wished he had answered.
Too shy to ask himself, Ali had Al-Miqdad ask about frequent urethral discharge, and the Prophet said it requires ablution.
The Prophet named where the people of Medina, Syria, Najd and perhaps Yemen assume ihram, and said a muhrim avoids shirts, turbans, trousers, hooded cloaks and scented garments.
Prayer after hadath needs ablution, whose traces will make the Prophet's followers shine on Resurrection Day, and one who doubts in prayer leaves only on hearing or smelling something.
The Prophet prayed after sleeping without new ablution, made a light ablution after Arafat and a full one at Muzdalifa, and Ibn Abbas demonstrated his ablution handful by handful.
A man who asks Allah's protection from Satan, in Allah's name, before intercourse with his wife will have any child destined from it safe from Satan's harm.
The Prophet sought refuge on entering the toilet, prayed for Ibn Abbas for bringing water, and forbade facing the Qibla in the open, though Ibn Umar saw him face Jerusalem.
The Prophet's wives went out at night to relieve themselves; Umar, wanting them veiled, called out to Sauda, Allah revealed the veil verses, and the Prophet let them go out.
Ibn Umar saw the Prophet relieving himself facing Syria with his back to the Qibla, and Anas and another boy followed him carrying water for cleaning and a short spear.
One should not touch or clean the private parts with the right hand nor breathe into a drinking vessel, and the Prophet cleaned himself with stones, rejecting bone and dung.
The Prophet washed the limbs once or twice, and Uthman, washing thrice, reported that such an ablution followed by an attentive prayer brings forgiveness of sins.
Ablution includes rinsing the nose and, after sleep, washing the hands before dipping them; stones are used in odd numbers, and unwashed heels are threatened with the Fire.
Ibn Umar explained four habits others noticed, touching only the Yemeni corners, wearing tanned shoes, dyeing with henna and delaying ihram, as following what he saw the Prophet do.
When his daughter died the Prophet told those washing her to begin on the right with the parts washed in ablution.
The Prophet liked to begin with the right side in putting on shoes, combing his hair, washing himself and everything else.
When no water could be found for the Asr ablution, the Prophet put his hand in a pot and water sprang from between his fingers until all had made ablution.
Abida said one hair of the Prophet would be dearer to him than the world, and Abu Talha took the first of his hair when his head was shaved.
A vessel a dog drinks from is washed seven times, a man entered Paradise for watering a thirsty dog, and no water was sprinkled where dogs urinated in the mosques.
Game caught by one's trained dog sent with Allah's name may be eaten, unless the dog ate from it or another dog joined the hunt.
Waiting in the mosque counts as prayer until hadath, doubt requires a sound or smell, and urethral discharge and intercourse without emission were each said to need ablution.
Usama poured water for the Prophet's ablution after Arafat, and Al-Mughira on a journey, when he wiped over his head and khuffs.
Staying at Maimuna's, Ibn Abbas saw the Prophet wake at midnight, recite the last ten verses of Al-Imran, make ablution and pray two rak'at six times and a witr.
After a solar eclipse prayer the Prophet said he had seen Paradise and Hell, and that in the grave people will be asked about him: believers answer, hypocrites cannot.
Asked to show the Prophet's ablution, Abdullah bin Zaid rinsed mouth and nose and washed his face thrice, forearms twice, wiped his head back and forth, and washed his feet.
People wiped themselves with the Prophet's leftover ablution water, he had Abu Musa and Bilal drink and pour from his tumbler, and companions nearly fought over such water.
As-Sa'ib's aunt brought him ill to the Prophet, who prayed for him; he drank the leftover ablution water and saw the seal of prophethood between the Prophet's shoulders.
Abdullah bin Zaid again showed the Prophet's ablution from a pot, and Ibn Umar said men and women made ablution together in the Prophet's lifetime.
The Prophet visited the unconscious Jabir and sprinkled his ablution water on him; Jabir woke and asked who would inherit from him, and the verses on inheritance were revealed.
Water in a small painted pot brought to the Prophet sufficed for the ablution of eighty or more people.
The Prophet washed his hands and face in a tumbler and threw in a mouthful, and made ablution from a brass pot, washing his face thrice and forearms twice.
When his illness grew severe the Prophet was nursed in Aisha's house with his wives' consent and had seven skins of water poured over him before going to the people.
Asked by a man who used too much water, Abdullah bin Zaid showed the Prophet's ablution from an earthenware pot, rinsing mouth and nose thrice from one handful.
Water sprang from between the Prophet's fingers in a shallow tumbler, enough for seventy to eighty people to make ablution.
The Prophet used a sa' to five mudds of water for bathing and one mudd for ablution, and companions saw him wipe over his khuffs and once his turban.
The Prophet prayed without new ablution after eating cooked mutton, and after saweeq only rinsed his mouth, as he did after milk, saying it has fat.
One who grows drowsy while praying should sleep until he knows what he is saying, lest he pray against himself instead of asking forgiveness.
The Prophet made ablution for every prayer while companions kept one until hadath, and after eating saweeq he only rinsed his mouth before praying.
Hearing two people tortured in their graves, one for not guarding against urine and one for calumnies, the Prophet set half a palm leaf on each, hoping to ease it.
Anas brought water whenever the Prophet went to relieve himself, and he cleaned his private parts with it.
Passing two graves, the Prophet said one buried there was punished for not guarding against urine and one for calumnies, and fixed a palm leaf piece on each.
The Prophet had water poured on a Bedouin's urine in the mosque, telling people to make things easy, poured water over a baby's urine, and urinated standing at a dump.
Menstrual blood on clothes is rubbed and washed before praying in them, and bleeding from a vein is not menses, so a woman prays, leaving prayer only during real menses.
Aisha washed semen from the Prophet's clothes, and he went to prayer with the wet spots still visible.
People of Ukl or Uraina, healed by camels' milk and urine, killed the herdsman and drove off the camels; their hands and feet were cut, eyes branded, water withheld.
Before the mosque was built, the Prophet prayed in sheepfolds.
Asked about ghee into which a mouse had fallen, the Prophet said to remove the mouse and the ghee around it and use the rest.
A wound received in Allah's cause will appear on Resurrection Day bleeding but smelling of musk, and the Muslims, the last to come, will be foremost on that Day.
One should not urinate in still water and then bathe in it.
At the Ka'bah one of Abu Jahl's group put camel entrails on the prostrating Prophet until Fatima removed them; he invoked against Quraysh, naming men later seen dead at Badr.
The Prophet once spat into his clothes.
Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden.
Ali brought water in his shield and Fatima washed the blood from the Prophet's face, then the ash of a burnt straw mat filled his wound.
The Prophet used the siwak, with a retching sound, including on rising at night, and dreamt he was told to give it to the older of two men.
Before sleep one makes ablution, lies on the right side and supplicates, entrusting oneself to Allah and affirming His Book and Prophet; dying that night, one dies with faith.
In the bath after janaba the Prophet washed his hands, made ablution and poured water over himself; he shared one pot with a wife, and a sa' sufficed.
The Prophet poured water thrice on his head, rubbed scent into it, washed his private parts, cleaned his hand with earth, washed his feet last and declined a towel.
The Prophet and a wife bathed from one pot in turn; he washed his hands first, and Maimuna, who screened him, described each step and how he declined a towel.
Answering Ibn Umar's view, Aisha said she scented the Prophet, he went round his wives, and in the morning he assumed ihram with the scent's fragrance still on him.
Anas said the Prophet visited all his wives, eleven or by another report nine, in one round, day and night, and companions said he had the strength of thirty.
Ali had a man ask the Prophet about frequent urethral discharge, and was told to wash the organ and make ablution.
Aisha scented the Prophet, who went round his wives and was muhrim by morning, and she recalled the glint of scent in his hair parting while he was in ihram.
The Prophet's janaba bath began with ablution and ended with the feet; once he recalled janaba at the iqama and went to bathe, and women pour thrice on the head.
The Children of Israel bathed naked together and claimed Moses, who bathed alone, had a defect, until a stone ran off with his clothes and they saw him unblemished.
While Job bathed naked, golden locusts fell on him and he gathered them, telling his Lord he could never do without His blessings.
Fatima and Maimuna screened the Prophet while he bathed, and he told Um Sulaim a woman must bathe after a wet dream if she sees discharge.
Abu Huraira, junub, slipped away from the Prophet to bathe, and the Prophet told him a believer never becomes impure.
Anas said the Prophet visited all his wives in one night, when he had nine wives.
Junub, Abu Huraira slipped away from the Prophet's side to bathe and found him still sitting on return, and was told that a believer never becomes impure.
A junub person may sleep after washing his private parts and making ablution, as the Prophet did and told Umar.
Intercourse makes the bath compulsory; Uthman and others reported washing and ablution when there is no emission, but the bath is called safer and the final ruling.
Menses, ordained for Adam's daughters, bar only tawaf in Hajj, and while menstruating the Prophet's wives combed his hair, let him recite leaning on their lap, and shared his sheet.
The Prophet had a wife in her menses wear a waist-sheet before fondling her; Aisha shared his bath pot and washed his head during his I'tikaf while menstruating.
At Eid the Prophet told women to give alms, as he saw most of Hell's dwellers were women, and tied their deficiency in intelligence and religion to testimony and menses.
Aisha, weeping when her menses began on the way to Hajj, was told it is ordained for Adam's daughters and to do all the pilgrims do except Tawaf until clean.
Bleeding between periods is from a blood vessel and does not stop prayer or a wife's I'tikaf; menstrual blood is rubbed and washed off garments before praying in them.
Women were forbidden to mourn beyond three days, except four months and ten days for a husband without kohl, perfume or coloured clothes, save light perfume after menses.
After menses a woman cleans the blood's place with a musk-scented cloth; Aisha, menstruating at Hajj, undid and combed her hair, postponed her Umrah, then made it from Tan'im.
An angel at each womb names its stages, then asks whether the child is male or female, wretched or blessed, and its provision and age, all written in the womb.
Aisha, menstruating till Arafat, made her Umrah later from Tan'im; bleeding from a blood vessel does not stop prayer, and prayers missed in menses are not made up.
Umm Salama, getting her menses under the Prophet's woollen sheet, slipped away into her menstrual clothes, but he called her back under it; he kissed her while fasting.
Young, secluded and menstruating women were told to attend the Eid gatherings, one without a veil sharing her companion's, while the menstruating kept away from the prayer place.
Told that bleeding between periods comes from a blood vessel, Fatima bint Abi Hubaish and Umm Habiba bathed and prayed outside their menstrual days; yellowish discharge was not counted.
A woman whose menses begin after Tawaf al-Ifada may leave for home, as the Prophet allowed Safiya; Ibn Umar, who first said she should not, later agreed.
The Prophet told Aisha to give up prayer when her menses begin and, when they end, to wash the blood off and pray.
The Prophet led the funeral prayer for a woman who died in childbirth, standing by the middle of her body.
Maimuna, not praying during her menses, sat on a mat beside the Prophet's mosque while he prayed on his sheet, and his clothes touched her when he prostrated.
The verse of Tayammum came when Aisha's lost necklace held the people without water; the earth, the Prophet said, was made for his followers a place of prayer and Tayammum.
The Prophet did Tayammum on a wall to return a greeting, and taught Ammar, who had rolled in dust when Junub, that stroking earth and wiping face and hands suffices.
A Junub man without water was told Tayammum suffices, and a woman's water bags quenched all; Ibn Mas'ud refused it to the Junub, fearing its use when water was cold.
Gabriel opened and washed the Prophet's chest, took him up through the heavens where he met Adam, Idris, Moses, Jesus and Abraham, and fifty prayers were reduced to five.
Prayer was first enjoined as two rak'at at home and on journeys; the journey's prayer stayed so, while the resident's prayer was increased.
Menstruating and veiled women were brought out to the Eid gatherings, the menstruating keeping away from the prayer place, and one without a veil was to share her companion's.
The Prophet and Jabir prayed in one garment, ends crossed over the shoulders or tied as a waist-sheet if tight, the Prophet asking whether everyone had two garments.
Men prayed with waist-sheets tied at the neck, the Prophet was never again seen naked, Umar listed garment pairs, and two wrappings, certain Muhrim garments and naked Tawaf were forbidden.
As the Prophet rode into Khaybar his thigh was uncovered; after its conquest he took Safiya from Dihya, freed and married her, her freedom her mahr, with a wedding feast.
Women attended Fajr in sheets; the Prophet sent away a marked garment and pictured curtain distracting his prayer, cast off a silk gown and prayed in a red cloak.
The Prophet led prayer from the pulpit, stepping down to prostrate, and, injured by a fall from a horse, led it sitting, saying the imam is to be followed.
The Prophet prayed on mats, leading Anas, an orphan and an old woman on one, with Maimuna beside him in her menses and Aisha lying in front of him.
Worshippers prostrated on their clothes' ends in heat; the Prophet prayed in shoes and after wiping khuffs, held his arms out wide, and Hudhaifa rejected an imperfectly performed prayer.
Whoever says none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, prays like the Muslims, faces their Qibla and eats their slaughter is a Muslim, his blood and property protected.
When relieving oneself one should neither face nor turn one's back to the Qibla; Abu Ayyub turned away from Qibla-facing lavatories in Sham and asked forgiveness.
Asked whether an Umrah pilgrim may approach his wife before going between Safa and Marwa, Ibn Umar cited the Prophet's Tawaf, two rak'at and Sa'i, and Jabir said no.
The Prophet prayed two rak'at facing the Ka'bah, calling it the Qibla; after sixteen or seventeen months towards Jerusalem the Qibla was changed, and he faced it for compulsory prayers.
Told he had prayed more or less than usual, the Prophet made two prostrations of forgetfulness, saying he forgets like others, and the doubtful should follow what they think correct.
Umar said his Lord agreed with him in three things: taking Abraham's station as a place of prayer, veiling the Prophet's wives, and warning those wives they could be replaced.
While praying Fajr at Quba, people were told the Prophet had been ordered to face the Ka'bah, and turned from Sham towards it.
Having prayed five rak'at of Zuhr, the Prophet made two prostrations of forgetfulness when told of it.
The Prophet scraped spittle off the mosque's Qibla wall and told those praying to spit left, under the foot or into a garment, never in front or to the right.
The Prophet told his followers that their bowing and humility in prayer were not hidden from him, for he saw them from behind his back.
The Prophet held a horse race, trained horses running from Al-Hafya' to Thaniyat Al-Wada' and untrained ones from there to the mosque of Bani Zuraiq, with Ibn Umar taking part.
Goods from Bahrain were spread in the mosque; after prayer the Prophet gave them out to everyone until none remained, refusing to help Al-Abbas lift his overloaded garment.
Asked in the mosque whether Abu Talha had sent him to invite him to a meal, Anas said yes, and the Prophet told his companions to get up and go.
A man asked whether a husband who finds another man with his wife should kill him, and the couple were later seen doing Li'an in the mosque.
The Prophet prayed where Itban chose in his house, to be his prayer place, and said the Fire is forbidden to whoever sincerely says none is worshipped but Allah.
The Prophet liked to start everything from the right where possible, as in washing, combing and wearing shoes.
Told of a church in Ethiopia with pictures, the Prophet condemned building places of worship over graves; in Medina he built his mosque on land cleared of pagan graves.
Ibn Umar prayed with his camel in front of him as a sutra, saying he had seen the Prophet do the same.
During the eclipse prayer the Prophet was shown the Hellfire, and said he had never seen a more horrible sight.
The Prophet told people to offer some of their prayers at home and not to make their houses like graves.
The Prophet forbade entering the dwellings of people struck by Allah's punishment except weeping, lest what befell them befall the visitor.
The Prophet called those making pictured places of worship at graves the worst creatures, and in his last moments cursed Jews and Christians for building them at their prophets' graves.
The Prophet was given five things no earlier prophet had: victory by awe, the earth for prayer and Tayammum, lawful booty, a mission to all mankind, and intercession.
A freed slave woman, cleared when a kite dropped the scarf she was accused of stealing, lived in a tent in the mosque, where Ibn Umar and Ali also slept.
Abu Huraira saw seventy Suffa men without upper garments, in waist-sheets or sheets tied at the neck, which they held lest their private parts be exposed.
One entering a mosque should pray two rak'at before sitting, and the angels ask forgiveness for a worshipper as long as he stays at his prayer place without passing wind.
Built of adobe and palm, the Prophet's mosque was enlarged by Umar and rebuilt in stone by Uthman, who cited a place in Paradise for whoever builds a mosque.
Whoever passes through mosques or markets carrying arrows should hold them by their heads lest they injure a Muslim.
Abu Huraira confirmed hearing the Prophet tell Hassan bin Thabit to reply on his behalf, praying that Allah help him with the Holy Spirit.
The Prophet screened Aisha with his cloak at her door so she could watch Ethiopians displaying their skill with spears in the mosque.
Barirah's masters wanted her wala' if Aisha freed her; the Prophet told Aisha to buy and free her, and declared from the pulpit conditions not in Allah's Book invalid.
When Ka'b and Ibn Abi Hadrad raised their voices over a debt in the mosque, the Prophet had Ka'b remit half and told the debtor to pay the rest.
Learning that the black man or woman who swept the mosque had died, the Prophet asked why he was not told and offered the funeral prayer at the grave.
When the verses of Al-Baqara on usury were revealed, the Prophet recited them to the people in the mosque and then banned the trade in alcohol.
Abu Huraira mentioned the man or woman, most probably a woman, who used to clean the mosque, and narrated the Prophet's hadith about that person.
The Prophet overpowered a jinn demon that tried to interrupt his prayer, but did not tie it to a mosque pillar, remembering Solomon's prayer for a unique kingdom.
Horsemen sent to Najd brought Thumama bin Uthal, who was tied to a mosque pillar; released by the Prophet, he bathed and declared his Islam.
Wounded in the arm at the Trench, Sa'd bin Mu'adh was nursed in a tent the Prophet pitched in the mosque, until his wound bled profusely and he died there.
Being sick, Umm Salama was told to perform Tawaf riding behind the people, while the Prophet prayed beside the Ka'bah reciting Surat At-Tur.
Two companions leaving the Prophet on a dark night were lit by two lamp-like lights, one going with each when they parted until he reached home.
The Prophet said no one had favoured him more than Abu Bakr, who would be his Khalil if he took one, and ordered every mosque door closed except his.
The Prophet entered the Ka'bah with Bilal, Usama and Uthman bin Talha, and Bilal told Ibn Umar he prayed between the two pillars.
Horsemen sent to Najd brought back Thumama bin Uthal of Bani Hanifa, and he was tied to one of the mosque's pillars.
Umar said he would have punished men raising voices in the Prophet's mosque were they from Medina; when Ka'b argued loudly over a debt, the Prophet had him remit half.
Asked from the pulpit about night prayer, the Prophet said to pray two rak'at at a time and, fearing dawn, one rak'a as witr, the night's last prayer being odd.
Of three men at the Prophet's mosque gathering, Allah took in the one who joined the circle, sheltered the shy one behind, and turned from the one who left.
The Prophet was seen lying on his back in the mosque with one leg over the other, as Umar and Uthman also did.
Abu Bakr built a mosque in his courtyard, praying and weeping as he recited the Quran, which drew pagan women and children and alarmed the Quraysh chiefs.
Congregational prayer is twenty-five times better than prayer alone; each step to the mosque raises a degree and erases a sin, and angels pray for one waiting at his place.
The Prophet clasped his hands by interlacing his fingers.
The Prophet asked Abdullah bin Amr how he would fare when left among the worst remnants of people, who would be in conflict with each other.
The Prophet likened believers to bricks of a wall strengthening each other, interlacing his fingers as he said it.
After the Prophet ended a prayer at two rak'at, Dhul-Yadain asked if he forgot or it was shortened; when the people confirmed it, he completed it and made two prostrations.
Ibn Umar and his son Salim prayed at the places on the road between Medina and Mecca where the Prophet had prayed.
The Prophet prayed behind a spear as sutra at Eid and Al-Batha, passers going beyond it; his prayer place stood a sheep's width from the wall, and companions sought pillars.
Bilal told Ibn Umar the Prophet prayed inside the Ka'bah between the front pillars, about three cubits from the wall opposite the door, and Ibn Umar prayed there too.
The Prophet used his camel or saddle as sutra; one passing before a worshipper should be repulsed and sins gravely, and Aisha rejected likening women to dogs and donkeys.
The Prophet prayed with Aisha lying across before him, pushing her legs aside to prostrate and waking her for witr, with Maimuna beside him, and once carrying his granddaughter Umama.
As the Prophet prostrated by the Ka'bah, Uqba put camel entrails on his back as Quraysh laughed; Fatima removed them, he invoked against them, and they lay dead at Badr.
When Umar bin Abdul Aziz delayed a prayer, Urwa told him Gabriel had led the Prophet in the five prayers, and that Asr was prayed while sunshine lit Aisha's room.
The Abdul Qais delegation were ordered to believe in Allah, pray, give zakat and pay a fifth of spoils, and forbidden four vessels; Jarir pledged prayer, zakat and good advice.
Hudhaifa told Umar that afflictions from family, wealth and neighbours are expiated by prayer, fasting and charity, and that a door to be broken, Umar himself, held back wave-like afflictions.
Prayers wipe out evil deeds, even an unlawful kiss, as bathing five times a day removes dirt; timely prayer is the dearest deed, and Anas wept over prayer being lost.
One praying speaks privately to his Lord, so he spits left or under his foot, not ahead or right, and prostrates without laying his forearms flat like a dog.
In severe heat Zuhr is delayed until it cools and hillocks cast shadows, for intense heat is from Hell's raging; Hell was allowed two breaths, in summer and winter.
After Zuhr the Prophet spoke of the Hour and invited questions, naming Abdullah bin Hudhafa's father, until Umar knelt declaring contentment; he said Paradise and Hell had been shown him.
Abu Barza gave the Prophet's times, Zuhr at the sun's decline, Asr while the sun was hot and Isha late; Asr was prayed with sunshine still in Aisha's room.
Asr was prayed early enough to reach Quba or Al-Awali with the sun still high; whoever misses Asr is as if he lost family and property, his deeds annulled.
Believers will see their Lord as they see the full moon, so they should not miss the prayers before sunrise and sunset, when the angels of night and day gather.
Whoever catches one rak'a of Asr before sunset, or of Fajr before sunrise, should complete the prayer.
The Muslims' span beside earlier nations is like Asr to sunset; in parables of hired labourers, the Torah and Gospel people worked longer, yet the Muslims earned double.
Maghrib was prayed once the sun set, Isha early or late as people gathered and Fajr in darkness; Maghrib should not be called Isha as bedouins do.
With Isha delayed until people slept, the Prophet said none on earth but they awaited it, waiting counts as prayer, and but for hardship he would order it then.
Believers will see their Lord as they see the full moon, so they should not miss the prayers before sunrise and sunset; whoever prays these two cool prayers enters Paradise.
Fajr began about fifty verses' recitation after the pre-dawn meal, in a darkness that hid veiled women; whoever catches one rak'a of a prayer in its time has caught it.
The Prophet forbade prayer after Fajr until the sun rises and after Asr until it sets, and at sunrise and sunset themselves; Ibn Umar forbade only those two moments.
Aisha said the Prophet never missed two rak'at after Asr, praying them at home rather than in the mosque lest it burden his followers, and two before Fajr.
Asr is hastened on cloudy days; Fajr missed in sleep was prayed after sunrise, Asr missed at the Trench after sunset, and a forgotten prayer is prayed when remembered.
The Prophet preferred Isha late and disliked talk after it, said those waiting for prayer are in prayer, and after Isha said none then alive would outlive a hundred years.
Abu Bakr hosted three poor Suffa companions but stayed late with the Prophet; when they ate, the food increased from beneath, and it was taken to the Prophet.
When fire, a bell or horn were proposed to signal prayer, Umar suggested a man calling, and Bilal was ordered to say the adhan's words twice and the iqama's once.
Satan flees from the adhan and iqama, then returns to distract worshippers; all who hear the caller witness for him, and the Prophet held off attacking where adhan was heard.
Hearers repeat the caller's words, and the invocation after it earns the Prophet's intercession; knowing the reward, people would draw lots for the adhan and first row.
In rain the caller said pray at home; Bilal's adhan came at night so eating continued until Ibn Umm Maktum's at dawn, and two light rak'at preceded Fajr's iqama.
A prayer may be offered between adhan and iqama; companions prayed two rak'at before Maghrib, and the Prophet two light ones before Fajr, then lay on his right side.
Men going home and travellers were told to call the adhan and iqama and let the eldest lead; on a journey the Prophet delayed the Zuhr adhan until it cooled.
One of a group calls the Adhan and the eldest leads; on cold or rainy nights the caller adds 'Pray at your homes'; Bilal turned his face while calling.
Come to the prayer calmly, not hurrying, pray what you catch and complete what you missed; at the Iqama do not stand until you see the Prophet.
After the Iqama the Prophet, being junub, told the people to keep their places, bathed and returned with his head dripping to lead the prayer.
On the day of the Trench Umar said he could not pray Asr before sunset; the Prophet made ablution at Buthan and prayed Asr after sunset, then Maghrib.
After the Iqama the Prophet kept talking quietly with a man in a corner of the mosque, delaying the prayer until some people dozed.
The Prophet nearly burned the houses of men absent from congregational prayer, which is twenty-five or twenty-seven times better than praying alone; Abu ad-Darda found only it still kept up.
Walking far to the mosque, waiting for the imam, removing a thorny branch, the Adhan, the first row and Isha and Fajr earn reward; five kinds of death are martyrdom.
Fajr and Isha are heaviest for the hypocrites, and the Prophet nearly burned the houses of the absent; two people should give the Adhan and Iqama, the elder leading.
Angels pray for one waiting for the prayer, which counts as prayer; one attached to mosques is among seven Allah shades; going to the mosque earns a place in Paradise.
The Prophet rebuked a man praying two rak'at after the Iqama of Fajr had been called, asking whether Fajr has four rak'at.
In his fatal illness the Prophet had Abu Bakr lead, then came out supported by Al-Abbas and Ali and sat beside him; he was nursed in Aisha's house.
On cold, rainy or muddy days the caller said 'Pray in your homes'; the Prophet prayed at the homes of blind Itban and a heavy Ansari, and prostrated in mud.
When supper is served at the Iqama, eat first without hurrying; the Prophet stopped eating meat to pray without new ablution, and left his household work at prayer time.
Malik bin Huwairith led a prayer only to show how the Prophet prayed, sitting briefly after the prostration before rising from the first rak'a.
In his last illness the Prophet insisted Abu Bakr lead, calling the women companions of Joseph; on Monday he lifted his curtain, smiled at the rows, and died that day.
Abu Bakr stepped back when the Prophet arrived during his prayer, and men should say Subhan Allah rather than clap; the eldest leads; the Prophet led Itban's household when visiting.
Aisha tells how the Prophet, in his last illness, bathed and fainted repeatedly, sent Abu Bakr to lead, then prayed seated beside him while Abu Bakr and the people followed.
The imam is to be followed: bow, rise and prostrate after him, and sit if he sits; companions waited until he prostrated; one rising before him risks a donkey's head.
Salim, a slave knowing most Quran, led the first emigrants; obey a chief even if Ethiopian; an imam's mistake is his own; Uthman: share people's good deeds, avoid their bad.
Staying at Maimuna's house, Ibn Abbas stood at the Prophet's left in the night prayer and was drawn round to his right.
An imam should keep the prayer short for the weak, old and needy: the Prophet rebuked Mu'adh for reciting Al-Baqara, and shortened his own prayer on hearing a child cry.
In his last illness the Prophet sat at Abu Bakr's left and led seated, while Abu Bakr, standing, repeated his Takbir for the people to hear.
The Prophet ended a prayer after two rak'at; when Dhul-Yadain asked and the people confirmed it, he prayed the other two and made two prostrations.
In his last illness Aisha and Hafsa urged that Umar lead instead of the weeping Abu Bakr; the Prophet told them to keep quiet, calling them companions of Joseph.
Straighten the rows, shoulder to shoulder, for the Prophet sees behind him; if people knew the first row's reward they would draw lots for it; Anas found Medina's rows unaligned.
The Prophet moved Ibn Abbas from his left to his right; Anas and an orphan stood behind the Prophet, with Umm Sulaim alone behind them.
People followed the Prophet's night prayer behind a low wall or mat; he stopped, fearing it would become compulsory, and said the best prayer is at home except the compulsory.
After falling from a horse the Prophet led seated and said the imam is to be followed in Takbir, bowing, rising and prostration.
The Prophet raised both hands shoulder-high at the opening, bowing and rising; people were ordered to place the right hand on the left forearm; he supplicated silently before reciting.
The Prophet prayed the eclipse prayer with long standings, bowings and prostrations, then said Paradise and Hell came near and he saw a woman clawed by the cat she starved.
Followers watched the imam: Khabbab knew the Prophet recited in Zuhr and Asr from his moving beard, and Al-Bara's companions stood until they saw him prostrate.
In the eclipse prayer the Prophet reached for a bunch of Paradise's fruit, and once he saw Paradise and Hell displayed on the mosque's qibla wall.
Do not look up at the sky in prayer; glancing around is Satan stealing from it; a marked garment distracted the Prophet; none should spit towards the qibla.
During Fajr the Prophet lifted the curtain of Aisha's dwelling, smiled at the rows and signalled them to complete the prayer; he died late that day.
Accused at Kufa of praying badly, Sa'd said he lengthened the first two rak'at as the Prophet did; a prayer without Al-Fatiha is invalid; a man is taught calm prayer.
The Prophet recited Al-Mursalat or At-Tur in Maghrib, At-Tin in Isha, sixty to a hundred verses in Fajr; Abu Huraira prostrated at Surah 84; Al-Fatiha alone suffices.
When devils were barred from the news of heaven, jinn heard the Prophet reciting in Fajr at Nakhla, believed, and Allah revealed Surat al-Jinn about them.
The Prophet recited aloud or quietly as ordered, Al-Fatiha and a surah in the first two rak'at, the first longer; love of Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad earns Paradise.
Say Amin when the imam says it, or says 'nor of those who go astray'; one whose Amin coincides with the angels' has his past sins forgiven.
Abu Bakra is told not to bow before reaching the row again; Ali, Abu Huraira and others said Takbir at every bowing, rising and prostration, as the Prophet did.
Hands rest on the knees in bowing; one who skimps bowing and prostration has not prayed; after the imam's 'Sami'a l-lahu liman hamidah' followers say 'Rabbana laka l-hamd'.
After rising from bowing came the Qunut, asking forgiveness for believers and invoking against disbelievers and Mudar; angels raced to record a man's praise; the Prophet stood straight and long.
Believers will see their Lord like the full moon; the bridge over Hell, people brought out of Hell by their marks of prostration, and the last man to enter Paradise.
The Prophet kept his arms off his sides in prayer; he was ordered to prostrate on seven bones: forehead with nose, hands, knees, toes, not tucking up clothes or hair.
The Prophet sought the Night of Qadr in Itikaf, said it lies in the odd nights of the last ten, and his dream of prostrating in mud came true.
Men with small Izars tied them round their necks, and women were told not to rise from prostration before the men sat up; prostration is on seven bones.
Glorifying Allah in bowing and prostration, sitting between prostrations, a brief sitting before rising, forearms off the ground, Takbir aloud, and sitting on the left foot.
The Prophet stood up after two rak'at of Zuhr without sitting, and before the Taslim made two prostrations of forgetfulness while seated.
The Tashahhud the Prophet taught instead of 'peace be on Allah', who is As-Salam, and supplications in prayer: refuge from the grave, the Dajjal, sin and debt, and forgiveness.
Mud marked the Prophet's forehead from prostrating; followers said the Taslim together with him, as at Itban's house, and he stayed seated while the women left.
After compulsory prayers Allah was praised aloud; the poor are told to say Subhan Allah, Al-hamdu lillah and Allahu Akbar thirty-three times each; the Prophet's words of Allah's oneness.
After the Taslim the Prophet faced the people, once relaying Allah's words on crediting rain to stars; he waited for women to leave and once hurried to give away gold.
Whoever eats garlic or onion should keep away from the mosque; the Prophet declined a pot of strong-smelling vegetables, saying he converses with those they do not.
A man who passed a grave set apart from the others with the Prophet said the Prophet led the people in the funeral prayer, with them aligned behind him.
An orphan stood with Anas behind the Prophet; young Ibn Abbas joined the rows and the Eid; Friday bathing binds those past puberty; Isha was delayed till children slept.
Men should not stop women going to the mosque, even at night; women left first after the Taslim, unrecognised in Fajr's dark; Umm Sulaim stood behind Anas and an orphan.
Friday, which earlier nations differed over, was given to this nation; whoever attends should bathe, use siwak and perfume, come early and listen silently, his sins since last Friday forgiven.
Umar urged a silk cloak on the Prophet for Fridays; he said it is worn by one with no share in the Hereafter; Umar gave his to a pagan brother.
The Prophet would have ordered the siwak for every prayer but for the hardship, urged it repeatedly, cleaned his mouth at night, and used a siwak Aisha chewed for him.
The Prophet recited As-Sajda and Ad-Dahr in Friday's Fajr; the next Jumua after his mosque's was at Jawathi in Bahrain; a governor is told to lead Jumua, all being guardians.
Whoever comes to Jumua should bathe, a duty on all past puberty; Friday was given to this nation after others differed, and every Muslim should bathe once in seven days.
Women should be allowed to mosques at night; a wife of Umar kept praying Fajr and Isha there, as the Prophet forbade stopping Allah's women-slaves from Allah's mosques.
On a muddy day Ibn Abbas had people pray at home though Jumua is compulsory; bathing was urged on workers arriving dusty and sweaty; Jumua was prayed soon after midday.
Feet dusty in Allah's cause are saved from Hell; walk calmly to the prayer; whoever bathes and does not push between two people is forgiven; none may unseat another.
The Friday Adhan was called once the imam sat on the pulpit, until Uthman added one at Az-Zawra; Muawiya repeated the Adhan's words from the pulpit, as the Prophet did.
An Ansari woman's slave carpenter made the pulpit of tamarisk; the Prophet prayed on it to teach, the palm stem he stood by cried, and he preached standing, sitting between.
After the eclipse prayer the Prophet said 'Amma ba'du' and told that he had seen Paradise and Hell and that people will be tried in their graves, asked about him.
The Prophet opened addresses with the Tashahhud, praise and 'Amma ba'du', as when explaining why he gave to some and not others, and why he stopped leading the night prayer.
In his last gathering, from the pulpit, the Prophet said the Ansar will decrease, and any ruler should accept the good among them and overlook their wrongdoers' faults.
The Prophet gave two sermons, sitting between them; angels record Friday arrivals by the hour, then listen; a man entering during the sermon is told to pray two rak'at.
In a Friday sermon the Prophet prayed for rain at a man's request; it rained a week until a man asked again, and the Prophet prayed it away from Medina.
Telling a companion to be quiet during the sermon is wrong; Friday holds a short hour when requests are granted; people left for a food caravan, and a verse came.
The Prophet prayed two rak'at before and after Zuhr and after Maghrib and Isha, and after Jumua prayed two rak'at only once he was home.
After Jumua the companions ate a woman's dish of silq roots and barley, looking forward to Friday; they napped and ate only after the Jumua prayer, which was prayed early.
Facing the enemy, the Prophet led the fear prayer in two parties, one praying with him while the other stood guard, then changing; if outnumbered, pray standing or riding.
On the day of the Trench neither Umar nor the Prophet had prayed Asr before sunset; the Prophet made ablution at Buthan and prayed Asr, then Maghrib.
Returning from the Confederates, the Prophet said to pray Asr only at Bani Quraiza; some delayed it, others prayed on the way, and he blamed neither group.
After praying Fajr in the dark the Prophet rode on Khaybar; its fighters were killed, women and children taken captive, and he married Safiya, her freedom being her dowry.
Umar urged a silk cloak on the Prophet for Eid; he said it is for those with no share in the Hereafter, then later sent Umar one to sell.
On Eid the Prophet told Abu Bakr to leave two girls singing songs of Bu'ath, and let Aisha watch, standing behind him, as Bani Arfida played with shields and spears.
On Eid al-Adha the first act is the prayer and the sacrifice comes after returning from it; whoever does so follows the Prophet's way.
When Abu Bakr objected to two Ansari girls singing on Eid, the Prophet said every nation has its Eid; he ate an odd number of dates before Eid al-Fitr prayer.
A sacrifice slaughtered before the Eid prayer must be repeated, being only meat; the Prophet let Abu Burda offer a young she-goat instead, valid for him alone.
On both Eids the Prophet prayed first, without Adhan, then preached and went to the women for alms; Abu Sa'id protested when Marwan gave the sermon before the prayer.
The Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman prayed the Eid prayer before the sermon, without adhan; the Prophet then preached to the women, who gave their jewellery as alms.
On Eid the prayer comes first and the sacrifice after; an animal slaughtered before the prayer is only meat, and the Prophet allowed Abu Burda alone a young goat instead.
Wounded by a spearhead at Mina, Ibn Umar told Al-Hajjaj he was to blame, for allowing arms to be carried on a day they never were and inside the Haram.
In his Nahr sermon the Prophet said the prayer comes before slaughtering, a sacrifice before it is only meat, and Abu Burda alone could offer a young goat instead.
No good deeds on other days surpass those of the first ten days of Dhul Hijja, not even jihad, unless one risks life and property and returns with neither.
Asked on the way from Mina to Arafat how Talbiya was said with the Prophet, Anas said people said Talbiya and Takbir, and neither was objected to.
On Eid women, even virgins and menstruating women, were ordered out to say Takbir behind the men; a spear was the Prophet's sutra, and he told women to give alms.
Going towards Al-Baqi on Eid al-Adha the Prophet said prayer comes before sacrifice, an animal slaughtered earlier is no sacrifice, and allowed one man a young goat for himself alone.
After the Eid prayer and sermon the Prophet, with Bilal, preached to the women, who gave rings as alms; all women were ordered out, menstruating ones keeping from the musalla.
The Prophet slaughtered at the musalla; whoever slaughtered before the prayer was to slaughter again, others in Allah's name, and one man alone was allowed a young goat.
On Eid the Prophet returned by another way and prayed only two rak'at; he let girls beat tambourines in the days of Eid and Mina, and Aisha watch a display.
Night prayer is offered two rak'at at a time and closed with one rak'a of witr, as the Prophet did before Fajr's two rak'at; three-rak'at witr was also seen.
The Prophet prayed witr at various hours of the night, woke Aisha to pray it, told people to make it their last night prayer, and prayed it on his mount.
Qunut was recited in Fajr and Maghrib; for a month the Prophet recited it after bowing, invoking Allah against tribes who, despite a treaty, killed about seventy men he sent.
The Prophet went out to offer the prayer for rain and turned his cloak inside out.
Rising from the last bowing, the Prophet asked Allah to save named weak believers, send famine years on Mudar like Joseph's, forgive Ghifar and save Aslam.
When people refused Islam the Prophet prayed for famine years like Joseph's; hunger made them see smoke, Abu Sufyan asked him to pray for them, and verses 44:10-16 came down.
Ibn Umar recalled Abu Talib's verse watching the Prophet's rain prayer; Umar asked Al-Abbas to pray for rain; the Prophet faced the Qibla, reversed his cloak and prayed two rak'at.
Asked during the Friday sermon, the Prophet raised his hands and prayed for rain; it rained a week until he asked that it fall around them, not on them.
The rain prayer was held outside without pulpit, adhan or iqama: the Prophet faced the Qibla, invoked Allah, turned his cloak inside out and prayed two rak'at aloud.
The Prophet raised his hands high asking for rain, the people with him; seeing rain he asked for a fruitful rain, and prayed it away when excessive.
A strong wind brought anxiety to the Prophet's face, and he said he was granted victory with the wind As-Saba while 'Ad were destroyed by the westerly wind.
The Hour will not come until knowledge is taken away, earthquakes become frequent, time passes quickly, afflictions and killing increase and wealth overflows.
Asked twice to bless Najd too, the Prophet blessed only Sham and Yemen, saying earthquakes and afflictions would appear there and the side of Satan's head come from there.
After a night of rain at Al-Hudaibiya the Prophet said Allah declares that whoever credits rain to His blessing believes in Him, and whoever credits a star disbelieves in Him.
The keys of the unseen are five, known only to Allah: what tomorrow brings, what is in the womb, what one will gain, where one dies, and when rain falls.
When the sun eclipsed, as when his son Ibrahim died, the Prophet said sun and moon eclipse for no one's death or birth, and called for prayer and invocation.
The Prophet led a congregational eclipse prayer, standing and bowing long twice each rak'a, then said eclipses are Allah's signs to frighten His slaves, calling for remembrance, prayer and charity.
Asked by Aisha about punishment in the grave, which a Jewish woman had mentioned, the Prophet sought refuge from it, and after an eclipse prayer ordered people to seek refuge.
The Prophet bowed twice in each rak'a of a long eclipse prayer and said he saw Paradise, and Hell, mostly peopled by women ungrateful to husbands and good deeds.
After an eclipse prayer the Prophet said people will be tried in their graves: the believer affirms he is Allah's Messenger, the hypocrite says he does not know.
The Prophet ordered people to free slaves during the solar eclipse.
After a Jewish woman spoke of punishment in the grave the Prophet sought refuge from it, and after a long eclipse prayer ordered the people to seek refuge from it.
Sun and moon, signs of Allah, do not eclipse for anyone's death or life, as claimed at Ibrahim's death; at an eclipse hasten to pray, remember Allah and seek forgiveness.
The eclipse prayer, called in congregation and recited aloud, has four bowings and four prostrations in two rak'at; Abdullah bin Az-Zubair's two-rak'at version missed the Prophet's way.
The Prophet prostrated on reciting An-Najm, with all present but an old man who lifted earth to his forehead, and at Sad, yet not when Zaid recited An-Najm.
Abu Huraira prostrated at Al-Inshiqaq because the Prophet did, crowds prostrating with the Prophet lacked room, and Umar taught that the prostration is right but not compulsory.
The Prophet shortened prayers during a nineteen-day stay and in Mecca, and prayed two rak'at at Mina, as did Abu Bakr and Umar, while Uthman later prayed four.
The Prophet and his companions reached Mecca on the fourth of Dhul Hijja intending Hajj, and he told those without sacrificial animals to assume ihram for Umra instead.
A woman should not travel for more than three days, or in another narration a day and night, except with a mahram or her husband.
Prayers were first two rak'at and stayed so on journeys; the Prophet shortened Asr at Dhul-Hulaifa and, when hurried on a journey, prayed Maghrib together with Isha.
On journeys the Prophet prayed voluntary prayers and witr on his mount, nodding, facing wherever it went, but dismounted and faced the Qibla for the compulsory prayers.
On journeys the Prophet prayed two rak'at and no optional prayers, yet Um Hani saw him pray eight rak'at of Duha, and he prayed nawafil on his mount at night.
On journeys the Prophet combined Maghrib with Isha and Zuhr with Asr, delaying Zuhr to Asr's time if he set out before noon, with no optional prayer between them.
Ill or hurt by a fall, the Prophet prayed sitting, signalled those standing behind him to sit, and said the imam is to be followed in Takbir, bowing and rising.
Prayer standing is best, sitting earns half its reward, lying half again; the unable sit or lie on their side, and the aged Prophet recited sitting, then stood to bow.
The Prophet praised Allah on rising for Tahajjud, prayed eleven rak'at with long prostrations, wished Ibn Umar prayed it after his dream of the Fire, and missed it when ill.
When Gabriel did not come for a time and a Quraysh woman said his Satan had left him, revelation came that his Lord had neither forsaken nor hated him.
The Prophet urged the women of his dwellings, and Ali and Fatima, to pray at night, and left loved deeds like the mosque's Ramadan night prayer lest they become compulsory.
The Prophet prayed until his feet swelled, to be a thankful slave, rose at cock's crow, used siwak and stood long; David's prayer and fasting were most beloved to Allah.
The night prayer is two rak'at at a time ended by witr; the Prophet prayed seven to thirteen rak'at, and at night he could be seen praying or sleeping.
Satan's three knots on a sleeper are undone by remembrance, ablution and prayer; in a dream one who slept through prayers was punished, and Satan urinated in an oversleeper's ears.
In every night's last third our Lord comes down to the nearest heaven, asking who will invoke Him, ask of Him or seek His forgiveness, so He may answer.
The Prophet slept early and prayed late in the night, never over eleven rak'at in Ramadan or otherwise, his heart awake as his eyes slept, reciting sitting in old age.
Bilal, whose footsteps the Prophet heard ahead of him in Paradise, said his best deed was praying after every ablution, by day or night.
The Prophet had a prayer rope removed and told people to pray while energetic, do deeds within their capacity, not abandon night prayer, and give body and family their right.
Whoever wakes at night, declares Allah's oneness and asks forgiveness is answered, his prayer after ablution accepted; Ibn Rawaha's verse says the Prophet spends nights away from his bed.
After Ibn Umar's dreams the Prophet wished he prayed Tahajjud, and finding the companions' dreams agree, said to seek the Night of Decree in Ramadan's last ten nights.
The Prophet never missed the two light rak'at before Fajr, praying them after the adhan, then lay on his right side or talked with Aisha until the iqama.
The Prophet taught Istikhara's two rak'at and invocation and two rak'at on entering a mosque, even mid-sermon, and prayed two before and after Zuhr and after Jumua, Maghrib and Isha.
With the Prophet, Zuhr and Asr were prayed together as eight rak'at and Maghrib and Isha as seven, which the narrators thought meant delaying one prayer and advancing the other.
Ibn Umar doubted the Prophet prayed Duha and Aisha never saw it, yet Um Hani saw him pray eight rak'at, and he advised Abu Huraira to pray it.
The Prophet kept ten voluntary rak'at around the daily prayers, never missed four before Zuhr and two before Fajr, and allowed prayer before Maghrib without making it a tradition.
The Prophet prayed two rak'at at a spot Itban chose in his house, saying whoever declares Allah's oneness seeking His pleasure is saved from Hell; pray some prayers at home.
Journeys should be made only to three mosques; a prayer in the Prophet's Mosque surpasses a thousand elsewhere but al-Masjid al-Haram, and he went to Quba Mosque every Saturday.
Between the Prophet's house and his pulpit is a garden of the gardens of Paradise, and his pulpit is on his fountain tank.
Four rulings: a woman travels two days only with husband or mahram, no fasting on the two Eids, no prayer after Fajr or Asr, and journeys only to three mosques.
Staying at Maimuna's house, Ibn Abbas joined the Prophet's night prayer; the Prophet twisted his ear, prayed twelve rak'at in twos and one witr, then two light rak'at before Fajr.
Speaking in prayer stopped when 2.238 came down and the tashahhud replaced greetings; men say Subhan Allah and women clap, and Abu Bakr, leading, drew back for the Prophet.
Juraij kept praying through his mother's three calls; she prayed he would see prostitutes' faces, a shepherdess named him her child's father, and the infant named the shepherd.
Levelling the ground once for prostration is allowed, worshippers prostrated on their clothes in scorching heat, and the Prophet touched Aisha's legs stretched before him when he prostrated.
The Prophet said Satan tried to interrupt his prayer and he choked him, but recalling Solomon's prayer for a unique kingdom, he did not tie him to a pillar.
Rebuked by a Kharijite, Abu Barza said he saw the Prophet's leniency in battles and would rather keep his struggling animal while praying than let it return to its stable.
In the eclipse prayer the Prophet stepped forward on seeing Paradise and back on seeing Hell, where he saw Amr bin Luhai, who began freeing animals in idols' names.
One praying speaks privately to his Lord, so he spits only to his left; with men's short sheets tied at the neck, women waited to lift heads until men sat.
The Prophet did not return greetings while praying, even on his mount, told people to say Subhan Allah instead of clapping, and hands on hips in prayer were forbidden.
Remembering gold at home during prayer, the Prophet hurried to have it given away; Satan distracts the worshipper until he loses count, which two prostrations make good.
When the Prophet forgot to sit after two rak'at, prayed five, or ended after two, he made two prostrations of forgetfulness; whoever loses count through Satan's distraction does the same.
Praying, the Prophet beckoned Um Salama's maid to wait, Abu Bakr to continue, followers to sit; Aisha nodded to Asma; his two rak'at after Asr replaced two missed after Zuhr.
Whoever dies worshipping none besides Allah enters Paradise, even after adultery and theft, and whoever dies worshipping others besides Him enters the Fire.
A Muslim's rights on Muslims include returning greetings, visiting the sick, following funerals, accepting invitations and answering sneezers; silver vessels, gold rings and silk were forbidden.
Abu Bakr kissed the dead Prophet, weeping, then told the people that whoever worshipped Muhammad, he is dead, but Allah is alive, and recited 3:144.
The Prophet questioned a claim that Allah honoured the dead Uthman bin Maz'un, allowed weeping over a martyr, prayed for An-Najashi, wept announcing three martyrs, and prayed at a grave.
A Muslim whose three children, or even two, die before puberty is granted Paradise and screened from the Fire.
The Prophet told a woman weeping beside a grave to fear Allah and be patient.
The Prophet had his dead daughter washed an odd number of times with water and Sidr, from the right side, with camphor last, and shrouded in his waist-sheet.
The Prophet had his dead daughter washed three, five or more times with water and Sidr, camphor last, and shrouded in his waist-sheet; her hair was put in three braids.
The Prophet was shrouded in three white cotton sheets; a pilgrim killed by his mount at Arafat was shrouded in two sheets, unperfumed and bareheaded, to rise saying Labbaik.
The Prophet gave his shirt to shroud Abdullah bin Ubai and prayed over him despite Umar's objection; a verse then forbade praying over dead hypocrites.
The Prophet was shrouded in three cotton sheets; Abdur-Rahman wept that Mus'ab and Hamza had only a Burd as shroud; a man asked for the Prophet's cloak as his shroud.
Women were forbidden, not strictly, to follow funerals, and may mourn no one over three days except a husband, four months and ten days, as Um Habiba and Zainab taught.
The Prophet told a woman weeping at a grave that patience is at the first stroke of a calamity, urged his daughter to be patient, and called his tears mercy.
The Prophet wept at his daughter's grave; Umar said the dead are punished for relatives' wailing, which Aisha limited to disbelievers; slapping cheeks and tearing clothes are condemned.
Visiting the sick Sa'd, whose only heir was a daughter, the Prophet limited his bequest in charity to one third, heirs being better left rich, and pitied Sa'd bin Khaula.
The Prophet disowned those who wail, shave their heads, slap cheeks or tear clothes; grieving Zaid, Ja'far and Ibn Rawaha, he had Ja'far's crying women forbidden.
Abu Talha's wife hid their son's death from him until morning, and the Prophet prayed that their night be blessed; real patience is at the first stroke of a calamity.
The Prophet wept for his son Ibrahim and, beside the sick Sa'd bin Ubada, said Allah punishes for the tongue, not tears; only five women kept the pledge against wailing.
Stand for a passing funeral procession, even a Jew's, until it passes or is set down, and do not sit before it is down; carry the dead quickly.
The Prophet led An-Najashi's funeral prayer in rows with four Takbir and prayed at a grave of one buried at night; attending a funeral prayer earns a Qirat, burial two.
The Prophet ordered a Jewish man and woman, brought to him for illegal sexual intercourse, to be stoned near the place of funeral prayers beside the mosque.
Allah cursed Jews and Christians for praying at their prophets' graves; the Prophet stood by a dead woman's middle, said four Takbir and prayed at graves; Al-Fatiha is recited.
Two angels ask the newly buried about the Prophet; the believer is shown his place in Paradise, while the disbeliever or hypocrite is struck with an iron hammer.
Moses slapped the angel of death; offered years as many as the hairs under his hand on an ox, he chose death then, near the Sacred Land.
The Prophet prayed over a man buried at night, called those who build places of worship with pictures at graves the worst creatures, and had Abu Talha bury his daughter.
Uhud's martyrs were buried in pairs, the one knowing more Quran first, in their blood, unwashed and unprayed for; another report says the Prophet prayed for them.
Allah made Mecca a sanctuary where none may cut its plants, chase its game or pick up lost things except to announce them, idhkhir excepted for graves, goldsmiths and houses.
The Prophet had the dead Abdullah bin Ubai taken from his grave and clothed in the Prophet's shirt, in return, people thought, for Ibn Ubai's shirt given to Al-Abbas.
Jabir moved his father, Uhud's first martyr, to a separate grave after six months, barely changed; the Prophet buried Uhud's martyrs two to a grave, unwashed, in their blood.
The Prophet tested the boy Ibn Saiyad and refused Umar leave to kill him, saying the Dajjal could not be overpowered; he later tried to overhear him.
A sick Jewish boy serving the Prophet embraced Islam; Ibn Abbas was a child among the weak; every child is born with true faith and receives the funeral prayer.
Dying, Abu Talib refused the Prophet's call to declare Allah's oneness and, urged by Abu Jahl, kept Abdul Muttalib's religion; a verse forbade seeking forgiveness for pagans.
Passing two graves, the Prophet said one man was punished for carelessness with urine, the other for slander, and fixed a green palm leaf on each to lessen it.
At a funeral in Baqi the Prophet said every soul's place in Paradise or Hell is written; asked why act, he said good deeds are made easy for the blessed.
Whoever swears falsely by another religion is as he said; whoever kills himself by iron, throttling or stabbing repeats it in Hell, and Paradise was forbidden to one who did.
Umar objected when the Prophet stood to pray over Abdullah bin Ubai; the Prophet said he had been given the choice and prayed, and soon verses forbade it.
When people praised a passing dead man the Prophet said Paradise was affirmed for him, and Hell when they spoke ill; even two Muslims testifying to piety suffice.
The believer in his grave testifies to Allah and His Messenger; the Prophet addressed Badr's slain in the well, confirmed the grave's punishment and sought refuge from it.
Two angels question the buried; Jews were heard punished in their graves; the Prophet sought refuge from that punishment; the dead are shown their place morning and evening.
A Muslim whose three children die before puberty enters Paradise; Ibrahim has a wet-nurse there; Allah knows what pagans' children would have done; every child is born with true faith.
In a dream Gabriel and Michael showed the Prophet the punishment of a liar, a neglecter of the Quran, adulterers and usurers, then Abraham with children and the martyrs' home.
Dying, Abu Bakr asked Aisha about the Prophet's shroud and the day he died, hoped to die that Monday, and asked to be shrouded in his worn garment.
The Prophet told a man whose mother died suddenly that she would be rewarded if he gave alms on her behalf.
The Prophet died in Aisha's lap and was buried in her house, his grave not made prominent lest it be prayed at; a foot later exposed there was Umar's.
Aisha chose burial in Al-Baqi, not beside the Prophet and his two companions; the stabbed Umar sought her leave to lie beside them and named six for the caliphate.
The Prophet said not to abuse the dead, for they have reached the result of what they sent forward.
When Abu Lahab said to the Prophet, "Perish you all the day," the revelation came: perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he.
Zakat, taken from the rich for the poor, ranks with worship and prayer among deeds leading to Paradise; Abu Bakr vowed to fight anyone withholding it, and Umar agreed.
Unpaid Zakat returns on Judgement Day as trampling animals and a snake; paying it purifies wealth, none is due below set amounts, and Abu Dhar warned hoarders.
Spending wealth rightly is worth envying; Allah grows charity from honest earnings; give now, for before the Hour a time will come when no one accepts charity.
A verse answered those mocking large and small gifts; companions worked as porters to give; half a date shields from Hell, as do daughters treated well; give while healthy.
The wife with the longest hand, first to follow the Prophet, loved charity; alms given unknowingly to a thief, adulteress and rich man may reform them; secret givers are shaded.
A wife giving food from home is rewarded, as are her husband and storekeeper; the best charity is from surplus, dependents first; the giver's hand is better than the beggar's.
The Prophet hurried to give away charity gold before night, had women give jewellery at Eid, urged interceding for those who ask, and told Asma not to withhold money.
Hudhaifa told Umar that failings with family and neighbours are expiated by prayer and charity, and that a closed door, Umar himself, held back tribulation spreading like waves.
Charity and good deeds done before Islam keep their reward; a wife giving food from her husband's house, and an honest storekeeper paying as told, are rewarded alongside the husband.
Angels pray daily for spenders and against misers, whose iron cloak never widens; every Muslim owes charity, by work, help or good deeds; passed-on charity reaches its place.
No Zakat is due below five camels, uqiyas or wasqs; Abu Bakr's letter allows another camel age with adjustment and bars combining or splitting herds; women gave ornaments at Eid.
Abu Bakr's letter set Zakat on camels, sheep and silver, refusing old or defective animals; he would fight over a withheld goat; Mu'adh was to spare people's best property.
Abu Talha gave his beloved Bairuha garden to his relatives on the Prophet's advice; after urging women to give alms, the Prophet told Zainab her husband and children deserved hers.
No Zakat is due on a Muslim's horse or slave.
The Prophet feared the world's splendour for his people: wealth is sweet and green, blessed when given to the poor, orphans and travellers, but taken wrongly it never satisfies.
Zainab earns a double reward for giving Zakat to her husband and the orphans in her care, and Um Salama is rewarded for spending on Abu Salama's children.
Told three men refused Zakat, the Prophet faulted Ibn Jamil, whom Allah made rich, excused Khalid, whose armour was kept for Allah's cause, and said Al-Abbas owes it double.
Whoever refrains from asking, Allah makes content; selling firewood beats begging; wealth taken without greed is blessed; one who keeps begging comes on Judgement Day with a fleshless face.
