Sent to govern Yemen, Abu Musa and Mu'adh are told to make things easy; the Prophet forbids all intoxicants, an apostate is killed, and they compare their Quran recitation.
Abu Musa, back from governing his people, took Ihram with the Prophet's intention but brought no sacrificial animal, so is told to do Tawaf and Sa'i and end Ihram.
Mu'adh is told to invite the People of the Scripture in Yemen to the testimony, then prayer, then Zakat; there he leads Fajr reciting that Allah took Abraham as Khalil.
The Prophet sends Ali to Yemen in Khalid's place, and tells Buraida, who hated Ali and faulted his taking a slave-girl from the fifth, that Ali deserves more than that.
Rebuked over sharing Ali's gold among four, the Prophet refuses Khalid's request to kill the man and foretells people from his offspring who recite the Quran but leave the religion.
Ali, back from Yemen, took Ihram with the Prophet's intention and is told to keep it, as they have sacrificial animals; those without one make their Ihram Umrah.
The Prophet sends Jarir with 150 Ahmas riders to Dhul-Khalasa, an idol house called the Yemeni Ka'bah; he prays for Jarir to sit firm, and Jarir burns and dismantles it.
Amr bin al-As, commander at Dhat-us-Salasil, asks whom the Prophet loves most and hears Aisha, then her father, then Umar, then many other men.
In Yemen Dhu Amr tells Jarir the Prophet died three days ago, which riders confirm; he says Arabs prosper while they choose chiefs, but rule taken by sword makes kings.
Three hundred men under Abu Ubaida on the coast, reduced to a date a day and eating leaves, eat a huge fish for half a month; the Prophet eats some.
At the Hajj Abu Bakr led before the Farewell Hajj, it is announced that no pagan may make Hajj after that year and none may circle the Ka'bah naked.
Al-Bara says the last surah revealed in full was Bara'a, and the last revealed were the closing verses of an-Nisa', on those who leave no descendants or ascendants.
The Banu Tamim delegation asks for gifts beyond good tidings; Abu Huraira lists three qualities the Prophet ascribed to them, and Abu Bakr and Umar argue over appointing their ruler.
Abdul Qais delegates are told to believe, pray, pay Zakat, fast and give a fifth of booty, and forbidden four vessels; they delay the Prophet's two rak'at until after Asr.
Thumama, captured by cavalry sent to Najd and tied in the mosque, is released on the third day, embraces Islam, performs Umrah and vows to withhold Yamama's wheat from Mecca.
Musailima in Medina asks to rule after the Prophet, who refuses him even a stick; his dream of two gold bangles blown away meant two liars, al-Ansi and Musailima.
Abu Raja recalls worshipping stones and mounds of earth before Islam, removing spearheads in Rajab, and his people running to Musailima when they heard of the Prophet.
Musailima, in Medina, offers not to contest the Prophet's rule if it is his afterwards; refused, he is named with al-Ansi as the two liars of the bangles dream.
The rulers of Najran, deciding against mutual cursing, ask for a trustworthy man, and the Prophet sends Abu Ubaida bin al-Jarrah, the most trustworthy of this nation.
After the Prophet's death Abu Bakr invites anyone the Prophet owed or promised, and, after delays, gives Jabir the Bahrain money promised him, calling miserliness the worst disease.
Abu Musa, arriving from Yemen, at first takes Ibn Mas'ud and his mother for members of the Prophet's family, so often did they enter upon him.
Abu Musa tells a man who swore off chicken that the Prophet swore not to give the Ash'ariyin mounts, then did, acting on a better course and expiating his oath.
People of Yemen accept the good tidings Banu Tamim refused; the Prophet says belief and wisdom are Yemenite and Yemenis gentle-hearted, while harshness and afflictions come from the east.
Ibn Mas'ud has Alqama recite fifty verses of Surat Maryam, which Khabbab praises, then tells Khabbab to throw away his gold ring, and he does.
Asked by Tufail bin Amr to invoke Allah against the Daus, who refused Islam, the Prophet instead asks Allah to guide them and bring them.
Abu Huraira, arriving to pledge allegiance to the Prophet, sees his runaway slave reappear and frees him for Allah's sake.
Coming to Umar in a delegation, Adi bin Hatim is told he embraced Islam when his people disbelieved, kept promises they broke and recognised the truth they denied.
At the Farewell Hajj those with sacrificial animals keep Ihram, others end it after Tawaf; menstruating Aisha does Umrah later; a daughter may perform Hajj for her frail father.
In the year of the Conquest the Prophet enters the Ka'bah with Usama, Bilal and Uthman bin Talha and prays between its two front pillars.
Safiya menstruates in the Farewell Hajj, but as she has already done Tawaf al-Ifada, the Prophet lets her set off.
At the Farewell Hajj, his only Hajj after migrating, the Prophet warns of the Dajjal, declares blood and property sacred and forbids killing one another; verse 5:3 came at Arafat.
Aisha says pilgrims took Ihram for Umrah, Hajj or both; the Prophet's was for Hajj, and those for Hajj or both kept it until the day of sacrifice.
Visiting Sa'd, gravely ill in the Farewell Hajj, the Prophet limits his charity of his wealth to a third, as leaving heirs rich is better than leaving them poor.
At the Farewell Hajj the Prophet and some companions shave their heads, others cut their hair; Ibn Abbas's donkey passes the row at Mina; the Prophet combines Maghrib and Isha.
For Tabuk the Prophet refuses Abu Musa's companions mounts, then gives six camels; he leaves Ali in Medina like Aaron to Moses, and denies a biter compensation for his tooth.
Ka'b bin Malik tells how he stayed behind from Tabuk without excuse, told the Prophet the truth, was shunned fifty nights with two others, and Allah accepted their repentance.
Passing al-Hijr, the Prophet tells his companions to enter the dwellings of those punished for wronging themselves only weeping, covers his head and hurries through the valley.
During Tabuk the Prophet wipes over his khuffs; returning, he calls Uhud a mountain that loves us, and says those kept in Medina by genuine excuse were with them.
The Prophet sends a letter to Khosrau through the governor of Bahrain; Khosrau tears it up, and the Prophet is reported to have invoked Allah to tear them to pieces.
Abu Bakra recalls the Prophet saying, when the Persians crowned Khosrau's daughter, that a people ruled by a lady will never succeed, which kept him from fighting at al-Jamal.
As-Sa'ib remembers going out with the boys to Thaniyat-ul-Wada to welcome the Prophet back from Tabuk.
In his last illness the Prophet feels the Khaibar poison and leads a last Maghrib; people dispute his Thursday request to write; verse 110:1 is read as foretelling his death.
Fatima weeps then laughs at his secret words; given the choice, the Prophet asks for the highest companion and uses a siwak, and Aisha recites the Mu'awwidhat over him.
Gravely ill, the Prophet curses Jews and Christians for making prophets' graves places of worship, is nursed in Aisha's house, and has Abu Bakr lead the prayer despite Aisha's objection.
Ali refuses Abbas's urging to ask the ailing Prophet about the Caliphate; the Prophet smiles at the Muslims praying Fajr, and dies in Aisha's house after using a siwak.
Abu Bakr kisses the dead Prophet, then tells the people that Muhammad is dead but Allah lives, reciting verse 3:144, and Umar collapses on hearing it.
Those who forced medicine on him are made to take it; Aisha denies he willed the rule to Ali; he left only a mule, weapons and land; Fatima grieves.
The Prophet spent ten years in Mecca receiving the Quran and ten in Medina, died aged sixty-three, and at his death his armor was mortgaged to a Jew for barley.
When people criticise Usama's command of the troops, the Prophet says they criticised his father Zaid's before, Zaid deserved it, and Usama is among those dearest to him.
Abu al-Khair, emigrating from Yemen, hears the Prophet was buried five days before, and learns Bilal said the Night of Qadr is one of seven nights in the last ten.
Companions count the Prophet's Ghazawat: Zaid bin Arqam says nineteen, of which he joined seventeen, while al-Bara fought fifteen and Buraida sixteen with him.
Al-Fatiha, the seven oft-repeated verses, is the greatest surah of the Quran, and whoever says Ameen when the imam ends it, in time with the angels, is forgiven.
On the Day of Resurrection believers ask Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus to intercede; all decline; the Prophet intercedes until only those the Quran confines remain in Hell.
The greatest sins are setting up a rival to Allah, killing one's son for fear he will share one's food, and adultery with a neighbour's wife.
The Kam'a fungus is like manna, and its water is a cure for eye trouble.
Told to enter the gate prostrating and saying 'Hittatun', the Children of Israel entered dragging themselves on their buttocks and added 'a grain in a hair'.
Abdullah bin Salam asks the Prophet three questions only a prophet knows, embraces Islam, and the Jews, who had called him their best, then disparage him.
Umar calls Ubai the best reciter yet leaves some of his statements, since Ubai keeps all he heard though Allah says He abrogates verses or causes them to be forgotten.
Allah says the son of Adam lies against Him by denying He can recreate him, and abuses Him by claiming He has offspring, though He has no wife or child.
Umar says his Lord agreed with him in three things: the station of Abraham as a place of prayer, veiling the Prophet's wives, and warning them of better wives.
The Prophet tells Aisha the Ka'bah was not built on all Abraham's foundations, and he would rebuild it were her people not so recently out of heathenism.
As the People of the Scripture read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic, the Prophet says neither believe nor disbelieve them but declare belief in Allah's revelation.
After praying towards Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months the Prophet faces the Ka'bah; others turn while bowing; Allah reveals the prayers of those who died before are not lost.
On the Day of Resurrection Noah says he conveyed the Message, his nation denies it, and the Prophet's followers testify for him, as the verse on a just nation describes.
People praying Fajr at Quba hear the Prophet has been ordered to face the Ka'bah and turn to it from Jerusalem; Anas is the last left who prayed towards both.
Aisha corrects Urwa's reading of the verse on Safa and Marwa: it came because Ansar held going between them sinful; Anas says they had dropped it as pre-Islamic.
The Prophet says whoever dies invoking a rival to Allah enters Hell, and Ibn Mas'ud adds that whoever dies without doing so enters Paradise.
Unlike the Children of Israel, Muslims may take blood money instead of retribution, a mercy; for a girl's broken tooth the Prophet rules retribution until her family forgives.
People fasted on Ashura before Islam and the Prophet ordered it in Medina, but once fasting in Ramadan was prescribed, fasting on Ashura became optional.
Ibn Abbas said the verse allowing feeding a poor person instead of fasting still applies to the old who cannot fast; Ibn Umar and Salama said it was abrogated.
When Ramadan was prescribed some men broke the abstention from their wives and Allah forgave them; the white and black threads were explained as day and night, not real threads.
In the pre-Islamic period people in ihram entered their houses from the back, so Allah revealed that righteousness is fearing Allah, and to enter houses by their doors.
During Ibn az-Zubair's strife, Ibn Umar refused to shed his brother's blood, saying the command to fight until there is no affliction was fulfilled in the Prophet's time.
Hudhaifa said the verse about spending and not throwing oneself into destruction was revealed concerning spending in Allah's Cause.
Verses of Hajj explained: the ransom for shaving the head when lice troubled Ka'b bin Ujra, Hajj at-Tamattu, trading in the Hajj season, and departing from Arafat with the people.
The Prophet used to ask Allah for good in this world and in the Hereafter and to be saved from the torment of the Fire.
The Prophet said the most hated man in Allah's sight is the most quarrelsome.
Ibn Abbas read 'kudhibu' in the verse on messengers losing hope, but Aisha read 'kudh-dhibu', saying the messengers feared their followers would call them liars, never doubting Allah's promise.
On 'your wives are a tilth', Ibn Umar spoke of how a man may approach his wife; Jabir said it answered a Jewish saying about intercourse from the back.
When Ma'qil bin Yasar refused to let his divorced sister remarry her former husband after her waiting period, the verse forbidding such prevention was revealed.
Uthman would not remove a widows' verse said to be abrogated; the widow's four months and ten days, her year's bequest of residence, and a pregnant widow's term are explained.
On the day of the Trench the Prophet said the pagans had kept them from the middle prayer till sunset; the verse on guarding the prayers ended speaking in prayer.
In the fear prayer the imam leads each of two groups in one rak'a while the other faces the enemy; in great fear people may pray standing or riding.
Uthman told Ibn az-Zubair he would not move anything of the Quran from its place, keeping the widows' verse said to be abrogated.
The Prophet said we have more right to doubt than Abraham, who asked Allah to show him how He gives life to the dead so his faith would be stronger.
Ibn Abbas called the verse of the garden a parable for deeds; Umar explained it as a rich man whose good deeds are lost when Satan leads him into sin.
The Prophet said the poor person is not the one a date or a morsel will satisfy, but the one who does not beg from people or show his poverty.
When the verses of Al-Baqara on usury were revealed the Prophet recited them and prohibited trade in alcohol; Ibn Abbas said the usury verse was the last revealed.
Ibn Umar said the verse 'whether you show what is in your minds or conceal it' was abrogated by the verse following it.
The Prophet recited the verse on the Book's clear and unclear verses and warned against those who follow the unclear ones, saying Allah named them as deviating.
Satan touches every newborn child, who cries out at his touch, except Mary and her son.
A false oath taken to seize a Muslim's property brings Allah's anger; the verse is linked to Al-Ash'ath's well and a trader's false oath, and the defendant takes the oath.
Heraclius of Byzantium questioned Abu Sufyan about the Prophet, said the answers marked a true prophet, and read the letter calling him to Islam and to a common word.
When the verse on spending what you love was revealed, Abu Talha gave his beloved Bairuha garden in Allah's Cause, and on the Prophet's advice divided it among his relatives.
Jews brought a man and woman who had committed illegal intercourse; when Abdullah bin Salam exposed the stoning verse hidden in the Torah, the Prophet ordered them stoned.
Abu Huraira explained 'the best of peoples' as the best for people, who bring others with chains on their necks until they embrace Islam.
Jabir said the verse about two parties about to lose heart, with Allah their Protector, concerned Banu Haritha and Banu Salama, and they were glad it was revealed.
After bowing in prayer the Prophet cursed certain people and tribes and prayed for named men to be saved, until the verse 'Not for you is the decision' came.
At Uhud the infantry under Abdullah bin Jubair returned defeated, leaving twelve men with the Prophet, and slumber overtook Abu Talha till his sword kept falling.
'Allah is sufficient for us and the best Disposer of affairs' was said by Abraham when thrown into the fire, and by Muhammad when warned of a great army.
Wealth whose zakat is unpaid will become a bald poisonous snake on the Day of Resurrection, coiling round its owner's neck and biting his cheeks.
Abdullah bin Ubai rebuffed the Prophet's preaching; the Prophet excused him, for Muslims were then ordered to forgive the pagans and People of the Scripture until fighting was permitted.
Some hypocrites stayed behind from the Prophet's campaigns, then made false excuses and oaths, wanting praise for what they had not done, so the verse about them was revealed.
Ibn Abbas told Marwan the verse on loving praise for what one has not done concerned Jews who hid the truth from the Prophet and wanted praise for answering.
Staying with his aunt Maimuna, Ibn Abbas saw the Prophet wake at night, recite the last ten verses of Al Imran and pray two by two, ending with witr.
Guardians were forbidden to marry orphan girls for their wealth or beauty without a fair dowry, and a poor guardian may take a reasonable wage from the orphan's property.
The inheritance verses cover relatives present at the division, the shares of children, parents and spouses, the ban on inheriting women against their will, and ending inheritance by brotherhood.
Believers will see Allah on the Day of Resurrection as clearly as the sun and full moon, after each nation that worshipped other than Allah falls into Hell.
Ibn Masud recited An-Nisa to the Prophet, who liked hearing the Quran from others; at the verse on a witness from each nation he stopped him, eyes overflowing with tears.
When Asma's necklace was lost and the men searching for it prayed without ablution for lack of water, Allah revealed the verse of tayammum.
Ibn Abbas said the verse on obeying Allah, the Apostle and those in authority was revealed about Abdullah bin Hudhafa when the Prophet made him commander of a detachment.
When an Ansari disputing water claimed the Prophet favoured his cousin Az-Zubair, the Prophet gave Az-Zubair his full right; Az-Zubair linked the verse on making the Prophet judge.
Every sick prophet is offered this world or the Hereafter; in his last illness the Prophet recited the verse on those Allah blessed, and Aisha knew he was offered it.

Ubai bin Ka'b, told that Ibn Mas'ud excluded the two surahs of refuge, says the Prophet told him they were revealed to him and he recited them.
The Quran came to the Prophet over ten years in Mecca, most heavily before his death, in Quraysh's dialect; Gabriel looked like Dihya, and revelation left the Prophet red-faced.
After Yamama Abu Bakr has Zaid bin Thabit collect the Quran; Uthman sends a copy to every province and has other copies burnt; Zaid also wrote verses for the Prophet.
Gabriel recited the Quran to the Prophet in seven ways, and when Umar objects to Hisham's different reading of al-Furqan, the Prophet says both were revealed so.
Aisha explains why a surah mentioning Paradise and the Fire came before laws, and dictates the surahs in order; companions name surahs learnt early and paired surahs the Prophet recited.
Gabriel met the Prophet every night of Ramadan to go over the Quran, once a year and twice in the year he died, when he stayed twenty days in Itikaf.
The Prophet names four companions to learn the Quran from; Ibn Mas'ud knows where every surah came down, four Ansar collected it, and Ubai was the best reciter.
Al-Fatiha is the most superior surah and cured a chief stung by a scorpion, and reciting the last two verses of al-Baqarah at night is sufficient.
A thief caught stealing Zakat food tells Abu Huraira that reciting Ayat al-Kursi at bedtime brings Allah's guard against Satan, and the Prophet says the liar, Satan, spoke the truth.
Tranquillity and angels descended on reciters of al-Kahf and al-Baqarah; the Prophet loved al-Fath; al-Ikhlas equals a third of the Quran; he recited the refuge surahs and blew over himself.
Ibn Abbas and Muhammad bin al-Hanafiyya say the Prophet left nothing except what is between the two bindings of the Quran.
A believer reciting the Quran is like a citron and a wicked reciter like basil; Muslims working from Asr to sunset earn twice the wage of Jews and Christians.
Asked if the Prophet made a will, Abdullah bin Abi Aufa first says no, then that he made a will recommending Allah's Book.
Allah listens to no prophet as He listens to one who recites the Quran aloud in a pleasant tone.
One may wish to be like only two men: one given the Quran who recites it night and day, and one given wealth who spends it rightly.
The best of the Muslims are those who learn the Quran and teach it.
A woman offers herself to the Prophet, who marries her to a man owning not even an iron ring for the amount of the Quran he knows by heart.
Keep reciting the Quran, which escapes faster than tied camels, and do not say 'I forgot'; the Prophet recited al-Fath riding, and Ibn Abbas learnt the Mufassal as a boy.
A reciter reminds the Prophet of missed verses; saying 'I forgot' is disliked, the Quran was revealed in several readings, and reciting the Mufassal in a day is too quick.
The Prophet moved his tongue hastily as Gabriel brought revelation, so Allah revealed that He would collect it in his mind; afterwards he listened, then recited it.
The Prophet prolonged sounds when reciting and recited al-Fath softly in a vibrating tone on his camel; he tells Abu Musa he has a melodious voice like David's family.
The Prophet likes hearing the Quran from others and weeps as Ibn Mas'ud recites an-Nisa; Ibn Shubruma holds three verses the least to recite, and al-Baqarah's last two suffice.
Abdullah bin Amr, fasting daily and finishing the Quran nightly, is told to finish it in a month, then no less than seven days; the Prophet weeps hearing Ibn Mas'ud.
The Prophet foretells people who recite the Quran without it passing their throats and who go out of Islam like an arrow through game; Ali's report says to kill them.
A believer who recites the Quran and acts on it is like a citron, and a hypocrite who recites it is like basil, sweet-smelling but bitter.
Recite the Quran while agreeing on its meaning and stop when you differ; the Prophet tells two men reciting differently both are correct, and says earlier nations perished by differing.
Three men resolve on endless prayer, fasting and celibacy, but the Prophet says he sleeps and marries; Aisha explains the orphan-girl verse; young people who can marry should.
The Prophet had nine wives, giving night turns to eight and going round all in one night; Ibn Abbas urges marriage, as the nation's best had the most wives.
Rewards follow intentions: emigration for Allah and His Apostle counts as such, while emigration for worldly gain or to marry a woman earns only that.
Wifeless men on campaigns are forbidden castration and Uthman bin Maz'un celibacy, temporary marriage is then allowed, Abdur-Rahman marries in Medina, and Abu Huraira is told the pen has dried.
Aisha hints she was the Prophet's only virgin bride, shown to him in dreams; he asks Abu Bakr for her, asks Jabir why not a virgin, and praises Quraysh women.
A man who educates, frees and marries his slave girl gets double reward; a tyrant gave Sara Hajar; the Prophet freed Safiyya and made her freedom her bridal gift.
A man with nothing is married for the Quran he knows, Abu Hudhaifa weds his niece to the freed slave Salim, and a woman should be married for her religion.
The Prophet says that if evil omen exists it is in the woman, the house and the horse, and that he leaves men no trial more severe than women.
Barira, once freed, was given the choice about her slave husband; the Wala goes to the one who frees, and charity given to her became a present for the Prophet.
Foster-suckling forbids what blood relation forbids: the Prophet's foster nieces are unlawful to him, foster uncles may enter, and Uqba must leave his wife after a woman claims nursing both.
Ibn Abbas lists women unlawful by blood and marriage; none may wed two sisters or a woman and her aunt together, nor swap daughters in marriage without bridal gift.
Aisha, after Khaula offers herself and the verse on postponing wives' turns comes, says the Prophet's Lord hastens to please him; Ibn Abbas says the Prophet married in Ihram.
Ali reports the Prophet forbade temporary marriage at Khaibar; Ibn Abbas allowed it in need, it was allowed in an army for three nights, and Ali said it was cancelled.
Women offer themselves to the Prophet in marriage, one praised by Anas; Umar offers Hafsa to Uthman and Abu Bakr; Durra is unlawful to the Prophet as a foster niece.
One may hint, not openly declare, a proposal to a widow in her waiting period; the Prophet saw Aisha in a dream and looked closely at a woman offering herself.
Aisha says the Prophet ended pre-Islamic marriages except asking a guardian for a woman's hand; guardians may not stop orphan girls or a divorced sister marrying, and Umar offers Hafsa.
Aisha says the Prophet married her when she was six and consummated the marriage when she was nine, and she stayed with him nine years.
A matron must be consulted, a virgin's silence is consent; Khansa's marriage against her wish is annulled; the Prophet marries a woman to a man for the Quran he knows.
No man should propose to a woman engaged to his brother or undercut another's bargain, and suspicion and spying are forbidden; Abu Bakr kept secret the Prophet's mention of Hafsa.
After two men from the east give speeches, the Prophet says some eloquent speech has the influence of magic.
After Ar-Rubayyi's wedding the Prophet sits with her while girls beat tambourines mourning her father, killed at Badr, and he stops a line claiming he knows tomorrow.
Abdur-Rahman gives a date-stone's weight of gold as bridal gift, a man is wed for the Quran he knows, and the Prophet says marry even with an iron ring.
The conditions most binding are those of the marriage contract, and a woman may not demand that her would-be husband divorce another wife.
The Prophet blesses Abdur-Rahman and tells him to give a banquet, even of one sheep; he gives one for Zainab, and Ansar women bless Aisha as a bride.
A prophet bars grooms yet to consummate from his campaign; the Prophet consummates with Aisha and Safiyya, tells Jabir he will have Anmat, and notes the Ansar like wedding amusement.
At the Prophet's wedding to Zainab, Um Sulaim's dish feeds batches of guests, and after some linger he recites the verse telling guests to disperse after eating.
When a necklace Aisha borrowed was lost and searchers prayed without ablution, the verse of Tayammum was revealed, and Usaid bin Hudair praises the blessing she brought.
Saying Allah's name and asking protection from Satan when having intercourse with one's wife keeps Satan from harming any child destined from it.
After guests lingered at Zainab's wedding banquet the Hijab verses came; the Prophet's best banquet was one sheep for Zainab, others were of hais or barley.
Wedding invitations must be accepted, Ibn Umar going even when fasting; the worst feast invites only the rich; the Prophet would accept a trotter; Abu Usaid's bride served the guests.
Seeing women and children returning from a wedding, the Prophet rises and tells the Ansar they are the most beloved of all people to him.
The Prophet will not enter where Aisha placed a cushion with pictures, saying picture-makers will be punished and angels do not enter a house with pictures.
At Abu Usaid's wedding his bride alone prepared and served the food and gave the Prophet a drink of dates soaked overnight.
Woman is like a rib that breaks if straightened, so the Prophet urges care for women; Ibn Umar says men spoke freely with their wives only after the Prophet's death.
Everyone is a guardian responsible for his wards: the ruler for his people, a man for his family, a wife for her husband's house, a slave for his master's property.
Eleven women describe their husbands and the Prophet tells Aisha he is to her as Abu Zar to Um Zar; he screens her as she watches Ethiopians play.
Umar names Aisha and Hafsa as the two wives in verse 66:4 and tells of the Prophet's twenty-nine days away from his wives, his bare room, and the option verses.
A wife should not fast voluntarily without her husband's leave when he is home, nor admit anyone without his leave, and angels curse a wife refusing his bed until morning.
The Prophet saw that most in Paradise were the poor and most in the Fire were women, explaining after the eclipse prayer that they were ungrateful to their husbands.
Abdullah bin Amr is told his wife has a right over him, and everyone is a guardian: a man of his family, a wife of her husband's house and children.
The Prophet swore to stay away from his wives for a month, sat in his upper room, and returned after twenty-nine days, saying the month can be twenty-nine days.
Do not flog a wife like a slave then lie with her; Allah curses women lengthening hair artificially, even at a husband's wish; a wife facing divorce may waive rights.
Companions practised coitus interruptus while the Quran was being revealed, including with female captives, and the Prophet says every soul destined to exist will come into existence.
The Prophet drew lots among his wives for journeys, kept turns and died in Aisha's house; a virgin bride gets seven days, a matron three; Umar cautioned Hafsa about Aisha.
A woman asked if she may claim her husband gave her what he had not, to tease his other wife; the Prophet likened this to wearing two garments of falsehood.
None has a greater sense of ghira than Allah, so He forbade illegal sexual intercourse; it is provoked when a believer does what He prohibited, and none loves praise more.
Ghira and jealousy: Zubair's, Umar's, a wife's who broke a co-wife's dish, Aisha's over Khadija; the Prophet refused Ali another wife, since what hurts Fatima hurts him.
Among the portents of the Hour: religious knowledge taken away, ignorance, illegal sexual intercourse and drinking widespread, and women so outnumbering men that one man looks after fifty.
Men must not enter upon women or be alone with one without a mahram, in-laws above all; the Prophet spoke aside with an Ansari woman and barred an effeminate man.
Aisha watched Ethiopians play, screened by the Prophet; women may go out for needs or to the mosque; foster uncles may enter; wives must not describe women to husbands.
Solomon meant to go round a hundred wives to beget fighters in Allah's cause but forgot to say 'If Allah will', and only one bore a child, half a person.
Travellers should not return to their families at night before wives can groom; the Prophet asked newly married Jabir why not a virgin, urging him to seek children.
At Uhud, Fatima washed the blood from the Prophet's face while Ali brought water in his shield, and ash of a burnt palm-leaf mat was put into the wound.
Ibn Abbas, young but close to the Prophet, saw him lead the Eid prayer and sermon, then urge the women to give alms, and they threw their jewellery to Bilal.
Aisha recalls Abu Bakr scolding her and poking her flank while she kept still, as the Prophet's head lay on her thigh.
The Prophet had Ibn Umar, who divorced his wife during menses, take her back until a later purity, then keep or divorce her; that divorce was counted as one.
When Al-Jaun's daughter, brought to the Prophet as a bride, sought refuge with Allah from him, he told her to return to her family, giving her two linen dresses.
A menses divorce counted; Uwaimir divorced thrice after li'an; a thrice-divorced wife returns only after another husband consummates marriage; the option the Prophet gave his wives was no divorce.
Making one's wife unlawful is not divorce; the Prophet's wives played a trick, claiming a bad smell, until he gave up honey, and verses of Surah 66 came down.
Allah forgives the Prophet's followers evil thoughts not acted upon or spoken, and Qatada said a divorce made only in the mind has no effect.
A married man of Bani Aslam confessed illegal sexual intercourse four times; the Prophet asked if he was insane, then had him stoned, caught at Al-Harra when he fled.
Thabit bin Qais's wife, finding no fault in his character or religion yet unable to stay with him, returned his garden, and the Prophet had him divorce her.
The Prophet said Banu Al-Mughira had asked his leave to let Ali marry their daughter, and he gave no leave.
Freed and given the choice, Barira left her slave husband Mughith despite his tears and the Prophet's intercession; wala goes to whoever frees, and alms given her became a gift.
Ibn Umar held marrying a woman who calls Jesus her Lord unlawful; an emigrant woman from warring pagans could marry after one menses; Umar and Iyad divorced wives who remarried.
The Prophet tested believing women who came as emigrants, as Allah ordered, and accepted their pledge of allegiance by word alone, his hand never touching a woman's.
The Prophet ended his oath of abstention from his wives after twenty-nine days; Ibn Umar said after Ila's four months a husband must keep his wife well or divorce her.
Asked about lost property, the Prophet said a stray sheep may be taken, a stray camel left alone, and found money announced for a year before it is kept.
Riding in Tawaf, the Prophet pointed at the Black Stone corner saying Allahu Akbar, and showed with his fingers the opening made in the wall of Gog and Magog.
On Friday there is a moment when a Muslim who is praying and asks Allah for some good is granted it.
Dying, a girl whose head a Jew had crushed for her silver ornaments nodded at his name, and the Prophet had his head crushed between two stones.
Pointing towards the East, the Prophet said afflictions would emerge from there.
Pointing east, the Prophet said a fasting person breaks the fast when night falls from there, and that Bilal's adhan does not mark dawn or stop the pre-dawn meal.
The generous and the miser are like two men in iron cloaks: the generous one's spreads to cover him when he spends, while the miser's rings stick tight.
The Prophet ranked the best Ansar families, Banu An-Najjar first, then Banu Abdil Ash-hal, Banu Al-Harith and Banu Sa'ida, adding there is good in every Ansar family.
Holding up two fingers, the Prophet said his advent and the Hour are as close as these.
With his fingers the Prophet showed that a month is sometimes thirty days and sometimes twenty-nine.
Pointing to Yemen the Prophet said faith is there; towards the East, among Rabi'a and Mudar, are harsh camel-herders heedless of religion, where the two sides of Satan's head appear.
Showing his middle and index fingers, the Prophet said he and the one who looks after an orphan will be like this in Paradise.
When a man said a black child had been born to him, the Prophet, likening it to a grey camel among red ones, said the colour may come from heredity.
Husbands accusing wives of adultery swore li'an with them before the Prophet, who urged repentance and separated them; the mahr was not returned and the child was the mother's.
Rifa'a's divorced wife, remarried to an impotent man, was told she could not return to Rifa'a until the second husband consummated the marriage.
Subai'a al-Aslamiya, widowed while pregnant, was told by the Prophet after giving birth that she could marry, and she did.
Aisha faulted a divorced woman for leaving her husband's house, and rebuked Fatima bint Qais for saying such women get no housing or upkeep, since Fatima left an unsafe place.
Leaving Mecca after Hajj, the Prophet found Safiyya sad at her tent; learning she had done Tawaf al-Ifada on the day of sacrifice, he said she could depart.
Ma'qil, refusing to let his divorced sister remarry her former husband, yielded when verse 2:232 came down; Ibn Umar, who divorced in menses, was ordered to take his wife back.
A woman mourns her husband four months and ten days and anyone else three days at most, without kohl, perfume or dyed clothes; verse 2:240 on widows' residence is explained.
The Prophet forbade the price of a dog, a soothsayer's fee and earnings from prostitution, including a slave girl's, and cursed tattooing, taking or giving riba, and picture-makers.
Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet separated a couple after li'an, saying one of them lies, and told the husband his mahr could not be taken back.
Spending on one's family for Allah's reward is charity, even a morsel for a wife; caring for widows equals jihad; start with dependants; the Prophet stored his family's yearly food.
Umar reminded Ali and Abbas, claiming the Prophet's estate, that what prophets leave is charity, not inheritance, and held them to manage it as the Prophet and Abu Bakr had.
Hind may take from miserly Abu Sufyan's property what is reasonable for her children, and a wife who gives charity from her husband's property unbidden earns him half the reward.
Fatima asked for a servant for her mill-worn hands; the Prophet taught her and Ali to say Subhan Allah and Al-hamdu lillah thirty-three times and Allahu Akbar thirty-four at bedtime.
Aisha said the Prophet worked for his family at home and went out when he heard the adhan.
Hind, whose husband Abu Sufyan gave her too little, was told she may take what suffices her and her children, in a just and reasonable amount.
The best women among camel riders are of Quraysh, the righteous of them kind to their young children and careful of their husbands' property.
Ali wore a silk suit the Prophet gave him, then, seeing anger on his face, cut it up and shared it among his womenfolk.
Jabir, whose father left seven or nine daughters, married a matron rather than a virgin so she could look after them, and the Prophet blessed him.
Unable to free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty poor after intercourse while fasting in Ramadan, a man was given dates as expiation and allowed to keep them.
Umm Salama is rewarded for spending on Abu Salama's children, and Hind may take from miserly Abu Sufyan's property what she and her children reasonably need.
The Prophet left the funeral prayer of debtors who left nothing to others, but after Allah gave him victories he paid believers' debts himself, their wealth going to heirs.
The Prophet declined to marry Umm Habiba's sister, unlawful to him, or Umm Salama's daughter, his foster niece through Thuwaiba, and asked not to be offered daughters and sisters.
Feed the hungry, visit the sick and free captives; Muhammad's family never ate their fill three days running, and the Prophet fed a starving Abu Huraira milk until full.
The Prophet told his stepson Umar bin Abi Salama to say Allah's name, eat with his right hand and from what is nearest; he liked starting from the right.
Abu Talha's few barley loaves, blessed by the Prophet, fed eighty men in tens, and one sheep fed all 130 men with some left over.
The Prophet's household lived on dates and water, near Khaibar only sawiq; he ate no thin bread and not at tables but on leather sheets, as at Safiyya's wedding.
Taunted as son of the woman of two waist-belts, Ibn az-Zubair heard from Asma that she split her belt to tie the Prophet's water skin and food container.
Mastigure meat, not unlawful, was eaten on the Prophet's dining sheet though he disliked it, not being of his people's land; at As-Sahba they ate only sawiq.
Food for two suffices three and for three suffices four; a believer eats in one intestine and a disbeliever in seven; a man ate less after embracing Islam.
The Prophet did not eat while leaning, and withdrew his hand from roasted mastigure, not unlawful but not found in his people's land, while Khalid ate it.
At Itban's house, where the Prophet prayed, he told a man calling Malik a hypocrite that the Fire is forbidden to whoever sincerely testifies that none but Allah deserves worship.
The Prophet drank milk and ate iqt but left the mastigures set on his dining sheet; Sahl's companions relished an old woman's silq and barley dish after Friday prayer.
The Prophet bit meat off a shoulder, stripped the foreleg of Abu Qatada's onager though in Ihram, and cut mutton with a knife, praying afterwards without renewing ablution.
The Prophet never criticised food; they had no white flour or sieves and ate unsifted barley, dates or leaves; his family never ate wheat bread their fill three days running.
When a relative died, Aisha had talbina served to the women, citing the Prophet's saying that talbina soothes the patient's heart and eases some sadness.
Many men reached perfection but among women only Mary, daughter of Imran, and Asia, Pharaoh's wife; Aisha excels other women as tharid excels other food.
The Prophet picked gourd from a tailor's tharid, never saw thin bread or a roasted sheep, Anas said, and cut mutton with a knife, praying without new ablution.
The Prophet barred keeping sacrifice meat beyond three days only in a year of hunger, so the rich would feed the poor; later it was stored and carried to Medina.
Anas, serving the Prophet, often heard him seek refuge from worry and debt; returning from Khaibar he held Safiyya's wedding feast, said Uhud loves us, and declared Medina a sanctuary.
Hudhaifa threw back the cup a Magian brought him, citing the Prophet's ban on silk and on eating or drinking from gold or silver vessels, the unbelievers' in this world.
A believer reciting the Quran is like a citron, one not reciting like a date; a hypocrite reciting is like a fragrant bitter plant, one not reciting like colocynth.
The Prophet said Aisha excels other women as tharid excels other kinds of food.
Travel is a kind of torment, keeping one from sleep and food, so when one's business is done, one should hurry back to one's family.
Three rulings came through Barira: wala goes to whoever frees, once freed she might keep or leave her husband, and charity meat given her was a gift to the Prophet.
The Prophet loved sweets and honey; hungry Abu Huraira sought meals and praised Ja'far's kindness to the poor; the Prophet ate gourd at his slave tailor's house.
When an extra man followed the Prophet to Abu Shu'aib's meal for five, the Prophet left it to the host to admit or refuse him, and he admitted him.
The Prophet picked gourd from a tailor's soup; Aisha said sacrifice meat was kept fifteen days; the family never ate wheat bread with meat their fill three days running.
The Prophet ate fresh dates with cucumber; Abu Huraira's share of dates from him included a hard, unripe one; and when he died, dates and water had sufficed them.
When a Jew refused Jabir more time on a date debt, the Prophet walked the garden and ate there, and the dates plucked repaid the debt with some left over.
The date palm is like a Muslim; seven morning Ajwa dates guard against poison and magic; never two dates at once without leave; the Prophet ate them with cucumber.
Umm Sulaim's porridge from one mudd of barley fed forty men whom the Prophet called in by tens, and Anas looked to see if it had lessened.
Whoever has eaten garlic or onion should keep away from the mosque.
Gathering kabath fruit, the Prophet said the black ones are better, and when asked if he had shepherded sheep, said every prophet had done so.
After eating, the Prophet rinsed his mouth and prayed without new ablution; lick fingers before wiping them; he praised Allah after meals; a servant who cooked should get a share.
Seeing hunger on the Prophet's face, Abu Shu'aib had a meal for five made; when a sixth man followed, the Prophet left it to him, and he admitted the man.
Called to prayer, the Prophet left his mutton and prayed without renewing ablution; when supper is served as the Isha iqama is called, supper comes first, as Ibn Umar did.
Guests lingered after the Prophet's wedding meal for Zainab bint Jahsh; when they left he hung a curtain before Anas, and the verse of Hijab was revealed.
The Prophet put chewed dates in newborns' mouths and blessed them, among them Asma's son Abdullah bin az-Zubair, and named Abu Musa's son Ibrahim and Abu Talha's son Abdullah.
Aqiqa is offered for a newborn boy, with an animal slaughtered and his suffering relieved; Fara' and Atira, the pagans' firstling for idols and the Rajab sheep, are not permitted.
Game killed by a Mi'rad's edge or a trained hound sent with Allah's name may be eaten, not if struck by its side or another dog joined; stone-throwing hunts nothing.
Whoever keeps a dog not for hunting or guarding livestock loses two qirats of reward each day.
Game a trained hound sent with Allah's name catches is lawful unless it ate or other hounds joined; arrow-shot game found days later may be eaten unless in water.
Anas caught a rabbit whose legs the Prophet accepted; Abu Qatada, not in Ihram, killed an onager alone, and the Prophet told companions in Ihram it was food from Allah.
Troops ate a fish the sea cast up, and locusts; People of the Scripture's vessels are used, washed, only if no others exist; domestic donkey meat at Khaibar was discarded.
Any blood-letting tool may slaughter, with Allah's name, except tooth or nail, and a runaway camel may be shot; Zaid bin Amr refused meat slaughtered on stone altars.
Those who slaughtered their sacrifice before the Eid prayer were told to slaughter another; others were to slaughter after it, mentioning Allah's name.
A dying sheep slaughtered with a stone was allowed; any blood-letting tool serves except tooth or nail; meat from recent converts is eaten with Allah's name said over it.
Besieging Khaibar, Abdullah bin Mughaffal went to take a skin of fat thrown down, then, seeing the Prophet behind him, held back out of shyness.
Facing battle without knives, they were told any blood-letting tool serves except tooth or nail and a runaway camel may be shot; Asma's people slaughtered a horse and ate it.
Anas and Ibn Umar, seeing boys shoot at a tied hen, said the Prophet forbade killing tied animals, cursed mutilating a live one, and forbade An-Nuhba.
Abu Musa saw the Prophet eating chicken.
Abu Musa urges a man who swore off chicken to eat it, recalling that the Prophet, having sworn to give no mounts, gave them, doing what is better and expiating.
Donkey meat and Mut'a marriage were forbidden at Khaibar, horse meat allowed, though Ibn Abbas withheld a verdict on donkeys; fanged beasts are forbidden; a dead sheep's hide is usable.
Whoever is wounded in Allah's cause will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound bleeding, its colour that of blood and its smell that of musk.
A good companion is like a musk-carrier, who gives, sells or lets you smell musk; a bad one like a bellows-blower, who burns your clothes or leaves a stench.
The Prophet accepted a rabbit's legs and neither ate nor forbade mastigure, unknown in his land; butter-fat is eaten once a dead mouse and the fat around it are discarded.
Ibn Umar disliked branding animals on the face, as the Prophet forbade striking the face, while Anas saw the Prophet branding a sheep, on its ear he thought.
Without knives, slaughter with anything that makes blood flow, naming Allah, but not tooth or nail; a camel bolting like a wild beast may be stopped with an arrow.
Sacrifice follows the Eid prayer, earlier slaughter being only meat; Abu Burda and Uqba were allowed young animals, and the Prophet sacrificed two rams, and cows for his wives.
On the day of Nahr the Prophet names the four sacred months, declares blood, property and honour sacred, forbids killing one another, and has those present inform the absent.
The Prophet slaughtered at the Musalla and sacrificed two horned black-and-white rams himself; a sacrifice before the Eid prayer is repeated, Abu Burda's young goat sufficing for him only.
The Prophet sent garlanded sacrificial animals to the Ka'bah without avoiding anything lawful; sacrificial meat, banned beyond three days in a hard year, was later allowed to be stored.
Umar relayed the Prophet's ban on fasting the two Eids, Ali his ban on sacrificial meat after three days; at a Friday Eid, Uthman let suburb-dwellers go home before Jumua.
The Prophet said to eat sacrificial meat for three days, so Ibn Umar, leaving Mina, ate bread with oil rather than the meat of the Hadi.
Whoever drinks alcohol unrepentant is denied it hereafter; the Prophet chose milk over wine on his night journey; drinking portends the Hour, and a drinker is no believer while drinking.
Banned alcohol, mostly made from dates, was poured out; Umar said it comes from five things and clouds the mind; all intoxicants are unlawful, though some will deem them lawful.
Abu Usaid's bride soaked dates overnight for the Prophet's drink; he forbade certain drink containers, such as Ad-Dubba', Al-Muzaffat and green jars, then allowed some to those in need.
Any intoxicating drink is unlawful whatever its name, while the Prophet liked sweets and honey; drinks of mixed dates counted as alcohol, and mixing fruits for a drink was forbidden.
The Prophet chose milk on his ascent, drank it at Arafat and from Abu Bakr on leaving Mecca, said to cover it, rinsed after it, and praised lending milch animals.
Abu Talha gave his beloved Bairuha garden, where the Prophet drank, in charity when the verse on spending what one loves came, dividing it among his kin as advised.
The Prophet drank milk mixed with water and passed it to his right, even a boy before elders; he liked sweets and honey, and he and Ali drank water standing.
Anas was serving his uncles a drink of ripe and unripe dates when alcohol was announced prohibited, and they told him to throw it away.
At night cover vessels, tie water-skins and shut doors naming Allah; do not drink from a water-skin's mouth or breathe into the vessel, and the Prophet took three breaths drinking.
Gold and silver vessels, like silk, are for unbelievers here, and drinking in silver fills the belly with Hell Fire; Sahl and Anas kept bowls the Prophet drank from.
At Asr, with only a little water in a vessel, water gushed from the Prophet's fingers and fourteen hundred men made ablution and drank from it.
Every hardship, sickness or thorn-prick expiates a Muslim's sins; the believer bends under trials like a tender plant, and the Prophet suffered double fever for a double reward.
Visit the sick, feed the hungry and free captives, the Prophet ordered; he and Abu Bakr walked to visit the unconscious Jabir, reviving him with his ablution water.
A black woman with epilepsy chose patience and Paradise over a cure, asking only not to be uncovered, and Allah promises Paradise to the patient who loses his sight.
Aisha visited the feverish Abu Bakr and Bilal; the Prophet visited a dying grandchild, a sick bedouin, a Jewish boy who embraced Islam and Sa'd, and was visited when ill.
Patients spoke of their pain: Ka'b's lice, Aisha's headache, the Prophet's high fever, and Sa'd's illness, when the Prophet said giving a third in charity was too much.
On his deathbed the Prophet offered to write a statement against going astray, but those present quarrelled after Umar said the Quran sufficed, and he sent them away.
Brought to the Prophet ill, the boy As-Sa'ib was blessed, drank the water of his ablution and saw the Seal of Prophethood between his shoulders.
None should wish for death over a calamity, but ask to live while life is better; only the ban kept Khabbab from wishing it, and deeds alone earn none Paradise.
Resting against Aisha, the Prophet asked forgiveness, mercy and to join the highest companions; over the sick he asked the Lord of the people for a cure leaving no disease.
The Prophet revived the ill Jabir with his ablution water, and when Jabir, with no son or father to inherit, asked about his estate, the verse of inheritance was revealed.
After the emigration Abu Bakr and Bilal had fever, and the Prophet asked Allah to make Medina loved as Mecca or more, healthy and blessed, moving its fever to Al-Juhfa.
Allah created treatment for every disease; women on expeditions brought back the wounded; healing is in honey, cupping and cautery, which the Prophet disliked; honey cured abdominal trouble.
Sick men sent to drink the Prophet's camels' milk and urine recovered, killed his shepherd and drove off the camels; caught, they had hands and feet cut and eyes branded.
Black cumin heals every disease except death, talbina comforts the sick and grieving, and Indian incense treats seven diseases; the Prophet was cupped, paid the cupper and used snuff.
The Prophet was cupped while fasting and in ihram, on his head, paid the cupper and forbade pressing children's tonsils; Ka'b was told to shave his lice-ridden head and expiate.
Shown the nations, the Prophet was told seventy thousand of his followers will enter Paradise without reckoning: those avoiding Ruqya, omens and cautery who trust their Lord, Ukasha among them.
A widow with sore eyes may not use kohl; the Prophet said she keeps four months and ten days, unlike the former custom of a year in dirty clothes.
There is no 'Adwa, evil omen from birds, Hama or bad omen in Safar, yet one should run from a leper as one runs from a lion.
Truffle water heals the eyes; the Prophet had those who forced medicine into his mouth take it, had seven water-skins poured on him, and prescribed Indian incense and honey.
Told there is no 'Adwa, Safar or Hama, a bedouin asked about mange spreading among his camels, and the Prophet asked who infected the first one.
Indian incense cures seven diseases; Ruqya was allowed for poison and ear ailment; Anas was cauterised; Fatima's ash stopped the Prophet's bleeding; fever, from Hell's heat, is cooled with water.
Men of Ukl and Uraina, given camels' milk and urine to drink, reverted to disbelief, killed the shepherd and took the camels; their eyes were branded and hands cut off.
Do not enter or flee a plague-struck land, as Abdur-Rahman told Umar; plague will not enter Medina, and dying of it or enduring it patiently brings a martyr's reward.
The Prophet blew the Mu'auwidhat over himself when ill; Al-Fatiha recited as Ruqya earned sheep he approved; Ruqya treats the evil eye and stings, invoking the Lord of the people.
A good dream is from Allah and a bad one from Satan; whoever sees one he dislikes should blow thrice and seek refuge with Allah from its evil.
At bedtime the Prophet recited Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas and blew on his palms, wiping his body, as Aisha did for him when ill; Al-Fatiha cured a stung chief.
Seventy thousand of the Prophet's followers will enter Paradise without accounts: those who draw no evil omen, use no cautery or Ruqya and trust their Lord; Ukasha is one.
There is no 'Adwa, Tiyara, Hama or Safar, though an evil omen may be in a woman, house or animal; the best omen is the Fal, a good word.
When a Hudhail woman's stone killed another's unborn child, the Prophet judged a male or female slave as blood money, calling the objecting guardian a brother of soothsayers.
The Prophet forbade money from a dog's price, prostitution and fortune-telling; foretellers are nothing, passing on a word a jinn snatched, mixed with a hundred lies.
Labid bin Al-A'sam worked magic on the Prophet till Allah revealed it lay in Dharwan's well; avoid shirk and witchcraft; some eloquence works like magic; Ajwa dates guard against magic.
The Prophet denied 'Adwa, asking who infected the first mangy camel, yet barred mixing sick cattle with healthy; evil omen is only in horse, woman or house; he liked Fal.
After Khaibar's conquest the Prophet questioned the Jews about a poisoned roasted sheep given him; they admitted poisoning it to learn whether he was a liar or a prophet.
Whoever kills himself by throwing himself from a mountain, by poison or with an iron weapon will go on doing so in the Fire forever.
Seven Ajwa dates guard against magic and poison; fanged beasts are forbidden as food; a fly falling in a vessel is dipped wholly, one wing bearing disease, the other healing.
Allah will not look at one dragging his garment in pride; a proud man sank into the earth; Abu Bakr's slipping Izar was excused; the Prophet once hurried, dragging his.
Rifa'a's irrevocably divorced wife, describing her new husband by her veil's fringe, is told she cannot return to Rifa'a until Abdur-Rahman consummates their marriage.
The Prophet put on his Rida and walked, Zaid and Ali following, to the house where Hamza was, and asked permission to enter.
Asked what a Muhrim wears, the Prophet said no shirt, trousers, hooded cloak or Khuffs, unless he lacks sandals, when he cuts the Khuffs below the ankles.
The Prophet clothed the dead Abdullah bin Ubai in his own shirt and moved to offer his funeral prayer; Umar objected, and a verse then forbade praying over hypocrites.
The Prophet likened the charitable man and the miser to two men in iron cloaks, one widening as he gives and one tightening, showing it at his own shirt's opening.
On a journey the Prophet made ablution in a narrow-sleeved cloak, drawing his arms out from beneath it, and wiped over his Khuffs, worn after ablution.
The Prophet kept a Qaba for Makhrama and took off a silk Farruj after praying in it as unfit for the God-fearing; Anas wore a yellow hooded cloak of Khazz.
A Muhrim does not wear shirts, turbans, trousers, hooded cloaks, clothes touched by saffron or Wars, or Khuffs; lacking sandals he cuts Khuffs short, lacking an Izar he wears trousers.
Allowed to leave Mecca, the Prophet came to Abu Bakr at midday, head covered; Asma tied their food bag with her girdle, and they stayed three nights in Thour's cave.
The Prophet entered Mecca in a helmet, smiled and gave to a bedouin who yanked his Burd, and gave a woman's Burda to a man wanting it as his shroud.
Seventy thousand of the Prophet's followers will enter Paradise without accounts, faces shining like the moon; Ukasha, lifting his sheet, asked to be among them and was prayed for.
Hibra, a Yemeni cloth, was the garment the Prophet loved most, and when he died he was covered with a Hibra Burd.
When his illness worsened the Prophet, covering his face with a Khamisa, cursed the Jews and Christians for taking their prophets' graves as places of worship, warning his followers.
The Prophet sent a patterned Khamisa that distracted him in prayer to Abu Jahm for a plain sheet, and Aisha showed the Kisa and Izar he died wearing.
The Prophet forbade one-garment wraps baring a side or the private parts, and Mulamasa and Munabadha sales; he dressed little Um Khalid in a black Khamisa, wishing her long life.
Rifa'a's divorced wife, her skin bruised green, calls Abdur-Rahman impotent; he denies it, and the Prophet says she cannot return to Rifa'a without consummation, noting the sons resembling him.
On the day of Uhud Sa'd saw two men in white clothes at the Prophet's right and left whom he never saw before or after.
Whoever says none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and dies believing it enters Paradise, even with illegal sexual intercourse and theft, the Prophet repeated to Abu Dharr.
Silk is forbidden beyond two fingers' width; who wears it here will not hereafter; itch excused Az-Zubair and Abdur-Rahman; Ali's silk went to his wives, Umar's to sell or give.
Umar names Aisha and Hafsa as the two wives who backed each other against the Prophet, telling of his warnings and the Prophet's twenty-nine days in his upper room.
One night the Prophet woke exclaiming at afflictions and treasures sent down, asked who would wake the rooms' women, and said many well dressed here will be naked at Resurrection.
The Prophet dressed Um Khalid in a Khamisa, forbade men saffron, wore a red suit, and prayed in shoes; put the right shoe on first, and never walk in one.
People sought the Prophet's leftover ablution water at his red leather tent; he prayed at night within a mat screen, urging steady deeds, and kept a gold-buttoned cloak for Makhrama.
The Prophet forbade gold rings; he threw away the gold ring he had made, saying he would never wear it, and wore a silver ring, its stone silver too.
The Prophet married a woman who offered herself to a man who could not find even an iron ring as Mahr, for the Quran he knew by heart.
A silver ring the Prophet had engraved 'Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah' sealed his letters, and Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman wore it until it fell into Aris well.
After the Eid prayer, offered before the sermon, the Prophet went to the women and told them to give alms, and they put their rings in Bilal's garment.
On Eid the Prophet prayed two rak'at with no prayer before or after, then went to the women and ordered alms, and they gave their earrings and necklaces.
When a necklace Aisha had borrowed from Asma was lost, the men searching for it prayed without ablution for lack of water, and Allah revealed the verse of Tayammum.
On Eid day the Prophet prayed two rak'at with no optional prayer before or after, then went with Bilal to the women and ordered alms, and they gave their earrings.
In a Medina market the Prophet called for little Al-Hasan, who came wearing a bead necklace; he embraced him and asked Allah to love him and those who love him.
The Prophet cursed men who take on women's manners and women who take on men's, had such people turned out of houses, and barred an effeminate man from his wives.
The Fitra's practices are circumcision, shaving pubic hair, clipping nails, removing armpit hair and cutting moustaches short, while the beard is kept, unlike the pagans.
The Prophet had too few grey hairs to dye; Um Salama kept some of his reddish dyed hair; Jews and Christians do not dye, so do otherwise.
Handsome in a red cloak, the Prophet was neither tall nor short, his hair neither curly nor straight; sent at forty, he died at sixty with barely ten white hairs.
In a dream near the Ka'ba the Prophet saw the Messiah son of Mary, his combed hair dripping, circling it, then the curly-haired Dajjal, blind in the right eye.
The Prophet's wavy hair hung to his shoulders or just above, and he had big hands and feet, soft palms and a good-looking face, unlike anyone else.
Ibn Abbas had not heard the Prophet say 'Kafir' is written between the Dajjal's eyes, but heard him liken Abraham to himself and describe brown, curly-haired Moses saying Labbaik.
Umar said whoever braids his hair should shave it on leaving Ihram; the Prophet, his hair gummed, said the Talbiya, and having garlanded his Hadi kept Ihram until slaughtering it.
The Prophet first let his hair hang down like the people of the Scripture, not parted like the pagans', then parted it; Aisha recalled its parting shining in Ihram.
Staying at Maimuna's, Ibn Abbas stood on the Prophet's left in the night prayer, and the Prophet took him by his locks of hair and moved him to his right.
The Prophet forbade Al-Qaza', shaving a boy's head while leaving tufts of hair here and there, as Nafi' explained.
Aisha perfumed the Prophet with her own hands for Ihram and at Mina before Tawaf al-Ifada, with the best scent, until its shine showed on his head and beard.
A man peeped through a hole as the Prophet combed his head; had he known, the Prophet said, he would have pierced his eye, as asking permission prevents unlawful looking.
Aisha combed the Prophet's hair during her periods, and he liked to start from the right in combing and in ablution.
Allah says fasting is for Him and He rewards it, and the smell of a fasting person's mouth is better to Allah than musk.
Aisha perfumed the Prophet with the best scent before Ihram, and with Dharira at the Farewell Hajj on entering and leaving it, and he never refused a gift of scent.
Allah cursed women who tattoo, remove facial hair, gap their teeth or add false hair, or have it done, false hair being refused even for a bride who lost hers.
The Prophet forbade tattooing and cursed women who tattoo, are tattooed or lengthen hair, as he forbade usury and the price of blood or a dog; Umar asked about it.
Angels do not enter a house with a dog or pictures; picture-makers face the severest punishment and must give life to their work, and the Prophet tore Aisha's pictured curtain.
Aisha added that she and the Prophet used to bathe from one container.
Seeing Aisha's pictured cushion the Prophet would not enter, saying picture-makers must give life to their work and angels avoid such houses, though a design on a garment is excepted.
The Prophet shared his mount: Usama rode behind him on a donkey, and at Mecca he took boys of Bani Abdul Muttalib, Qutham and Al-Fadl, one before and one behind.
Riding behind the Prophet, Mu'adh was told that Allah's right on His slaves is that they worship Him alone, and theirs on Him is that He will not punish them.
Coming from Khaibar, the camel carrying the Prophet and a wife slipped; Anas resaddled it, and nearing Medina the Prophet said they return repentant, worshipping and praising their Lord.
Abbad's uncle saw the Prophet lying down in the mosque with one leg placed over the other.
Dutifulness to parents, mother first, is among the best deeds, serving them a jihad; cursing them is a great sin, and a cave-trapped man invoked his care for them.
The greatest sins are joining partners with Allah, undutifulness to parents and killing a soul, and the Prophet warned repeatedly against a forged statement or false witness.
Asma asked whether she might be kind to her pagan mother, who came during the peace pact hoping for her favour, and the Prophet said yes.
Keeping ties of kinship leads to Paradise, more wealth and longer life, and severing them bars Paradise; the womb sought Allah's refuge, and the true keeper restores ties others cut.
The Prophet let little Um Khalid play with his Prophethood seal, called Hasan and Husain his flowers, carried Umamah in prayer and kissed Al-Hasan; well-treated daughters shield from Fire.
Allah is more merciful to His slaves than a captive mother to her child, and of mercy's hundred parts He sent one to earth, by which creatures show mercy.
The greatest sins are setting up a rival to Allah, killing one's son lest he share one's food, and illegal intercourse with a neighbour's wife, and a verse confirmed it.
A child the Prophet gave Tahnik urinated on him, and he poured water over it; he held Usama and Al-Hasan on his thighs and prayed for mercy on them.
Aisha was jealous of no woman as of Khadija, for the Prophet often mentioned her, was told to promise her a palace in Paradise, and sent meat to her friends.
The Prophet said he and the one who looks after an orphan will be in Paradise like his two joined fingers.
One who looks after and works for a widow and a poor person is like a fighter in Allah's Cause, or one who fasts by day and prays all night.
Sensing young men staying twenty nights missed their families, the kind-hearted Prophet sent them home to teach them, pray as he prayed, give the Adhan and let the eldest lead.
A thirsty man who went down a well again to water a panting dog was forgiven by Allah, and there is reward for serving any living being.
A bedouin who prayed for mercy on himself and Muhammad alone was told by the Prophet that he had narrowed something vast, meaning Allah's Mercy.
Believers in their mercy, love and kindness to one another are like one body: when one part is ill, the whole body shares its sleeplessness and fever.
If a Muslim plants something and a person or an animal eats of it, he is rewarded as if he had given it in charity.
Whoever is not merciful to others will not be treated mercifully, the Prophet said.
Gabriel urged kindness to neighbours till the Prophet thought they would inherit; one whose neighbour fears his harm lacks faith; gifts go to the nearest door, and guests are honoured.
Every Muslim owes charity, by working, helping the distressed, enjoining good or refraining from evil, and the Fire is warded off even with half a date or a kind word.
When Jews wished the Prophet death and Aisha cursed them, he said Allah loves kindness in all matters; he let a bedouin urinating in the mosque finish.
A believer to a believer is like a building whose parts support each other, and the Prophet told them to help and recommend the needy for a reward.
The Prophet, brave and generous, never spoke obscenely or refused requests, urged Aisha to gentleness and was polite to a man he called evil; the best have the best character.
The Prophet said time will pass quickly, good deeds will decrease, miserliness will be cast into hearts, and Harj, meaning killing, will increase.
Anas served the Prophet ten years without ever hearing a word of impatience or blame, and at home the Prophet served his family until prayer time.
When Allah loves someone, Gabriel and heaven love him and earth accepts him; faith's sweetness lies in loving others for Allah's sake and holding Allah and His Apostle dearest.
The Prophet forbade laughing at someone who passes wind, and asked how a man can beat his wife like a stallion camel and then embrace her.
A Muslim's blood, property and honour are sacred; abusing him is evil-doing, cursing him like murder, and calling him a disbeliever falsely rebounds; the Prophet himself never abused anyone.
When two men abused each other and one's face swelled with anger, the Prophet said seeking refuge with Allah from Satan would calm him, but the man refused.
The Prophet came to tell the date of the Night of Qadr, but two men quarrelled and its knowledge was taken away; seek it on the ninth, seventh or fifth.
Told that insulting a man's mother showed traits of ignorance, Abu Dhar dressed his slave as himself, for slaves are brothers to be fed and clothed as oneself.
After the Prophet ended Zuhr at two rak'at, Dhul-Yadain, the long-armed, asked if he forgot; when the people confirmed it, he prayed two more and two prostrations of forgetfulness.
Passing two graves, the Prophet said one man was punished for not guarding against his urine and the other for spreading calumnies, and planted a split palm leaf on each.
The Prophet said the best family among the Ansar is the Banu An-Najjar.
The Prophet called a man evil before admitting him, then spoke to him politely, saying the worst people are those others avoid for fear of their foul tongue or wrongdoing.
In Medina's graveyard the Prophet heard two people punished in their graves, one for urine and one for calumnies, and placed half a green palm leaf on each grave.
The Prophet said a Qattat will not enter Paradise.
Whoever does not give up false statements, evil deeds and bad words, Allah has no need of his leaving food and drink in fasting.
The worst people before Allah on Resurrection Day are the double-faced, who show one face to some people and another face to others.
Told that an Ansari said a distribution was not meant to please Allah, the Prophet's face changed with anger, and he said Moses was hurt worse yet stayed patient.
The Prophet rebuked men who over-praised another, saying they had cut his back or neck; one who must praise should say 'I think', for none can sanctify anyone before Allah.
Abu Bakr said his waist sheet slackened on one side, and the Prophet said he was not among those who drag their garments out of pride.
Lubaid bin Asam worked magic on the Prophet with a comb and hair hidden in Dharwan's well; Allah revealed it and cured him, and he would not spread the evil.
Beware of suspicion, the worst of false tales; do not spy, seek faults, be jealous, hate or desert one another beyond three days, but be brothers, O Allah's worshippers.
The Prophet told Aisha he did not think two certain men knew anything of their religion, and Al-Laith said the two were hypocrites.
All sins are forgiven except those whose doers expose what Allah screened, and on the Day Allah will make a believer confess his sins, then forgive what He had screened.
The people of Paradise are the obscure and humble, whose oaths by Allah He fulfils, and the people of the Fire are the cruel, violent, proud and conceited.
Any slave girl of Medina could take the Prophet by the hand and lead him wherever she wished, Anas said.
Aisha broke her vow never to speak to Ibn Az-Zubair, freeing forty slaves, as a Muslim may not desert his brother over three nights; the better greets first.
The Prophet knew Aisha's moods: pleased, she swore by the Lord of Muhammad, and angry, by the Lord of Abraham, leaving only his name, she said.
The Prophet visited Abu Bakr's house morning and evening, and one day came at noon to say he had been allowed to migrate.
The Prophet ate with an Ansari household, prayed in their house on a mat sprinkled with water, and invoked Allah's blessing on his hosts.
Umar urged the Prophet to buy a silk cloak for delegations; he said silk is worn by one with no share hereafter, then sent Umar a cloak only to sell.
The Prophet made Abdur-Rahman and Sa'd bin Ar-Rabi' brothers, told Abdur-Rahman to give a wedding feast, and made a brotherhood pact between the Ansar and Quraish in Anas's home.
The Prophet smiled rather than laughing aloud: at Rifa'a's divorced wife, women hiding from Umar, a poor man's Ramadan offence, a rough bedouin, Jarir, and rain prayers.
Truthfulness leads to righteousness and Paradise, and lying to wickedness and the Fire, until a man is written before Allah as truthful or as a liar.
The signs of a hypocrite are three: he lies when he speaks, breaks his promises, and betrays what he is entrusted with.
In a dream the Prophet was shown a man whose cheek was being torn, a liar whose lies spread over the world, punished so until the Day of Resurrection.
Hudhaifa said Ibn Um Abd most resembled the Prophet in bearing, piety and calm from leaving his house till returning, though none knew him alone with his family.
Abdullah said the best talk is Allah's Book and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad.
None is more patient than Allah with those ascribing children to Him, yet He provides for them; angered by an Ansari's remark, the Prophet recalled Moses, harmed worse yet patient.
The Prophet censured people who avoided something he did and allowed, saying he knew Allah better than they and feared Him more.
The Prophet was shyer than a virgin in her room, and when he disliked something it showed on his face.
Calling one's brother a disbeliever makes one of them so; cursing a believer or calling him a disbeliever is like killing him, and suicide is punished by its own means.
When Mu'adh called a man a hypocrite for leaving his long Surat al-Baqara prayer, the Prophet rebuked Mu'adh for burdening people and told him to recite shorter surahs.
One who swears by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza must say none is worshipped but Allah, one proposing to gamble must give charity, and swearing by one's father is forbidden.
The Prophet showed anger at a pictured curtain, over-long prayers, a lost-camel question and insistence on night prayer, and disgust at spittle toward the Qibla; the strong control their anger.
Haya, pious shyness, brings only good and is part of faith; the Prophet was shyer than a veiled virgin, yet Allah is not shy of the truth.
The Prophet told those sent to Yemen to make things easy and not repel people, chose the easier way unless sinful, and said they were sent to make things easy.
The Prophet joked with young Abu Umair about his bird, called back Aisha's playmates at dolls, spoke gently to a man he called evil, and saved Makhrama a cloak.
The Prophet said a believer is not stung twice from the same hole.
Told not to pray all night and fast every day, since body, eyes, guest and wife have rights, Abdullah bin Amr pressed until allowed David's fast of alternate days.
A guest is owed a day and night's best food and three days' hospitality, without overburdening his host; Salman would not eat alone, nor Abu Bakr's guests without him.
When Abdullah bin Sahl was murdered at Khaibar, the Prophet let the elder speak first, offered fifty oaths, and paid the blood money himself when they refused the Jews' oaths.
Asked which tree is like a Muslim, Ibn Umar thought of the date palm but kept silent before Abu Bakr and Umar, and his father wished he had spoken.
Some poetry holds wisdom: the Prophet quoted verse when his toe bled, called Labid's line the truest, and prayed for mercy on Amir, who chanted verse marching to Khaibar.
The Prophet told Anjasha to drive slowly the camels of his wives and Um Sulaim, as they carried glass vessels, a phrase Abu Qalaba said others would be blamed for.
Hassan was allowed to lampoon the pagans in verse, with Gabriel's support; Ibn Rawaha's verse praised the Prophet; yet a belly full of pus beats one full of poetry.
Aisha was told to admit the brother of Abu Al-Qu'ais as her uncle, since Abu Al-Qu'ais's wife had nursed her, for foster relations forbid what blood relations forbid.
Leaving after Hajj, the Prophet found Safiya sad with her menses and exclaimed 'Aqra Halqa', but since she had done Tawaf al-Ifada she could leave with them.
In the Conquest year Um Hani found the Prophet bathing, screened by Fatima; he welcomed her, prayed eight rak'at, and honoured her shelter of a man her brother would kill.
Seeing a man driving a sacrificial camel, the Prophet told him to ride it, and when he protested it was a Badana, said 'Ride it, woe to you'.
On a journey the Prophet told his black slave Anjasha, driving fast the camels women rode, to drive slowly with the glass vessels.
When a man praised another, the Prophet said thrice that he had cut his brother's neck; one who must praise should say 'I think', for none sanctifies anyone before Allah.
Told by Dhul Khawaisira to act justly, the Prophet foretold seemingly devout men who would leave Islam like an arrow, marked by a deformed-handed man found among those Ali fought.
A man who had intercourse while fasting in Ramadan could not free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty, so the smiling Prophet gave him dates to keep.
A bedouin asking about emigration was told it is hard, but since he paid Zakat on his camels, he could carry on from beyond the seas, losing no deed.
The Prophet, saying 'woe to you' or 'may Allah be merciful to you', told them not to become disbelievers after him by cutting one another's necks.
Asked when the Hour will come, the Prophet asked what was prepared, and hearing only love of Allah and His Apostle, said everyone will be with those he loves.
The Prophet tested the boy Ibn Saiyad, who answered 'Ad-Dukh', refused Umar leave to kill him, tried to overhear him, and warned that the Dajjal is one-eyed, unlike Allah.
Welcoming the Abdul Qais delegation, the Prophet ordered them to pray, pay Zakat, fast Ramadan and give a fifth of booty, and forbade four kinds of drinking vessels.
On the Day of Resurrection a flag will be raised for every betrayer, and it will be announced that this is the betrayal of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.
Say 'Laqisat Nafsi' rather than 'Khabuthat Nafsi'; do not abuse Time, for Allah is Time, nor call grapes Al-Karm, since Al-Karm is a believer's heart.
Ali never heard the Prophet say 'Let my father and mother be sacrificed for you' to anyone but Sa'd, as he shot arrows, perhaps at Uhud.
When the she-camel slipped and the Prophet and Safiya fell, Abu Talha covered her, and nearing Medina the Prophet kept saying they return repentant, worshipping and praising their Lord.
People may take the Prophet's name but not his kunya Abu-l-Qasim; a father was told to name his son Abdur-Rahman; the Prophet renamed Al-Mundhir and Zainab, but Hazn refused Sahl.
Ibn Abi Aufa said the Prophet's son Ibrahim died young, as there is no prophet after Muhammad, and the Prophet said Ibrahim has a wet nurse in Paradise.
Take the Prophet's name but not his kunya, for he is Al-Qasim who distributes Allah's blessings; Satan cannot take his form in dreams, and he named Abu Musa's son Ibrahim.
The sun eclipsed on the day the Prophet's son Ibrahim died, Al-Mughira said.
Rising from bowing, the Prophet asked Allah to save Al-Walid bin Al-Walid, Salama bin Hisham, Aiyyash and the weak believers of Mecca, and to send Mudar years like Joseph's.
The Prophet told Aisha that Gabriel was sending her greetings, and she returned them, adding that he saw things they did not see.
With Um Sulaim among the women in charge of the luggage, the Prophet told Anjash, his slave driving their camels fast, to drive slowly with the glass vessels.
