The Prophet, best in character, would ask Anas's little brother about his pet bird, and at prayer time in their house led them in prayer on a swept, sprinkled carpet.
Ali loved the name Abu Turab, first given by the Prophet when he found him, angry with Fatima, sleeping by the mosque wall, and wiped dust from his back.
The most awful name in Allah's sight on the Day of Resurrection is that of a man calling himself King of Kings, which some said means Shahan Shah.
Visiting sick Sa'd before Badr, the Prophet preached to a mixed gathering, was rebuffed by Abdullah bin Ubai and excused him, as Muslims then forgave pagans and Scripture people.
Asked whether he had helped his protector Abu Talib, the Prophet said yes: he is in a shallow place of Fire, and would otherwise be in its lowest depth.
On a journey the Prophet told Anjasha, whose chanting drove the camels fast, to drive slowly and not break the glass vessels, meaning the women.
When fear spread in Medina, the Prophet rode Abu Talha's horse and said they saw nothing, but found the horse like a sea.
Asked about fore-tellers, the Prophet said they are nothing: a true word is one stolen and poured into the fore-teller's ear, to which he adds a hundred lies.
After a pause in revelation, the Prophet heard a voice and saw the angel of the cave of Hira sitting on a chair between sky and earth.
At night in Maimuna's house the Prophet rose, looked at the sky and recited that the creation of heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day hold signs.
In a Medina garden the Prophet had Abu Musa open the gate with glad tidings of Paradise for Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, the last along with a coming calamity.
Scraping the ground with a stick, the Prophet said everyone's place in Paradise or the Fire is assigned, yet told them to act, as each is eased toward his place.
Waking at night, the Prophet exclaimed at treasures and afflictions sent down, asked who would wake his wives, and warned the well-dressed may be naked hereafter; Umar said Allahu Akbar.
Walking Safiya home from his I'tikaf, the Prophet told two Ansari men who she was, as Satan runs in man like blood and might put evil thoughts in their hearts.
The Prophet forbade flicking stones with the fingers, which neither hunts game nor hurts an enemy but gouges out an eye or breaks a tooth.
A sneezer who praises Allah is answered 'May Allah have mercy on you' and replies with a prayer; yawning is from Satan and should be stopped; Al-Bara lists seven duties.
Allah created Adam in His picture, sixty cubits tall, and had him greet the angels, whose reply became his offspring's greeting; all entering Paradise will have Adam's form.
The Prophet turned Al-Fadl's face from a Khath'am woman asking about Hajj for her father, and told those sitting on roads to lower their gaze, harm none and return greetings.
Allah is As-Salam; the young, the rider, the walker and the smaller group greet first; spread the greeting to known and unknown, and the better of two estranged greets first.
Guests lingering after the Prophet's wedding meal for Zainab bint Jahsh brought the verse of Al-Hijab and a screen; Umar's urging over Sauda preceded the verse veiling the Prophet's wives.
A man peeped into the Prophet's room, and the Prophet said he would have pierced his eye, for asking permission to enter was ordained because of looking.
Allah has written each son of Adam's share of adultery: the eyes' is looking, the tongue's is talk, the self desires, and the private parts confirm or deny it.
The Prophet greeted and repeated words three times; whoever asks permission thrice unanswered should leave, as Abu Musa proved to Umar, and the people of Suffa asked before entering.
Anas greeted boys as the Prophet did, the companions greeted an old woman who fed them after the Friday prayer, and Gabriel sent his greeting to Aisha.
When Jabir knocked and answered 'I' to the Prophet's 'Who is that?', the Prophet repeated 'I, I?' as if he disliked it.
A man who prayed improperly greeted the Prophet, who returned his greeting and sent him back to pray, then taught him to recite, bow, prostrate and sit with calmness.

Aisha returned Gabriel's greeting; the Prophet greeted a mixed gathering including Abdullah bin Ubai; Ka'b doubted his greeting was returned during the boycott; Jews' greetings are answered 'And on you'.
Hatib's letter to Mecca's pagans was seized and the Prophet accepted his excuse; the letter to Heraclius wished peace on whoever follows guidance; an Israelite sent money with a letter.
The Prophet told the people to stand for Sa'd, whose verdict on Qurayzah, that their warriors be killed and their women and children taken captive, he called Allah's judgement.
The companions shook hands, the Prophet was seen holding Umar's hand, and Ibn Mas'ud learned the tashahhud with his hand between the Prophet's hands.
During the Prophet's fatal illness Al-Abbas, foreseeing his death, urged Ali to ask him who would rule after him, but Ali refused to ask.
Allah's right is to be worshipped alone, and His slaves' right is not to be punished; Gabriel said whoever dies without associating others enters Paradise, even after adultery and theft.
No one should make another get up from his seat in order to sit there; people should make room instead.
Guests stayed talking after the Prophet's wedding meal for Zainab bint Jahsh; when they left he dropped a curtain before Anas, and the verse against entering his houses unbidden came.
Ibn Umar saw the Prophet sitting in the courtyard of the Ka'bah in the ihtiba posture, his hand round his legs.
The biggest of the great sins are associating others with Allah and undutifulness to parents, and the Prophet sat up from reclining to warn repeatedly against false statement.
The Prophet once hurried home after the Asr prayer, and he prayed in the middle of his bed while Aisha lay before him and slipped quietly away.
Sitting on the floor beside a cushion, the Prophet raised Abdullah bin Amr's fasting from three to eleven days a month, saying none is better than David's alternate-day fast.
Abu Ad-Darda' asked Alqama of Kufa about its distinguished companions and how Ibn Mas'ud recited Sura 92, upholding 'and by male and female' as heard from the Prophet.
The companions took their midday nap and their meals after the Friday prayer.
Finding Ali asleep and dusty in the mosque after a quarrel with Fatima, the Prophet wiped him and called him Abu Turab, the name Ali loved most.
Um Sulaim spread a leather sheet for the Prophet's midday nap and mixed his sweat and hair into perfume, some of which Anas had added to his embalming perfume.
Napping at Um Haram's, the Prophet woke smiling, shown followers sailing the sea to fight in Allah's Cause like kings on thrones, and said she would be among the first.
The Prophet forbade two ways of wearing a garment, Ishtimal As-Samma and Ihtiba leaving the private parts uncovered, and two bargains, Mulamasa and Munabadha.
Fatima wept when the Prophet confided that his death was near and laughed when told she would be chief of the believing women, telling Aisha only after his death.
The Prophet was seen lying on his back in the mosque with one leg over the other.
Two should not talk secretly apart from a third; Anas kept the Prophet's secret, Ibn Mas'ud secretly reported an angering remark, and one man's private talk outlasted the iqama.
At bedtime put out fires and lamps, close the doors and cover vessels and food, for fire burnt a house in Medina and a rat may drag a wick.
Five things are of the fitra, circumcision among them; Abraham circumcised himself past eighty, and Ibn Abbas was already circumcised when the Prophet died, boys then being circumcised at puberty.
Whoever swears by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza should say none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, and whoever invites a friend to gamble should give something in charity.
Ibn Umar built a house with his own hands in the Prophet's lifetime and said he built and planted nothing after the Prophet died, though a relative disputed it.
Every prophet has one invocation that is answered, and the Prophet keeps his to intercede for his followers on the Day of Resurrection.
The best plea for forgiveness, said with faith, brings Paradise to one dying that day or night; the Prophet repented over seventy times daily, and Allah rejoices greatly at repentance.
At bedtime the Prophet lay on his right side with words of surrender, recited the Mu'awwidhat and taught glorifications, and when praying at night asked for light and forgiveness.
In the last third of every night the Lord descends to the nearest heaven, asking who will invoke Him, ask Him or seek His forgiveness, that He may answer.
On going to the lavatory the Prophet sought refuge with Allah from al-khubuth and al-khaba'ith.
The Prophet gave the best plea for forgiveness, said 'In Your name I die and live' at bedtime and taught prayer invocations; invocation should be neither loud nor low.
The poor were told glorifying, praising and magnifying Allah ten times each after every prayer would match the rich, and the Prophet declared Allah's oneness after each prayer.
The Prophet invoked mercy and blessing on Amir at Khaibar, those bringing alms, Jarir sent against Dhul-Khalasa, Anas, a reciter who reminded him of a verse, and Moses.
Avoid rhymed prose in invocation and preach sparingly; ask Allah with determination, not 'if You wish', without growing impatient; the Prophet raised his hands until his armpits showed.
Asked in a Friday sermon, the Prophet invoked rain, then after a week's downpour asked that it fall around them; praying for rain at the Musalla, he turned his cloak.
The Prophet prayed for Anas's wealth and children, declared Allah's oneness, Lord of the Throne, in distress, and sought refuge from calamity, an evil end and enemies' gloating.
No prophet dies before being shown his place in Paradise and given the choice, and the Prophet's last words, his head on Aisha's thigh, were 'O Allah, the Highest Companions'.
Khabbab, branded seven times, would have prayed for death but for the Prophet's ban; none should long for death over a calamity but ask to live while life is better.

The Prophet blessed children, stroking As-Sa'ib's head, pouring water on an infant's urine, spraying Mahmud's face, touching another's eye; men sought partnership with Abdullah bin Hisham, whom he blessed.
Asked how to send Salat on him, the Prophet taught 'O Allah, send Salat on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham's family', and invoked Salat on those bringing alms.
The Prophet asked Allah to make any abuse of his against a believer a means of bringing that believer near to Him on the Day of Resurrection.
Angered by many questions, the Prophet offered to answer any; a man learned his father was Hudhaifa, Umar sought refuge from afflictions, and Paradise and Hell were shown to him.

The Prophet sought refuge from worry, grief, incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, debt, old age, worldly affliction and the grave's punishment, which he confirmed after Aisha doubted two Jewish women.
The Prophet asked Allah to make them love Medina as much as Mecca or more, move its fever to Al-Juhfa, and bless their measures.
Gravely ill, Sa'd was told even a third in charity is too much, since leaving heirs rich is better, and the Prophet prayed his companions' emigration be completed.
The Prophet sought refuge from cowardice, miserliness, old age, the trial and punishment of grave and Fire, poverty, wealth and the Dajjal, asking that his sins be washed away.
Um Sulaim asked the Prophet to invoke blessing for Anas, his servant, and he asked Allah to increase his wealth and offspring and bless what He gave him.
The Prophet taught the Istikhara: two voluntary rak'at, then asking Allah by His knowledge and power to decree a matter if good and turn it away if bad.
After ablution the Prophet raised his hands and asked Allah to forgive Ubaid Abi Amir and raise him above many on the Day of Resurrection.
Shouting Takbir is needless, for Allah hears and sees; 'La haula wala quwwata illa billah' is a treasure of Paradise; the Prophet praised Allah on heights and returning from journeys.
The Prophet invoked blessing on the marriages of Abdur-Rahman bin Auf and Jabir, and taught a husband words seeking protection from Satan before intercourse, protecting any child conceived.
The Prophet's most frequent invocation asked for good in this world and the Hereafter and safety from the Fire; he taught refuge from miserliness, cowardice, old age and worldly affliction.
Bewitched by Labid bin Al-A'sam so he thought he had done what he had not, the Prophet invoked Allah, learned from two men where the spell lay, and was cured.
The Prophet invoked against the confederates, Mudar, Usaiya and those who made him miss Asr at the Trench, returned the Jews' greeting in kind, but prayed for Daus's guidance.
The Prophet asked Allah to forgive his mistakes, ignorance and excess, his jest and earnest, what he did deliberately or not, past and future, secret and open.
On Friday there is a brief time when Allah grants whatever good a Muslim who is praying asks of Him.
When Jews wished the Prophet death and Aisha cursed them, he urged gentleness, saying he had returned their words and his invocation against them is accepted, theirs not.
When the imam says Amin all should say it, for whoever's Amin coincides with the angels' has his past sins forgiven.
Declaring Allah's oneness a hundred times, or Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi, brings great reward; angels seek those remembering Allah, whom He forgives, and 'La haula' is a treasure of Paradise.
Allah has ninety-nine Names, and whoever believes in their meanings and acts on them will enter Paradise; Allah is witr and loves the odd.
Ibn Mas'ud explained that he did not come out to preach every day because the Prophet preached to them at intervals so they would not be bored.
Many are cheated of health and free time; true life is the Hereafter's; live as a stranger; hope outruns one's term, while love of wealth and long life grows.
Mahmud recalls the Prophet spraying water on his face, and Utban relates that Allah forbids the Fire to whoever says 'La ilaha illallah' sincerely, seeking Allah's pleasure.
Allah says His only reward for a believer who stays patient when a dear one dies is Paradise.
The Prophet feared not his people's poverty but worldly wealth pouring in and their competing for it; wealth is sweet, a good helper if earned lawfully and spent rightly.
The best people are the Prophet's generation and those after them; later will come people who testify unasked, betray, break vows and grow fat.
Khabbab said companions who died took none of their reward in this world, while those after them gathered wealth they could spend only on building.
Uthman performed ablution as the Prophet did, who said such ablution followed by two rak'at in the mosque forgives past sins, but warned against being conceited about it.
The righteous will pass away one after another until worthless people remain, like husks of barley or bad dates.
Perish the slave of money and clothes; man would want a third valley of gold; true wealth is a content soul; the rich have little reward unless they give.
A poor Muslim is better than an earthful of nobles, most in Paradise are poor, and the Prophet's household and companions often went hungry, living on dates and water.
The deeds most loved are regular ones even if few; act moderately within your ability, for deeds alone admit none to Paradise, not even the Prophet, without Allah's mercy.
After leading the prayer, the Prophet said Paradise and Hell had been shown to him towards the mosque wall, the best and worst things he had ever seen.
Allah made mercy in a hundred parts, sending one to creation; knowing all His mercy, a disbeliever would not despair, and knowing His punishment, a believer would not feel safe.
Having given all he had to the Ansar, the Prophet said Allah makes content whoever refrains from begging and gives patience to the patient, the best gift of all.
The Prophet prayed until his feet swelled, and asked why, he replied by asking whether he should not be a thankful slave.
Seventy thousand of the Prophet's followers will enter Paradise without accounts: those who do not practise ruqya or see evil omens, and who trust in their Lord.
Idle talk and excessive questioning were forbidden; guarding tongue and private parts earns Paradise; speak good or keep silent, harm no neighbour, honour guests; one word can raise or ruin.
Allah will shade one who remembers Him with tears, and He forgave a man who, fearing Him, had his family burn his body and scatter his ashes.
The Prophet likened himself to a warner of an approaching army whom some believed and were saved, and to a man holding back moths rushing into a fire.
A Muslim is one from whose tongue and hands Muslims are safe, and an emigrant is one who abandons what Allah has forbidden.
The Prophet said that if they knew what he knows, they would laugh little and weep much.
The Fire is surrounded by desires and Paradise by disliked things, and each is nearer to a person than the strap of his shoe.
The truest verse a poet ever said is that everything except Allah is perishable.
Whoever looks at someone given more property and better appearance should also look at someone below him.
Allah writes an intended good deed as one, a done one tenfold to seven hundredfold, an evil done as one; Anas said sins now thought trivial were once deemed destructive.
A brave fighter the Prophet called one of the Fire's people killed himself; one may seem to do Paradise's or Hell's deeds, but results depend on the last deeds.
The best people strive in Allah's Cause or worship alone in a mountain pass sparing others harm; a Muslim will flee with his sheep to save his religion from afflictions.
When honesty is lost, await the Hour; honesty will leave hearts until the trustworthy are rare, and people are like camels, hardly one in a hundred fit to ride.
Whoever makes his good deeds heard or seen to win people's praise, Allah will expose his real intention.
Riding behind the Prophet, Mu'adh was told that Allah's right on His slaves is to be worshipped alone, and their right on Him is not to be punished.
When a bedouin's camel outran the Prophet's swift she-camel Al-Adba, he said Allah lowers whatever is raised high in this world.
Allah declares war on whoever is hostile to His pious worshipper, who draws near through obligations, then extra deeds, until loved, and Allah becomes his hearing, sight, hand and leg.
The Hour is as close to the Prophet's sending as two fingers; it comes after the sun rises in the west, so suddenly that bargains and meals go unfinished.
Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him; the dying believer, given good news, longs for that meeting, while the disbeliever, told of torment, dreads it.
Shown his place in Paradise and given the choice, the dying Prophet wiped his face with water, said death has stupors, and chose the highest companions with his last words.
The bedouins' Hour meant their death; death relieves the believer, and others of the wicked; the dead keep only their deeds, see their destination daily, and must not be abused.
Forbidding preference over Moses after a Muslim slapped a Jew, the Prophet said that when people swoon on Resurrection Day he will rise first and find Moses holding the Throne.
Allah will grasp the earth and roll up the heavens; the earth becomes bread, and people are gathered on white land, disbelievers on their faces, all barefoot, naked and uncircumcised.
Adam will be told to bring out the people of the Fire, nine hundred ninety-nine of every thousand, yet the Prophet hopes his followers will be half of Paradise's people.
On Resurrection Day people sweat to their ears, bloodshed is judged first, wrongs are repaid from good deeds, questioned accounts mean punishment, and a disbeliever would ransom himself with gold.
Allah will speak to each person on Resurrection Day without an interpreter, the Fire facing him; shield yourselves from the Fire even with half a date or a good word.
Seventy thousand of the Prophet's followers, faces like the full moon, will enter Paradise without reckoning, shunning branding, ruqya and omens and trusting their Lord; Ukasha asked to join them.
Once all enter Paradise or the Fire, death will be slaughtered between them and eternity announced; the Prophet saw most in Paradise were poor and most in the Fire women.
Allah will grant the people of Paradise His lasting pleasure, and the Prophet told Haritha's mother, her son martyred at Badr, there are many Paradises and he is in Firdaus.
The width between a disbeliever's two shoulders will equal the distance a fast rider covers in three days.
A rider cannot cross a Paradise tree's shade in a hundred years; seventy or seven hundred thousand enter together, faces like the full moon, seeing its lofty abodes like stars.
The Fire's least punished man has embers under his feet boiling his brain, as Abu Talib may; some come out burnt through intercession; shield yourselves even with half a date.
People will ask Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus to intercede, each declining, until Muhammad intercedes again and again, taking people out of the Fire into Paradise.
Haritha, martyred at Badr, is in Firdaus, the highest of many Paradises; a journey in Allah's Cause or a foot's space in Paradise outweighs the whole world.
Each sees his place in the other abode; the sincere monotheist wins the Prophet's intercession; the last man out of the Fire gets ten worlds; Abbas asks about Abu Talib.
Believers will see their Lord plainly as sun and moon; a hooked bridge spans the Fire, prostration marks save the burnt, and the last man pleads his way into Paradise.
The Prophet precedes his people at the Lake-Fount, a month's journey wide, its water whiter than milk, countless cups; al-Kauthar, the abundant good given him, includes a river in Paradise.
Some companions will be driven from the Prophet's Lake-Fount, he being told they innovated and turned apostate after him; in a dream he saw such groups led to the Fire.
Between the Prophet's house and pulpit is a garden of Paradise, his pulpit stands over his Lake-Fount, and he will be his people's predecessor there.
After praying over Uhud's martyrs, the Prophet said he saw his Fount and held the keys to earth's treasures, fearing not their worshipping others but their rivalry over worldly treasures.
The Lake-Fount is as wide as from Medina to Sana', its vessels countless as stars, and some will be taken from it for turning on their heels after the Prophet.
In the womb an angel writes each person's provision, lifespan and whether wretched or blessed; that writing decides his final deeds, and each finds easy what he was created for.
Asked about pagans' children dying young, the Prophet said Allah knows what they would have done; every child is born with Islamic faith, its parents making it Jew or Christian.
A woman gets only what Allah wrote for her, everything has its fixed term, coitus interruptus cannot stop an ordained soul, and the Prophet foretold everything till the Hour.
Each person's place in Fire or Paradise is assigned, yet all must act; a brave fighter the Prophet called of the Fire killed himself, deeds being judged by the last.
Vowing prevents nothing and brings nothing Allah has not written; it only draws out a miser's wealth.
On a campaign the Prophet told those shouting Takbir they call the All-Listener, All-Seer, not the deaf or absent, and taught 'La haula wala quwata illa billah', a Paradise treasure.
Every caliph has two groups of advisers, one urging good and one urging evil, and the protected one is whom Allah protects.
Allah has written each son of Adam's share of adultery: the eye's by looking, the tongue's by speech, the self's by longing, the private parts confirming or refusing it.
Ibn Abbas says the vision of verse 17.60, a trial for mankind, was what the Prophet saw with his eyes on his Night Journey, and the cursed tree is Zaqqum.
When Moses blamed Adam for turning them out of Paradise, Adam answered that Allah had written that deed forty years before creating him, and so Adam won the argument.
After prayer the Prophet said none can withhold what Allah gives or give what He withholds, and told people to seek refuge from calamity, an evil end and bad fate.
The Prophet very often swore, 'No, by Him Who turns the hearts'.
The Prophet told Ibn Saiyad he could not exceed his limits and stopped Umar killing him: if he were the Dajjal Umar could not overcome him, otherwise killing gained nothing.
Allah sent plague as punishment on whom He willed but made it mercy for believers: whoever patiently stays in a stricken town, accepting what Allah wrote, earns a martyr's reward.
At the Trench the Prophet carried earth, saying without Allah they would not have been guided, fasted or prayed, and asking for calm and firm feet against the enemy.
Whoever swears, then finds something better, should do the better and expiate, as Abu Bakr and the Prophet did; persisting in an oath harming one's family is a greater sin.
When people criticised Usama's command, the Prophet swore his father Zaid had deserved command and was among those most beloved to him, as Usama was after him.
The Prophet's oath used to be, 'No, by Him Who turns the hearts'.
The Prophet swore that once Caesar and Khosrau are ruined no Caesar or Khosrau will follow them, and that their treasures will be spent in Allah's Cause.
The Prophet swore that if his followers knew what he knows, they would weep much and laugh little.
Umar said the Prophet was dearer to him than all but himself; told he must be dearer than his own self, Umar said he now was, and the Prophet approved.
Judging a labourer's illegal intercourse with his employer's wife, the Prophet returned the ransom, gave him a hundred lashes and a year's exile, and had the confessing wife stoned.
The Prophet swore that the tribes of Aslam, Ghifar, Muzaina and Juhaina are better than Tamim, Amir bin Sa'sa'a, Ghatfan and Asad.
Rebuking a Zakat collector who kept presents, the Prophet asked if he would get them sitting at home, and swore thieves of Zakat carry it on their necks at Resurrection.
The Prophet swore that if they knew what he knows, they would weep much and laugh little.
In the shade of the Ka'bah the Prophet kept swearing that the wealthy are the losers, except those who spend their wealth this way and that.
Not saying 'Allah willing', Solomon lay with ninety women hoping for horsemen in Allah's Cause, but one bore a half-formed child; the Prophet swore saying it would have brought them.
When people marvelled at a gift of soft silk, the Prophet swore that Sa'd's handkerchiefs in Paradise are better.
Hind, once wishing the Prophet's family degraded and now honoured, was told she may feed her children from miserly Abu Sufyan's property only what is just and reasonable.
The Prophet asked whether his companions would be pleased to be a quarter, then a third, of the people of Paradise, and swore he hoped they would be half.
When a man thought repeating Surat al-Ikhlas alone was too little, the Prophet swore that it equals one third of the Quran.
The Prophet told people to bow and prostrate properly, swearing that he sees them from behind his back.
To an Ansari woman with her children the Prophet swore three times that they were the most beloved people to him.
Allah forbids swearing by fathers; whoever swears by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza must affirm Allah's oneness; Abu Musa told a man who swore off chicken how the Prophet expiated oaths.
The Prophet threw away the gold ring he wore with its stone inward, swearing never to wear it, and the people threw away their rings too.
Swearing by another religion than Islam makes one as he says; a suicide is punished in Hell by the same means; cursing or calling a believer disbeliever equals killing him.
Allah tested three men of the Children of Israel, sending an angel who came first to the leper as a stranded traveller with no help but Allah's and then his.
The Prophet ordered his companions to help others fulfil their oaths.
Urged on oath by his daughter to come to her dying child, the Prophet wept, saying this is mercy Allah places in hearts, and Allah is merciful to the merciful.
A Muslim who loses three children will not be touched by the Fire except as far as fulfils Allah's oath.
The people of Paradise are every poor, humble person whose oath Allah fulfils, and the people of the Fire every violent, cruel, arrogant person.
Best are the Prophet's generation and the next two; then come people whose witness runs ahead of their oaths, and elders forbade the young to swear by Allah's covenant.
Whoever swears falsely to take a Muslim's property will meet an angry Allah, as verse 3.77 confirms; Al-Ash'ath says it came about his dispute over a well.
Hell will keep asking for more until the Lord puts His Foot over it, and it says 'Enough, enough' by His Power and Honour as its sides draw together.
In Aisha's account of the slander, when the Prophet sought relief from Abdullah bin Ubai, Usaid bin Hudair swore by Allah's eternity to Sa'd bin Ubada they would kill him.
Aisha says verse 2.225 on unintentional oaths concerns phrases like 'No, by Allah' and 'Yes, by Allah', alongside verses excusing mistakes and Moses' plea about what he forgot.
Allah forgives the Prophet's followers the evil their souls whisper as long as they do not act on it or speak it.
Asked on the Day of Nahr about rites done out of order, such as Tawaf before stoning or shaving before slaughter, the Prophet answered each, 'There is no harm'.
Sent back three times to repeat his prayer, a man was taught to perform ablution, face the Qibla, say Takbir, recite, and bow, prostrate and sit until at rest.
At Uhud, Satan's shout made Muslims attack their own rear, killing Hudhaifa's father despite Hudhaifa's cries, and Hudhaifa asked forgiveness for the killers until he died.
Whoever eats or drinks forgetfully while fasting should complete his fast, for Allah fed him.
The Prophet made two prostrations of forgetfulness after rising without sitting and after praying the wrong number of rak'at, prescribing them for anyone unsure how many he prayed.
Moses' first excuse to his companion, 'Call me not to account for what I forget' (18.73), was his forgetfulness.
Whoever slaughtered his Eid sacrifice before the prayer was told to slaughter another, and Al-Bara, whose family had done so for a guest, offered a young milch she-goat.
The biggest sins are joining others in worship with Allah, undutifulness to parents, unlawful killing and the oath Al-Ghamus.
A false oath for a Muslim's property brings Allah's wrath; the Prophet promised mounts he swore to withhold, and Abu Bakr resumed the aid to Mistah he swore to stop.
As Abu Talib was dying, the Prophet asked him to say 'La ilaha illallah', a word by which he could defend him before Allah.
Two phrases light on the tongue, heavy in the balance and beloved to the Gracious are 'Subhan Allahi wa bi-hamdihi' and 'Subhan Allahi-l-Adhim'.
Whoever dies setting up rivals to Allah enters the Fire, the Prophet said, and Abdullah added that whoever dies without doing so enters Paradise.
Having sworn to keep from his wives for a month, the Prophet stayed in an upper room and came down after twenty-nine nights, saying a month can be twenty-nine days.
A bride served the Prophet soaked dates; Sauda soaked dates in a skin till worn out; his family never had their fill of wheat bread with meat three days running.
When Abu Talha and Um Sulaim sent the hungry Prophet barley loaves, he came with his companions and blessed the bread, and seventy or eighty men ate their fill.
Deeds are rewarded by intentions: emigration for Allah and His Apostle counts as such, while emigration for worldly gain or to marry a woman counts only for that.
Repenting for staying behind from Tabuk, Ka'b bin Malik offered all his property for Allah and His Apostle, but the Prophet told him to keep some, as that was better.
When Aisha and Hafsa agreed to say he smelled of Maghafir, the Prophet swore off the honey he drank at Zainab's, and verses 66.1-4 were revealed.
A vow neither hastens nor delays anything Allah has decreed, only drawing out a miser's wealth; after the best generations will come people who vow without fulfilling and testify unasked.
A vow to obey Allah must be kept, one to disobey Him not; Umar was told to fulfil a pre-Islamic I'tikaf vow; vows of the dead are fulfilled for them.
The Prophet rejected self-torment, cut ropes leading men round the Ka'bah, and let Abu Israil keep only his vow's fast; Ibn Umar cited the ban on fasting Eid.
When an arrow killed the slave Mid'am, the Prophet swore the sheet he stole from Khaibar's booty was burning on him, and called returned shoe straps straps of fire.
Lice-troubled Ka'b could expiate by fasting, charity or sacrifice; for intercourse while fasting in Ramadan, a man unable to free a slave, fast or feed sixty fed his family.
The Prophet's Sa' was a later Mudd and a third; Ibn Umar paid Zakat al-Fitr and oath expiations by the Prophet's Mudd; the Prophet asked Allah to bless Medina's measures.
Freeing a Muslim slave saves each of the freer's limbs from the Fire; the Prophet sold a Mudabbar slave, a man's only property; the Wala goes to the freer.
The Prophet swore not to give the Ash'ariyin mounts, then gave them camels, saying Allah provided them and that, Allah willing, he expiates an oath when he finds something better.
Solomon forgot to say 'If Allah will' when hoping ninety wives would bear warriors, so only one bore, a half-boy; had he said it, he would have got his wish.
Abu Musa told a man who swore off chicken how the Prophet broke an oath for something better and expiated; Abdur-Rahman was told likewise, and not to seek rule.
When Jabir lay unconscious the Prophet poured his ablution water over him; Jabir asked how to distribute his property, and the Prophet did not reply until the inheritance verses came.
Beware of suspicion, the worst of false tales; do not seek faults, spy, hate or desert one another, but be brothers, O Allah's slaves.
The prophets' property is not inherited but spent in charity, after the family's provision, as Abu Bakr told Fatima and Al-Abbas, Umar told Ali and Abbas, and Aisha the wives.
The Prophet pays the debts of believers who die leaving nothing, while any property goes to the heirs: the prescribed shares first, then the remainder to the closest male relative.
Near death with one daughter as heir, Sa'd was allowed to give a third in charity, though even that is much, as heirs are better left rich than poor.
A daughter takes half, a son's daughter a sixth, a sister the rest; shares come first, then the closest male; parents and spouses have fixed portions; Emigrant-Ansar brotherhood inheritance ended.
After a Li'an case the child went to the wife alone, and over Zam'a's slave girl's son the Prophet ruled that the boy belongs to the bed's owner.
The Wala goes to the one who pays and frees, as with Barira, who then left her husband; it may not be sold or given; Muslims freed none as Sa'iba.
A sister's son belongs to her people; a man's property goes to his heirs, his debts and dependants to the Prophet; Muslims and disbelievers do not inherit from each other.
Zam'a's slave girl's disputed son went to the bed's owner, Sauda screening herself; knowingly claiming another man as father forbids Paradise; whoever denies his father is charged with disbelief.
A wolf took one of two women's sons; David gave the boy to the elder, but Solomon, offering to cut him in two, gave him to the younger, who objected.
The Prophet was delighted when Mujazziz, seeing only the uncovered feet of Zaid and Usama, said these feet belong to each other.
An adulterer, a drinker, a thief and a robber watched by people are not believers while committing these acts.
The Prophet had drinkers beaten with palm stalks, shoes, hands and garments, forbidding cursing them; Abu Bakr gave forty lashes, Umar forty then eighty; Ali said none were fixed.
An adulterer is not a believer while committing illegal intercourse, nor a thief while stealing.
Allah curses the thief whose hand is cut for an egg or a rope; Al-A'mash says people took these as an iron helmet and a rope worth dirhams.
Taking a pledge against polytheism, theft and illegal intercourse, the Prophet said a legal punishment for such a sin expiates it, while one Allah screens is left to His will.
In the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet declared blood, property and honour as sacred as that day, town and month, and warned against reverting to disbelief by killing one another.
The Prophet chose the easier of two options unless it was sinful, and never took revenge for himself, only for Allah's sake when His limits were transgressed.
When Usama interceded for a Makhzumi woman thief, the Prophet said earlier nations perished by punishing the weak and sparing the noble, and swore he would cut even Fatima's hand.
A thief's hand is cut for a quarter dinar or more, not for less than a shield's price, as the Prophet did for a shield worth three dirhams.
A woman whose hand the Prophet cut repented sincerely; a legal punishment expiates and purifies the sins named in the pledge, and a repentant thief's witness is accepted.
Ukl men cured by camels' milk and urine turned renegades, killed the shepherd, took the camels; their hands and feet were cut, eyes branded, and they were left to die.
Allah will shade seven on Resurrection Day, including one refusing a noble woman's call to illegal intercourse; the Prophet guarantees Paradise to whoever guards his tongue and private parts.
Among the Hour's signs: religious knowledge taken away, ignorance spreading, drinking and open illegal intercourse common, and women so many that fifty have one man to look after them.
Faith leaves the adulterer, thief, drinker and killer while sinning, as Ibn Abbas showed by parting clasped hands, but returns if he repents, for repentance stays open.
The biggest sin is setting up rivals to Allah, then killing one's child lest it share one's food, then illegal intercourse with a neighbour's wife.
Ali stoned a woman following the Prophet; a married Aslami confessing four times was stoned and prayed over; stones are for the adulterer; Jewish adulterers were stoned per the Torah.
A man who had intercourse with his wife while fasting in Ramadan, told to free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty, was given food for his family.
A man who asked for a legal punishment was not questioned, and after praying with the Prophet was told Allah had forgiven his sin.
Ma'iz, asked whether he only kissed or looked, confessed and was stoned, as was a man confessing four times; a labourer was flogged and exiled; Umar affirmed stoning married adulterers.
Umar's sermon affirmed the revealed verse of stoning married adulterers and recounted the pledge to Abu Bakr; an unmarried adulterer is flogged a hundred stripes and exiled for a year.
The Prophet cursed effeminate men and women taking on men's manners, said to turn them out of houses, and he and Umar each turned one out.
A labourer's son was flogged and exiled, his employer's confessing wife stoned, and a Jewish couple stoned per the Torah; a slave girl is flogged and, after three offences, sold.
Abu Bakr rebuked Aisha and struck her for holding up the people over her necklace while the Prophet slept on her thigh, and the verse of tayammum was then revealed.
Told that Sa'd would kill any man he found with his wife, the Prophet said he had more ghira than Sa'd, and Allah more than he.
A bedouin whose wife bore a black child was asked about grey camels among his red ones and told the child had most probably inherited its colour from ancestors.
Beyond Allah's set punishments none gets over ten stripes; the Prophet prolonged a fast as if punishing wisal-fasters, resellers of unmoved food were beaten, and he avenged only for Allah.
The Prophet separated a couple after li'an and her child resembled the accused man; Ibn Abbas said the woman the Prophet would have stoned without witnesses was another.
The seven destructive sins are polytheism, sorcery, unjust killing, consuming usury, consuming an orphan's property, fleeing the battlefield, and accusing chaste believing women.
Whoever slanders his slave, who is innocent of what he says, will be flogged on the Day of Resurrection unless the slave is as he described.
A labourer's son who committed adultery with his employer's wife was flogged a hundred stripes and exiled a year, the ransom returned, and the wife stoned on confessing.
The greatest sins are setting up a rival to Allah, killing one's son lest he share one's food, and adultery with a neighbour's wife, as a revealed verse confirms.
A believer remains at liberty in his religion unless he kills unlawfully, bloodshed is the first case judged, and Al-Miqdad was told not to kill a foe who declared Islam.
Every unjust killing lays a share of the guilt on Adam's first son, who began the practice of murder on earth.
The Prophet warned, also at the Farewell Hajj, that after him they must not turn disbelievers by striking one another's necks.
The biggest sins are joining partners with Allah, undutifulness to parents, murder, and a false oath, statement or witness.
Usama was rebuked for killing a man who said none is worshipped but Allah; the pledge forbade killing, and two Muslims fighting with swords are both in the Fire.
A Jew who killed a girl was killed with stones; a Muslim's blood is lawful only in three cases, and the victim's relative may choose blood money or retaliation.
The three most hated to Allah are an evildoer in the sanctuary, one seeking pre-Islamic ways in Islam, and one seeking to shed blood without right.
At Uhud, after Satan's shout, the army's front ranks attacked their own rear and killed Al-Yaman despite his son Hudhaifa's cries, and Hudhaifa asked Allah to forgive them.
A Jew who crushed a girl's head was killed with stones, and the Prophet, dosed against his wish, said all but Al-Abbas would be made to drink medicine.
No blame falls on one who blinds with a stone a man peeping into his house without permission, and the Prophet aimed an arrowhead at a man peeping in.
At Uhud, after Satan's shout, Muslims killed Al-Yaman as his son Hudhaifa cried out, and Hudhaifa asked Allah to forgive the killer until he died.
Some said Amir, killed at Khaibar, lost his deeds by killing himself, but the Prophet said whoever says so lies, for Amir has a double reward.
No blood money for a biter's lost teeth, but retaliation for a broken tooth, slaps and a group killing; finger equals thumb; those who dosed the Prophet must drink it.
With no proof against the killer of a man found slain at Khaibar, the Prophet paid the blood money, and Abu Qilaba argued against basing retaliation on qasama oaths.
The Prophet aimed an arrowhead at a man peeping into his house, said asking permission exists to prevent unlawful looks, and one who pokes a peeper's eye is blameless.
Ali's sheet held blood-money rules; the Prophet ruled a male or female slave for a miscarried fetus, as Al-Mughira told Umar, and the killer's relatives paid for the slain woman.
Anas, brought as a boy to serve the Prophet at home and on journeys, said the Prophet never asked him why he had or had not done anything.
No blood money is due for one killed by an animal, a well or a mine, and a fifth of buried treasure goes to the state.
Whoever kills a person under the Muslims' pledge of protection will not smell Paradise's fragrance, though it reaches across forty years' travel.
Ali said he had only the Quran, understanding of it, and a sheet holding blood-money rules, captives' ransom, and that no Muslim is killed for killing a disbeliever.
Do not prefer some prophets to others; when an Ansari slapped a Jew for exalting Moses, the Prophet said he would find Moses holding a pillar of the Throne.
When the verse on believers not mixing belief with wrong distressed the companions, the Prophet explained the wrong meant joining others with Allah, as Luqman said.
The biggest sins are joining others with Allah, undutifulness to parents, and false witness or the Ghamus oath, a false oath taking a Muslim's property.
Whoever does good in Islam is not punished for pre-Islamic deeds, but whoever does evil in Islam is punished for both his former and later deeds.
Ibn Abbas cited the Prophet's order to kill, not burn, whoever changes his religion; Mu'adh insisted a man reverting to Judaism be killed; Abu Bakr resolved to fight Zakat refusers.
When Jews greeted the Prophet with 'death be upon you', he forbade killing the one who said it, told Aisha to be gentle, and taught replying 'and upon you'.
The Prophet told of one of the prophets who, beaten and bloodied by his people, wiped his face and asked his Lord to forgive them, for they did not know.
The Prophet foretold people whose Quran recital never passes their throats, who leave the religion like an arrow through game, and said to kill them; Ali killed them.
The Hour will not come until two great groups fight each other while making one and the same claim.
Umar dragged Hisham to the Prophet for reciting Surat al-Furqan differently; the Prophet approved both readings, saying the Quran was revealed to be recited in seven ways.
When the companions feared the verse on not mixing belief with wrong, the Prophet said the wrong meant joining others in worship with Allah, as Luqman told his son.
When a man called Malik bin Ad-Dukhshun a hypocrite, the Prophet said whoever meets Allah saying none is worshipped but Allah, for Allah's sake, will be saved from the Fire.
Ali seized Hatib's letter to the Meccans from a woman; Umar wanted him killed as a betrayer, but the Prophet accepted his excuse and spared him as one of Badr.
In his prayer the Prophet asked Allah to save Aiyash, Salama, Al-Walid and the weak believers, and to afflict Mudar with famine years like Joseph's.
Faith's sweetness belongs to whoever holds Allah and His Messenger dearest, loves others only for Allah, and hates returning to disbelief as he hates being thrown into the Fire.
Sa'id bin Zaid recalled Umar binding him to force him from Islam, and the Prophet told complaining companions that earlier believers sawn in two never left their religion.
At Bait al-Midras the Prophet thrice called the Jews to embrace Islam and be safe, then said he wanted to exile them, so those with property could sell it.
The Prophet annulled the marriage of Khansa, given by her father against her wish, and said a woman's consent is required, a shy virgin's silence counting as consent.
When an Ansari made his only property, a slave, free upon his death, the Prophet sold the slave to Nu'aim bin An-Nahham for 800 dirhams.
The verse forbidding inheriting women against their will concerns a pre-Islamic custom whereby a dead man's relatives could marry his wife, marry her off or stop her marrying.
Umar flogged and exiled a male slave who forced himself on a slave girl, not flogging her as she was unwilling; Az-Zuhri added a fine for raping a virgin slave.
When a tyrant demanded Sarah from Abraham and sought to harm her, she made ablution and prayed, and the king was seized by a fit.
A Muslim neither wrongs his brother nor hands him to an oppressor, Allah meets the needs of one meeting his brother's, and an oppressor brother is helped by being stopped.
Deeds are rewarded by intentions, so one emigrating for Allah and His Messenger has that, and one emigrating for worldly gain or a woman has what he sought.
Allah does not accept the prayer of one who has passed wind until he performs ablution anew.
Abu Bakr's letter forbade merging or splitting property to avoid Zakat, treasure whose Zakat is unpaid becomes a snake on Resurrection Day, and some people allowed tricks to escape it.
The Prophet forbade Shighar, exchanging daughters or sisters in marriage without Mahr, and Mut'a marriage at Khaibar, while some people judged such marriages made by trick valid or invalid.
No one should withhold his surplus water from others' animals in order to keep them from the surplus grass.
The Prophet forbade An-Najsh and told a man who was always cheated in bargains to say 'No cheating' whenever he bargained.
Aisha explained the verse on orphan girls: guardians drawn by their wealth and beauty were forbidden to marry them with less than a full Mahr.
Every betrayer will have a flag by which he is recognised on the Day of Resurrection.
The Prophet, only human, judges by what he hears, so whoever is wrongly awarded his brother's right by an eloquent case is given only a piece of Fire.
A virgin or matron is married only with her consent, a virgin's silence counting, and Khansa's forced marriage was cancelled, though some people upheld marriages faked through false witnesses.
When the Prophet stayed long with Hafsa drinking honey, Aisha had Sauda and Safiya say he smelled of Maghafir, a trick that made him refuse the honey thereafter.
Umar turned back from Sargh on hearing the Prophet's saying, from Abdur-Rahman, not to enter a plague-stricken land nor flee one, plague being a punishment sent on nations.
One who takes back his gift is like a dog swallowing its own vomit, an example believers should not follow.
The Prophet gave pre-emption in undivided property and said a neighbour has most right to his neighbour's care, yet some people allowed tricks like gifts or share-buying to defeat it.
The Prophet rebuked a Zakat collector claiming gifts, asking whether he would get them at his parents' home, and warned that anything taken unlawfully is carried on Resurrection Day.
The neighbour has most right to his neighbour's care, yet some allowed a sham price trick to defeat pre-emption, though the Prophet forbade selling Muslims defective or stolen goods.

Revelation began with true dreams and the angel's command to read in Hira; Khadija comforted the Prophet, Waraqa recognised the angel, and when revelation paused Gabriel reassured him on mountaintops.
A good dream is from Allah, one of forty-six parts of prophethood and its only remnant; a bad dream is from Satan, harmless if one seeks refuge and spits left.
Some were shown the Night of Qadr in the last seven days of Ramadan, and the Prophet said to seek it then.
Had he stayed in prison as long as Joseph and then been summoned by the messenger, the Prophet said, he would have answered the call.
Whoever sees the Prophet in a dream has truly seen him, for Satan cannot take his form, and after a bad dream one should spit thrice left and seek refuge.
The Prophet dreamt of earth's treasure keys in his hand, Jesus and the Dajjal at the Ka'ba, and his followers sailing as fighters, Um Haram among the first.
Questioned for testifying Allah had honoured the dead Uthman bin Maz'un, Um Al-Ala dreamt of a spring flowing for him, his good deeds; bad dreams come from Satan.
The Prophet dreamt he drank milk and gave the rest to Umar, interpreting it as knowledge, and saw Umar dragging a long shirt, interpreting it as the religion.
Abdullah bin Salam's dream of climbing a post to a handhold meant he would die holding to Islam, and the Prophet was twice shown Aisha in silk as his wife.
Given concise speech and victory by awe, the Prophet dreamt of earth's treasure keys; Abdullah bin Salam's handhold meant firm Islam, and Ibn Umar's silk cloth flew him across Paradise.
Near the Hour a believer's dreams will hardly fail, dreams being thoughts, Satan's frights or glad tidings, and Um Al-Ala's dream of a spring meant Uthman bin Maz'un's good deeds.
The Prophet dreamt Abu Bakr drew a bucket or two weakly and Umar drew mightily, and saw in Paradise a palace for Umar, whose ghira kept him out.
In dreams the Prophet saw Jesus and the Dajjal and passed Umar milk meaning knowledge; Ibn Umar dreamt of the well-like Fire and was urged to pray more at night.
The Prophet dreamt of two gold bangles he blew away, meaning two liars, and of migrating to a palm land, Yathrib, where slaughtered cows meant the believers killed at Uhud.
In the Prophet's dreams a black woman leaving Medina for Al-Juhfa meant its epidemic moving there, and a sword broken then restored meant Uhud's losses, then the conquest.
The worst lie is claiming a false dream, its teller made to knot two barley grains; eavesdroppers get molten lead in their ears, and picture-makers must put souls in pictures.
Keep a disliked dream to oneself, seeking refuge; Abu Bakr interpreted a dream of a cloud dripping butter and honey and a rope, partly right and partly wrong.
In a dream two angels showed the Prophet punishments of a Quran neglecter, a liar, adulterers and a usurer, Abraham with children, and the Eden Paradise awaiting him.
The Prophet will precede his people at the Lake-Fount, whose drinkers never thirst, but some will be pulled away for turning apostate and changing the religion after him.
Facing rulers' selfishness, give them their rights and ask Allah for yours, be patient rather than leave the Muslims, obey, and do not fight a ruler without proven open disbelief.
The Prophet said his followers' destruction will come at the hands of young men of Quraysh.
The Prophet warned the Arabs of an approaching evil, a gap having opened in Gog and Magog's wall, and said they could perish despite the righteous if evil increased.
From a high building in Medina the Prophet said he saw afflictions falling among their houses like raindrops.
Near the Hour time will pass quickly, good deeds decrease, miserliness spread, religious knowledge vanish, ignorance and afflictions appear, and killing (al-Harj) abound.
Near the Hour, religious knowledge will be taken away, ignorance will spread and killing (al-Harj) will abound, and the most wicked people will be living when it comes.
Every coming time will be worse than the last, so be patient; the Prophet woke alarmed at the afflictions sent down and wanted his wives woken to pray.
Whoever takes up arms against Muslims is not of them; do not point weapons or carry bare arrowheads, for Muslim blood is sacred and killing one another is disbelief.
In coming afflictions sitting is better than standing, two Muslims fighting with swords both go to Hell, hold to the Muslims' group or flee with sheep, and honesty will vanish.
Pressed with questions, the Prophet offered from the pulpit to answer any, named one man's father, and Umar sought refuge with Allah from the evil of afflictions.
Afflictions come from the East and Najd, whence the side of Satan's head emerges; the Prophet fought pagans, not for rule, and Umar was the door holding afflictions back.
While Abu Musa kept the gate of a Medina garden, the Prophet gave Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman glad tidings of Paradise, Uthman with a calamity to befall him.
Usama talked to the ruler secretly but would praise no ruler, citing a man in Hell who ordered good yet did evil; a nation ruled by a woman never succeeds.
With Aisha gone to Basra, Ammar told Kufa she was the Prophet's wife in both worlds but they were being tested; he, Abu Musa and Abu Mas'ud faulted each other.
When Allah sends punishment upon a nation it strikes all its people, and they are then resurrected according to their deeds.
As Al-Hasan bin Ali moved with armies against Muawiya, peace was proposed, and the Prophet had called Al-Hasan a chief through whom Allah may make peace between two Muslim groups.
Usama sent word to Ali that he would gladly be with him even in a lion's mouth, but would take no part in this matter.
When Medina deposed Yazid, Ibn Umar warned his friends and children that every betrayer gets a flag on Resurrection Day, and fighting one given allegiance is the worst faithlessness.
Abu Barza said Islam lifted the Arabs from misery, but worldly wealth brought mischief, and the factions in Sham, Mecca and among his hearers fought only for worldly gain.
Hudhaifa said the hypocrites of his day were worse than in the Prophet's lifetime, doing evil openly, not secretly, and what was once hypocrisy had become disbelief after belief.
Before the Hour come Daus women circling their idol, a fire from Hijaz, gold uncovered by the Euphrates, alms finding no taker, and the sun rising from the West.
Every prophet warned of the one-eyed Dajjal, marked 'Kafir', whose fire is water; he will kill and revive a man, but angels will keep him and plague out of Medina.
Alarmed, the Prophet said a hole had opened in the dam of Gog and Magog, warned the Arabs of approaching evil, and said people perish when evil increases.
Whoever obeys the Prophet obeys Allah and whoever disobeys him disobeys Allah, and obeying or disobeying the ruler he appoints is obeying or disobeying him.
Everyone is a guardian responsible for his charges, from the ruler to the slave, and the caliphate will stay with Quraish while they uphold the religion, even if two remain.
One may wish to be like only two people: one given wealth who spends it rightly, and one given wisdom who acts on it and teaches it.
Obey rulers, even an Ethiopian slave, and bear what you dislike, but obedience is only in good, as shown when a commander ordered his men into a fire.
Do not seek authority, which brings regret on Resurrection Day and is not given to those who ask; a ruler who deceives or neglects his subjects is denied Paradise.
Allah will expose on Resurrection Day whoever does good to show off and trouble whoever troubles people; Jundab advised eating only lawful food and shedding no blood.
A man asking about the Hour, who had prepared little but loved Allah and His Apostle, was told he will be with those he loves.
A woman weeping at a grave rebuffed the Prophet, not recognising him, and when she came to apologise he said patience is at the first stroke of a calamity.
Qais bin Sa'd served the Prophet like a chief police officer serves a ruler, and the Prophet sent Abu Musa and then Mu'adh to Yemen as governors.
Seeing a man who had become Muslim then reverted to Judaism, Mu'adh refused to sit unless he were killed, calling it the verdict of Allah and His Apostle.
Abu Bakra wrote to his son not to judge between two people while angry, for the Prophet said a judge should not judge in anger.
Angered that an imam's lengthy prayer kept a man from the morning congregation, the Prophet told imams to shorten it, for among the people are the old, weak and busy.
Angry that Ibn Umar divorced his wife in her menses, the Prophet ordered him to take her back and keep her through another period before divorcing, if he wished.
Hind, once wishing the Prophet's family degraded and now honoured, asked if she may feed her children from miserly Abu Sufyan's property, and was told she may, reasonably.
To write to the Byzantines, who read only sealed letters, the Prophet took a silver ring engraved 'Muhammad, Apostle of Allah'.
Umar urged a man refusing pay for public work to take it, as the Prophet bade Umar take unsought money, keep it, then give it in charity, never seeking it.
A husband and wife carried out li'an in the mosque after he asked whether a man finding another with his wife should kill him, and divorce was decreed.
A man confessed illegal sexual intercourse in the mosque; the Prophet turned away until he testified four times, asked if he was mad, then ordered him stoned at the Musalla.
A right awarded in error by the Prophet, who judged by what he heard, is a piece of Fire; he awarded Abu Qatada his slain foe's spoils at Hunain.
Walking Safiya home, the Prophet told two passing Ansar men 'She is Safiya', explaining that Satan circulates in the human body like blood.
Sending Abu Musa and Mu'adh to Yemen, the Prophet told them to make things easy, give glad tidings and cooperate, and said every intoxicant is prohibited.
The Prophet ordered that captives be set free and invitations be accepted.
Rebuking a zakat collector who claimed gifts, the Prophet asked whether he would get them sitting at home, warning that whatever is taken unlawfully is carried on Resurrection Day.
Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhaifa, led the early emigrants and companions, among them Abu Bakr and Umar, in prayer at the Quba mosque.
Over freeing the Hawazin captives, the Prophet said he could not tell who consented, so the people's representatives (urafa) consulted them and reported that all agreed gladly.
Ibn Umar counted praising rulers to their faces and speaking otherwise behind them as hypocrisy, and the Prophet called the double-faced person the worst of mankind.
Hind said Abu Sufyan was miserly, and the Prophet told her to take reasonably from his wealth what suffices her and her children.
A right wrongly won through eloquence is a piece of Fire; the child belongs to the owner of the bed, and a false oath to seize property meets Allah's anger.
A companion promised freedom after his death to his only property, a slave, so the Prophet sold the slave for 800 dirhams and sent him the price.
Answering criticism of Usama bin Zaid's command, the Prophet said his father had also been criticised yet deserved leadership, and both were among those most beloved to him.
The most hated person in Allah's sight is the most quarrelsome one.
Khalid killed and captured men of Bani Jadhima who could not say 'Aslamna', ordered captives killed, Ibn Umar refused, and the Prophet twice declared himself free of Khalid's deed.
While the Prophet made peace among Bani Amr, Abu Bakr led the prayer and stepped back on his arrival; in prayer, men say Subhan Allah to alert and women clap.
After many Quran reciters fell at Al-Yamama, Abu Bakr, urged by Umar, had Zaid bin Thabit collect the Quran from scattered writings and men's memories.
When Abdullah bin Sahl was found killed at Khaibar and the Jews denied it, his kin declined to swear, so the Prophet paid a hundred she-camels as blood money himself.
For a labourer's illegal intercourse with his employer's wife, the Prophet judged by Allah's Book: ransom returned, a hundred lashes and a year's exile for him, stoning for her.
Zaid learned the Jews' writing for the Prophet's letters, Umar and Ibn Abbas used interpreters, some held a ruler needs two, and Heraclius questioned Abu Sufyan through an interpreter.
The Prophet questioned a zakat collector who claimed gifts, asking whether he would get them at home, and warned that whatever is taken unlawfully is carried on Resurrection Day.
Every prophet and caliph has two groups of advisers, one urging good and one urging evil, and only the one Allah protects is safe.
Companions pledged to listen and obey, when active or tired, as far as they could, to observe jihad while alive, and to die; Ibn Umar so pledged to Abdul Malik.

Umar's chosen candidates left the choice to Abdur-Rahman, who consulted for three nights, chose Uthman on condition of following Allah's Laws and the Prophet's traditions, and everyone gave him allegiance.
Salama pledged twice under the tree, a feverish bedouin's pledge was not cancelled, a child was blessed instead, pledging for worldly gain was condemned, and women pledged by words only.
The Prophet thought of appointing Abu Bakr, who received public allegiance and to whom a woman was referred; Umar weighed naming a successor, and twelve rulers will be from Quraish.
The Prophet said he almost ordered the houses of men absent from congregational prayer burned, and that they would come to Isha for a meaty bone.
After Ka'b bin Malik and others stayed behind from Tabuk, the Prophet forbade Muslims to speak to them for fifty nights, then announced Allah's acceptance of their repentance.
The Prophet would join every battle but for men without mounts who hate staying behind, and would love to be martyred in Allah's cause, revived and martyred again and again.
Had the Prophet gold like Mount Uhud, he would love to give it all away within three days, if anyone accepted it, keeping only enough to pay debts.
The Prophet wished he had not brought his sacrificial animal (Hadi), so he could end ihram with the people, whom he had told to use their ihram for Umrah.
Unable to sleep, the Prophet wished a righteous companion would guard him and Sa'd came, while Bilal longed to spend a night in a Meccan valley.
One may wish to be like only two: a man given the Quran who recites it night and day, and a man given wealth who spends it rightly.
The Prophet forbade longing for or praying for death, for a good person may do more good and an evildoer may repent; Anas and Khabbab held back.
Carrying earth on the day of the Confederates, the Prophet said that without Allah they would not be guided, give charity or pray, asking tranquillity as the enemy had rebelled.
Do not long to meet the enemy, but ask Allah for safety.
Discussing a li'an case, Ibn Abbas said the Prophet's words about stoning a woman without proof concerned one whose open misbehaviour aroused suspicion.
When the Prophet delayed the Isha prayer until women and children slept, he said he would order it at that hour were it not hard on his followers.
Were it not hard on his followers, the Prophet would have ordered them to use the siwak.
The Prophet forbade continuous fasting (wisal), saying his Lord feeds him and gives him drink, and when people persisted he fasted it with them until the crescent appeared.
Aisha learned the outer wall, left out for lack of money, is the Ka'bah's, and but for her people's recent ignorance the Prophet would include it and lower the gate.
But for the emigration, the Prophet would have been one of the Ansar, and he would take the Ansar's valley if people took another.
The Prophet sent young men who missed their families home to teach them, telling them to pray as they saw him pray, call the adhan, and let the eldest lead.
Bilal's adhan at night does not stop suhur, for it lets night worshippers return to eat and sleepers wake; eat and drink until Ibn Um Maktum's adhan.
Told he had prayed five rak'at of Zuhr, and confirming Dhul-Yaddain's report that he had stopped at two, the Prophet made two prostrations of forgetfulness, completing the shortened prayer first.
When the qibla was changed to the Ka'bah, as the Prophet had wished, a man's report turned the worshippers at Quba, and some Ansar, towards it mid-prayer.
When a man announced that all alcoholic drinks were prohibited, Abu Talha had Anas break the jars of date drink he was serving.
The Prophet sent Abu Ubaida to the people of Najran as a truly trustworthy man, calling him the trustworthy one (Amin) of this nation.
Umar and an Ansari friend took turns attending the Prophet, each telling the other what he had heard from him.
When a commander ordered his soldiers into a fire, the Prophet said had they entered they would have stayed in it, for obedience is only in what is good.
For a labourer's illegal intercourse with his employer's wife, the Prophet judged by Allah's Book: ransom returned, a hundred lashes and exile for him, stoning for her on confession.
Az-Zubair answered the Prophet's call three times at the Trench and was named his helper (hawari), and Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman were given glad tidings of Paradise.
Umar found the Prophet in an upper room with a black slave at the top of the stairs, asked through him for permission, and was admitted.
The Prophet sent a letter to Khosrau through the ruler of Bahrain, Khosrau tore it up, and the Prophet reportedly invoked Allah to tear them to pieces.
The Prophet had a man of Aslam announce on Ashura that whoever had eaten should fast the rest of the day and whoever had not should complete the fast.
The Prophet told the Abd Al-Qais delegation that belief in Allah means testifying to Him and His Messenger, prayer, zakat and a fifth of booty, and forbade four drinking vessels.
When companions stopped eating meat on hearing it was mastigure, the Prophet told them to carry on, for it is lawful, though not among his own foods.
A Jew told Umar his people would have made a festival of the day the verse perfecting the religion came, and Umar said it came on Arafat day, a Friday.
Umar urged holding to the Book that guided the Prophet, who prayed for Ibn Abbas to be taught it, and Ibn Umar pledged obedience by Allah's Laws and Sunnah.
The Prophet was given concise speech of wide meaning, victory through awe and, in a dream, the world's treasure keys; unlike earlier prophets' miracles, his gift was revelation.
Umar said the Prophet and Abu Bakr must be followed, Quran and Sunna strengthen honesty, the best speech is Allah's Book, the best way Muhammad's, and heresies the worst.
All the Prophet's followers enter Paradise except those who disobey him, for obeying Muhammad is obeying Allah, as shown in parables of a banquet's inviter and a naked warner.
When some Arabs reverted to disbelief after the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr insisted, against Umar's doubt, on fighting those who separated zakat from prayer, and Umar saw he was right.
Uyaina accused Umar of giving too little and judging unjustly, but Umar held back when Al-Hurr recited the verse bidding forgiveness and turning from the foolish, keeping to Allah's Book.
After the eclipse prayer the Prophet said people will be tried in their graves, where the believer affirms Muhammad brought clear signs and the hypocrite says he does not know.

Earlier nations were ruined by questions and differences over their prophets; the Prophet disliked needless questions, feared night prayer becoming obligatory and grew angry when pressed; overburdening oneself is forbidden.
When some Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit, he waited for revelation, then recited that knowledge of the spirit is with his Lord.
People followed the Prophet in wearing and discarding gold rings, he forbade continuous fasting, Ali's scroll cursed innovators in Medina, and the Prophet rebuked those avoiding what he himself did.
Abu Bakr and Umar raised their voices before the Prophet over appointing a chief for Bani Tamim, the verse forbidding raised voices came down, and Umar spoke to him softly.
In his fatal illness the Prophet insisted Abu Bakr lead the prayer despite Aisha and Hafsa urging Umar, likening them to the companions of Joseph.
Uwaimir asked whether a husband who kills a man found with his wife is killed; the Prophet disliked the question, revelation came, they performed li'an, and he divorced her.
Ali and Abbas disputed the Bani Nadir property before Umar, who said the Prophet's property is not inherited but charity, and must be managed as he and Abu Bakr did.
Medina is a sanctuary whose trees may not be cut, and whoever innovates a heresy or sins there incurs the curse of Allah, the angels and all people.
Knowledge will vanish with the death of scholars, leaving the ignorant to give misleading verdicts by opinion, and at Siffin Sahl bin Hunaif told people to distrust their own opinions.
When the sick Jabir, revived by the Prophet's ablution water, asked how to deal with his wealth, the Prophet gave no reply until the verse of inheritance was revealed.
A woman asked for a day of teaching for women; the Prophet taught them, then said a woman who loses three children, or even two, is screened from the Fire.
A group of the Prophet's followers will stay victorious until Allah's order comes, understanding of the Quran and Sunna is Allah's favour, and the nation will remain good until then.
As verse 6:65 came down, the Prophet sought refuge with Allah's Face from punishment from above and below, and called party strife and mutual violence the easier warnings.
To a bedouin who doubted his black son was his, the Prophet pointed to grey camels among red ones, colour inherited from ancestors, and did not let him deny paternity.
Told of a mother who vowed Hajj but died, the Prophet bade her daughter perform it for her, as she would pay her debts, for Allah has more right.
One may wish to be like only two: a man given wealth who spends it rightly, and a man given religious wisdom who judges by it and teaches it.
For a woman miscarrying from a blow, the blood money is a male or female slave, as Al-Mughira told Umar, who demanded a witness and got Muhammad bin Maslama.
The Prophet's followers will copy earlier nations span by span, even into a mastigure's hole; asked if these were Persians and Byzantines, or Jews and Christians, he said who else.
Adam's first son shares the burden of every unjust killing, for he was the first to establish murder.
A bedouin refused release from his pledge left Medina, which expels impurities like bellows, and Umar delayed a sermon until Medina, place of the Sunna and the companions.
Wiping his nose on linen, Abu Huraira recalled fainting from hunger between the Prophet's pulpit and Aisha's dwelling, where passers-by thought him mad.
Ibn Abbas, though young, attended the Eid prayer with the Prophet, who prayed and preached, then bade the women give alms, which Bilal collected.
The Prophet used to go to the Quba mosque, sometimes walking and sometimes riding.
Aisha asked to be buried with the Prophet's wives rather than beside him, lest she be thought sanctified, yet let Umar be buried with his two companions.
The Prophet prayed Asr early enough that one could reach Al-Awali, three or four miles away, while the sun was still high.
The Sa' measure in the Prophet's time equalled a Mudd and a third of a later Mudd, and he asked Allah to bless the measures of Medina's people.
The Jews brought a man and a woman who had committed illegal sexual intercourse, and the Prophet had them stoned near the mosque where biers were placed.
The Prophet said Uhud loves us and is loved by us, made Medina a sanctuary as Abraham did Mecca, and between his house and pulpit is a garden of Paradise.
The Prophet held horse races, conditioned horses running from Al-Hafya to Thaniyat-al-Wada and others from there to the mosque of Bani Zuraiq.
Umar and Uthman were heard preaching from the Prophet's pulpit.
Aisha and the Prophet bathed together, taking water from one large copper vessel.
The Prophet made an alliance between the Ansar and Quraish in Anas's house in Medina, and invoked Allah against Bani Sulaim in prayer for a month.
The Prophet allied the Ansar and Quraish in Anas's house at Medina; Abdullah bin Salam let a visitor drink from the Prophet's bowl and pray in his mosque.
The Prophet was told to pray in the blessed Aqiq valley and declare Umra and Hajj, fixed the miqats, and dreamt at Dhul-Hulaifa he was in a blessed valley.
Rising from bowing in the morning prayer the Prophet praised Allah, and in the last rak'a asked Him to curse certain people; Allah revealed that the decision is not his.
Asked at night whether he and Fatima would pray, Ali said their souls are in Allah's Hands; the Prophet left striking his thigh, saying man is most quarrelsome.
At Bait al-Midras the Prophet called the Jews thrice to embrace Islam and be safe, then said he wanted to exile them and they should sell their property.
On Resurrection Noah's people will deny he conveyed Allah's message, and Muhammad's followers will testify for him; the Prophet recited the verse making them a just nation of witnesses.
The Prophet told his Khaibar governor not to take one sa' of good dates for two of mixed, but to exchange equal measures or sell and buy with the price.
A judge who strives to the best of his knowledge gets a double reward if his verdict is right and still a reward if it is wrong.
Umar wanted a witness for an instruction Abu Musa cited, which market business had hidden from him; Abu Huraira, staying close to the Prophet, narrated much and forgot nothing.
Jabir swore that Ibn Sayyad was the Dajjal, because Umar had sworn so before the Prophet and the Prophet did not object.
Horses bring reward if kept for Allah's Cause, shelter if kept for a living, and sin if kept for pride; for donkeys the Prophet cited only the atom's-weight verse.
A woman asked how to bathe after menstruation; the Prophet told her to clean herself with a perfumed cloth, and when she kept asking, Aisha took her aside and explained.
Mastigures were eaten on the Prophet's table cloth though he disliked them, so they were not unlawful; whoever eats garlic or onion should keep away from the mosque.
Asked by a woman what to do if she did not find him, the Prophet told her to go to Abu Bakr.
Ka'b reported truthfully about the People of the Scripture yet with faults; they are neither believed nor denied, and Muslims holding an undistorted Book should not ask them.
The Prophet said to recite the Quran while hearts agree on its meaning and to stop reading when people differ over it.
Near his death the Prophet offered to write something to keep them from going astray; Umar said Allah's Book suffices, the people disputed noisily, and he told them to leave.
Arriving for Hajj, the Prophet ordered the companions to end their ihram, making their wives lawful, saying he would too had he not brought the Hadi; they obeyed.
The Prophet said thrice to pray before Maghrib, adding the third time that whoever wants may do so, lest people take it as a Sunna.
When Aisha was slandered and revelation was delayed, the Prophet consulted Ali and Usama, questioned Barira, and asked from the pulpit for help against those abusing his wife.
Sending Mu'adh to Yemen, the Prophet told him to invite people first to Allah's Oneness, then prayer and Zakat; Allah's right on His slaves is worship of Him alone.
The surah 'He is Allah, the One' equals a third of the Quran, and a man who loved reciting it for describing the Beneficent was told Allah loves him.
Allah is not merciful to those who show no mercy; weeping over his dying grandson, the Prophet said this is mercy Allah puts in His slaves' hearts.
None is more patient than Allah with hurtful words: people ascribe children to Him, yet He gives them health and provision.
None but Allah knows the five keys of the unseen, and Aisha said whoever claims Muhammad saw his Lord or knew the unseen is lying.
Since Allah Himself is As-Salam, the Prophet told those praying not to say 'peace be on Allah' and taught them the tashahhud instead.
Allah will fold the heaven in His right hand saying 'I am the King'; the Prophet sought refuge in His Might; Hell fills when He puts His Foot on it.
The Prophet praised Allah at night as Lord, Light and Truth; he said Allah, Hearing and near, needs no shouting, and taught Abu Bakr an invocation for forgiveness.
Gabriel told the Prophet that Allah had heard what his people said and how they answered him.
The Prophet taught the istikhara: two voluntary rak'at, then asking Allah, who knows and is able, to ease a matter if good and turn it away if not.
The Prophet often swore by 'the One Who turns the hearts'.
Allah has ninety-nine Names, and whoever learns them all by heart will enter Paradise.
The Prophet taught invoking Allah's Name on going to bed, praising Him on waking, and a prayer before relations with one's wife so Satan never harms their child.
Game caught by trained dogs sent with Allah's Name may be eaten, as may meat brought by new Muslims when one mentions Allah's Name over it oneself.
The Prophet slaughtered two rams saying Allah's Name and Allahu Akbar; on the Day of Nahr he told anyone who slaughtered before the prayer to slaughter again.
Do not swear by your fathers; whoever swears should swear by Allah.
Of ten men the Prophet sent to scout the enemy, Khubaib was taken outside Mecca's sanctuary to be killed and recited verses on dying as a Muslim for Allah's sake.
None has more ghira than Allah, so He forbade shameful deeds, and none loves praise more than Allah.
When Allah created the creation He wrote about Himself in His Book, kept with Him on the Throne: 'My Mercy overcomes My Anger'.
