Allah is as His slave thinks of Him and with him when he remembers Him, remembering him in return, and comes running to one who comes walking.
When the verse on torment from above and below came down, the Prophet sought refuge with Allah's Face, and called being split into parties easier.
Allah is not one-eyed, while the Dajjal, of whom every prophet warned, is blind in the right eye with 'Kafir' written between his eyes.
Asked about coitus interruptus with women captured in the battle with Bani Al-Mustaliq, the Prophet said it is better not to, for Allah has written whom He will create.
On Resurrection believers will seek intercession from Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, then Muhammad, who intercedes again and again until those with an atom's weight of good leave Hell.
Allah's full Hand is undiminished by spending; He will grasp earth and heavens saying 'I am the King', as a Jew described with Fingers; and Allah has the most ghira.
The Prophet asked a man whether he knew anything of the Quran, and he named the surahs he knew.
Asked by Yemenis how the universe began, the Prophet said only Allah existed, His Throne over the water, then He created heavens and earth and wrote everything.
Allah's Right Hand stays full despite all He has spent since creating the heavens and earth; His Throne is over the water and He raises and lowers people.
Zainab boasted Allah married her to the Prophet from above seven heavens; the verse on what the Prophet hid concerned her and Zaid, and the Hijab verse concerned her.
When Allah finished His creation, He wrote over His Throne: 'My Mercy preceded My Anger'.
Allah will admit to Paradise whoever believes, prays and fasts Ramadan; it has a hundred degrees for those in jihad, and Firdaus, its highest, lies beneath the Beneficent's Throne.
The Prophet said the sun asks permission to prostrate, and one day will be told to return and rise in the west; he recited the verse on its course.
Sent by Abu Bakr to collect the Quran, Zaid bin Thabit found the last verses of Surat at-Tauba with Abu Khuzaima Al-Ansari alone.
In distress the Prophet said there is no god but Allah, the Knowing and Forbearing, Lord of the Mighty Throne, Lord of the heavens and earth.
When people fall unconscious on Resurrection, the Prophet, the first to be raised, will see Moses holding a pillar of the Throne.
Angels of the night and day meet at the Asr and Fajr prayers; those ascending tell Allah, who knows best, that they left His slaves praying and found them praying.
Allah takes charity of a date's value from honest earnings in His Right Hand and grows it like a foal into a mountain, for only good ascends to Him.
In distress the Prophet declared none worthy of worship but Allah, the Majestic and Forbearing, Lord of the Tremendous Throne and of the heavens.
A man rebuked the Prophet's gold gifts to Najd chiefs; the Prophet foretold the man's offspring would include Quran reciters who leave Islam like an arrow and kill Muslims.
Asked about the verse on the sun running its fixed course, the Prophet said its fixed course is beneath Allah's Throne.
Looking at the full moon, the Prophet told those with him they will see their Lord as clearly, so they should not miss the prayers before sunrise and sunset.
Believers will see their Lord like the full moon; each people follows what it worshipped, a bridge spans Hell, believers intercede, and the last man out of Hell enters Paradise.
Believers on Resurrection go from Adam to Jesus, then to Muhammad, who intercedes three times and takes people out of Hell; this is the Station of Praise promised him.
The Prophet gathered the Ansar in a tent and told them to be patient until they meet Allah and His Messenger, who will be at the Kauthar.
In his night prayer the Prophet praised Allah as Keeper and Light of the heavens and earth, affirmed that His word, Paradise and Hell are true, and asked forgiveness.
Everyone's Lord will speak to him with no interpreter or screen, and in the Paradise of Eden only the Cover of Majesty over His Face keeps people from seeing Him.
Whoever takes a Muslim's property by false oath will meet Allah angry; Allah will neither speak to nor look at false swearers over sales, nor withholders of surplus water.
On the Day of Nahr the Prophet said four of the twelve months are sacred, and that lives, property and honour are as sacred as that day, town and month.
Weeping over a dying grandson, the Prophet said Allah is merciful to the merciful; Paradise is His Mercy, Hell His Punishment; some scorched in Hell enter Paradise by His Mercy.
A Jewish rabbi said Allah will put the heavens, earth and all creation each on a finger and say 'I am the King'; the Prophet smiled and recited a verse.
The Prophet rose in the last third of the night, looked at the sky reciting the verse on the creation of the heavens and earth, and prayed eleven rak'at.
When Allah created the creation, He wrote with Him on His Throne: 'My Mercy has preceded My Anger'.
In the womb an angel writes each person's livelihood, death, deeds and whether wretched or blessed, and what is written decides his final deeds, leading to Paradise or Hell.
The Prophet asked Gabriel why he did not visit more often, and the verse came down that the angels descend only by the command of his Lord.
Jews in Medina asked the Prophet about the spirit, and he answered with the revealed verse that its knowledge is with his Lord and mankind has little knowledge.
Allah guarantees Paradise, or return with reward or booty, to one going out solely for jihad in His Cause; only fighting so Allah's Word is superior is in His Cause.
A group of the Prophet's followers will remain victorious and keep to Allah's commands, unharmed by those who oppose them, until Allah's Order, the Hour, comes.
The Prophet told Musailama he would not give him a palm stalk; he cannot escape what Allah ordained for him, and if he turned from Islam Allah would ruin him.
Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit; after a pause in which he was being inspired, he answered with the verse that its knowledge is with his Lord.
Allah guarantees one who goes out solely for jihad in His Cause, believing His Word, either Paradise or a return home with reward or booty.
When asking Allah, be firm and do not say 'if You wish', for no one can compel Him.
Asked at night whether he and Fatima would pray, Ali said their souls are in Allah's Hand; the Prophet left striking his thighs, saying man is most quarrelsome.
A believer is like a fresh plant bent by the wind that straightens again after calamities, and a disbeliever like a stiff pine that stands until Allah cuts it down.
The Muslims' time beside earlier nations is like Asr to sunset, yet they earn double the people of the Torah and Gospel, as Allah grants His favour as He wishes.

The pledge to the Prophet bars associating partners with Allah, stealing, illegal intercourse, killing offspring, slander and disobedience; punishment in this world expiates, and screened sins rest with Allah.
Had Solomon said 'If Allah wills', each wife would have borne a horseman for Allah's Cause; the Prophet told a sick bedouin his fever purifies, if Allah wills.
When the people overslept the morning prayer, the Prophet said Allah took their souls and returned them when He willed, and he prayed after the sun had risen.
When a Muslim slapped a Jew in a quarrel over Moses, the Prophet forbade preferring him to Moses, whom he will find holding the Throne on Resurrection.
Angels guard Medina, and if Allah wills neither the Dajjal nor plague will come near it.
Every prophet has one invocation surely answered, and the Prophet wishes, if Allah wills, to keep his as intercession for his followers on Resurrection.
The Prophet dreamt he drew water from a well, then Abu Bakr drew a bucket or two weakly, and Umar, with a huge bucket, watered the people and camels.
When someone in need came, the Prophet told his companions to intercede for him and be rewarded, for Allah fulfils what He wills through His Messenger's tongue.
No one should say to Allah 'forgive me if You wish', but ask firmly, for Allah does what He wills and none can force Him.
Told that Allah's slave Khadir was more learned, Moses sought him with a fish as the sign, finding him by retracing their steps to where it was lost.
The Prophet said they would camp at Khaif Bani Kinana tomorrow if Allah willed, and at the siege of Ta'if said they would return home tomorrow if Allah willed.
When Allah decrees a matter in heaven, angels beat their wings at His word; when their fear passes they ask what their Lord said and are told the truth.
Allah listens to nothing as He listens to the Prophet reciting the Quran aloud in a pleasant voice.
On Resurrection Allah will call Adam, and a voice will order him to bring out from his offspring those sent to the Fire.
Aisha was never as jealous of any woman as of Khadija, whom Allah ordered the Prophet to give glad tidings of a palace in Paradise.
When Allah loves someone He tells Gabriel, who loves him and announces it in the heavens, then earth's people welcome him; angels of night and day report His slaves praying.
Gabriel brought the Prophet glad tidings that whoever dies worshipping nothing besides Allah will enter Paradise, even if he stole or committed illegal intercourse.
The Prophet taught a bedtime invocation of surrender and trust in Allah, and on the Day of the Clans asked Allah, Revealer of the Book, to defeat and shake them.
The verse forbidding prayer too loud or too low came while the Prophet hid in Mecca: recite so companions hear, but not pagans, who abused the Quran.
Allah said the son of Adam hurts Him by abusing Time, for He is Time: all things are in His Hands and He alternates night and day.
Allah said the fast is for Him, the faster leaving desire, food and drink for Him; it shields from Hell, and the faster's breath is better to Allah than musk.
Job gathered gold locusts falling on him as he bathed; asked by his Lord whether He had not made him rich enough, he said he could not forgo His blessings.
Every night in its last third the Lord descends to the nearest heaven and asks who will invoke, ask or seek forgiveness, that He may answer, grant and forgive.
The Prophet said Muslims are the last but will be foremost on Resurrection; the narrators add that Allah tells man to spend, promising to compensate him.
Gabriel told the Prophet to convey her Lord's greeting to Khadija as she brought food, with glad tidings of a palace of Qasab in Paradise without noise or fatigue.
Allah said He has prepared for His righteous slaves what no eye has seen, no ear heard and no heart imagined.
In night prayer the Prophet praised Allah as Light and Lord of the heavens and earth, affirmed His promise, Paradise, Hell and the Hour are true, and sought forgiveness.
Slandered, Aisha hoped Allah would clear her through a dream of the Prophet, never thinking He would reveal verses to be recited, but He revealed ten verses of Surat an-Nur.
A bad deed only intended is not written, and abandoned for Allah's sake it counts as good; a good deed intended counts as one, and done, ten to seven hundred.
When creation was finished, the womb sought Allah's refuge from those who sever it, and He promised to join whoever joins it and cut whoever cuts it.
When it rained after the Prophet's invocation, he said Allah declared that some of His slaves had become disbelievers in Him and some believers.
Allah loves meeting whoever loves meeting Him, dislikes meeting whoever dislikes it, and is to His slave as the slave thinks of Him.
Allah forgave a man who had his body burned and the ashes scattered out of fear of Him, and forgives a slave who sins and asks forgiveness again and again.
The Prophet will intercede repeatedly until those with faith of a mustard seed leave Hell; on a fourth plea Allah will take out all who said La ilaha illallah.
The last man to leave Hell is given Paradise ten times the world; each person's Lord will speak to him, Fire ahead, so shield yourself even with half a date.
A Jewish priest said on Resurrection Allah will hold all creation on His fingers saying 'I am the King'; the Prophet smiled, amazed and believing, and recited a verse.
Each person will come close to his Lord, who will screen him from others, make him confess his sins, and forgive them as He screened them in the world.
Moses blamed Adam for turning his offspring out of Paradise; Adam answered that Moses blamed him for what was ordained before his creation, and so Adam prevailed.
Believers gathered on Resurrection will ask Adam, father of mankind, to intercede with their Lord, and he will say he is not fit, mentioning his mistake.
Gabriel opened the Prophet's chest at Zamzam and took him up the seven heavens meeting prophets; the fifty prayers were reduced to five, rewarded as fifty, before he woke.
Allah will grant the people of Paradise His lasting pleasure, and a man there who wishes to farm will see his crop grow and be harvested in moments, mountain-high.
The greatest sin is setting up rivals to Allah who created you, then killing your son for fear he will share your food, then illegal intercourse with your neighbour's wife.
Three men at the Ka'ba argued whether Allah hears them when they speak softly, and Allah revealed the verse that their ears, eyes and skins would testify against them.
Ibn Abbas asked how Muslims could consult the People of the Scripture, who altered their books, when Allah's latest Book is with them pure and undistorted.
Receiving revelation, the Prophet moved his lips in haste, so Allah revealed that He would gather it in his heart; afterwards he listened to Gabriel and then recited as taught.
The verse against praying too loud or too low told the Prophet, hiding in Mecca, to recite so companions but not pagans hear; Aisha said it concerned invocations.
Whoever does not recite the Quran in a pleasing voice is not one of us, which others explained as reciting it aloud.
One may wish only to be like two men: one given the Quran who recites it night and day, and one given wealth who spends it rightly.
The Prophet conveyed his Lord's message that whoever of them is martyred goes to Paradise.
Aisha said not to believe anyone claiming the Prophet concealed part of the revelation, since Allah ordered him to proclaim all that was sent down.
The greatest sins are setting up rivals to Allah, killing one's son for fear of sharing food, and illegal intercourse with a neighbour's wife, confirmed by a revealed verse.
The Muslims' stay beside earlier nations is like Asr to sunset, yet they receive double the reward of the people of the Torah and Gospel, by Allah's blessing.
The best deeds are praying at the stated times, being dutiful to parents and jihad in Allah's Cause.
The Prophet gave property selectively, giving those with impatience and discontent in their hearts and leaving those Allah made content, dearer to him, like Amr bin Taghlib.
Allah says if His slave comes a span nearer, He comes a cubit nearer, and if the slave comes walking, He comes running.
Allah said every deed can be expiated, but the fast is for Him and He rewards it, and the faster's breath is better to Him than musk.
The Prophet reported his Lord saying no slave should say he is better than Jonah son of Matta.
On the day of the Conquest of Mecca the Prophet recited Surat al-Fath on his camel in a vibrating, pleasant voice, which the narrators later imitated.
The Prophet's letter to Heraclius called the People of the Scripture to a word common to both, worshipping only Allah, and Muslims should neither believe nor deny them.
When a Jewish man and woman were charged with illegal intercourse, the Torah was read and its stoning verse, hidden under a hand, uncovered, and the Prophet ordered them stoned.
Allah listens to nothing as He listens to a Prophet reciting the Quran in an attractive, audible, sweet voice.
Knowing she was innocent, Aisha never thought Allah would reveal recited verses about her, yet He revealed ten verses of Surat an-Nur on those who brought the false charge.
Al-Bara' never heard a better voice than the Prophet's reciting At-Tin in the Isha prayer; hiding in Mecca, he was told to recite neither too loud nor too low.
Abu Sa'id told a shepherd to raise his voice in the adhan, for every jinn, human or thing that hears the caller will witness for him on Resurrection.
The Prophet recited the Quran with his head in Aisha's lap while she menstruated, and told Umar and Hisham, reciting differently, that the Quran was revealed in seven ways.
Everyone's place in Paradise or Hell is written, yet all should keep doing deeds, for each finds easy the deeds leading to the end he was created for.
Before creating the creation Allah wrote in a Book kept with Him over the Throne: 'My Mercy has preceded My Anger'.
The Prophet swore he would not give the Ash'ariyyin mounts, then gave them camels, saying Allah provided them and he breaks an oath for something better and expiates.
The Prophet told the Abdul Qais delegation that belief in Allah means testifying to Him alone, praying, giving Zakat and the khumus, and forbade four vessels used for alcoholic drinks.
Picture-makers will be punished on Resurrection and told to give life to what they made; Allah challenges those imitating His creation to create an ant or a grain.
A believer reciting the Quran is like a fragrant, tasty citron, one not reciting like a date; an impious reciter is like a fragrant bitter herb, a non-reciter like colocynth.
Soothsayers are nothing; the one true word they tell is snatched from heaven by a jinn and poured into their ears, and they mix it with a hundred lies.
People will come from the East reciting the Quran without it passing their throats, leaving the religion like an arrow never to return; their sign is shaving.
Two phrases dear to the Beneficent, light on the tongue and heavy in the balance, are Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi and Subhan Allah al-Azim.
